recap.text: Carl enters the dungeon in pink Crocs and boxers. He loses the shoes to a Goblin Murder Dozer. He and Donut, who becomes a talking cat after eating an Enhanced Pet Biscuit, fight through the first floor using explosives and a stolen chopper. After fighting a boss in a dog pound and winning an Enchanted Pedicure Kit, Carl remains barefoot and glittery.

Carl takes Primal for his race and a monk-rogue hybrid for his class, becoming a trapmaking and bomb-making anarchist. He loots strength rings from dead crawlers, snaps his own pinky to break a charm, and kills a bear on roller skates. After punching a level-75 guard and becoming a magistrate, he escapes a city explosion naked. He reaches level twenty-seven and decides to focus on progression and training.

Carl uses a Protective Shell to push mobs off a train and finds an Enchanted Necklace of the Haute Bourgeoisie. He trades westerns to a mole man for books and uses a Goo-inator to earn a bucket of pink glitter. After stealing a train and using a portal cart to save stranded crawlers, Carl fights a Mimic Rex in a Death Challenge. He reaches level forty-one and vows to break the system.

Carl earns a bounty modifier and a toe ring. He kills a Changeling Principal for a map and uses a garbage disposal to kill the boss Denise. Carl punches Ghazi for a winding box and kills a sharktopus with a Potion of Bloodlust. He takes Emberus as a patron and tears off Quan Ch's arm. Carl swaps a winding box for a fake and takes the number one spot on the board.

Carl takes the Agent Provocateur specialisation and uses the Ring of Divine Suffering to steal stats from hunters. He builds a massive bomb called Just Wait Until Your Daddy Gets Home and kills a hunter named Zabit with his own mines. After surviving the Butcher's Masquerade, Carl buys a lore book for the Commonwealth of the Bahamas, but with seconds left Donut spins the globe and lands them in the Caribbean instead.

Carl and Donut enter a replay of Havana to plant flags. Carl earns a Celestial Predator Box and a jacket that grants Soul Essence and a bone key. After confronting a version of his father and a half-brother named Asher, Carl helps a group of crawlers survive. Paz kills a goddess, and the crawlers enter the ninth floor without sponsor protections.

Carl takes command of an army at Larracos and discovers a Containment Interface that can kill the AI. He fights through the Naga and the Madness, using a spellbook to bomb himself while immortal. After Operation Ruin, Carl refuses a deal from Quasar and learns that Princess Chandra is Donut's lawyer and his new wife.

Carl drives a Big Shot Chicken food truck through races, using joey skins to kill a boss and a rocket button to survive a factory. He wins a quest to send two people to an arena but loses his friend Dong Quixote to a god. After a transformation into a dachshund, Carl enters the eleventh floor. He kills Scolopendra, earns a Mark of the Damned, and forms a party to stop anyone from winning the Ascendency.

beats.headline: January 3rd, 2:23 in the morning
beats.text: I crack the window of my apartment in Seattle for a cigarette. That's it. That's the whole decision. Donut, who is my ex-girlfriend's show cat and not mine in any way I agreed to, goes out through it and up the tree, and I go after her into the freezing dark in my leather jacket, boxers and Bea's pink Crocs, with a Zippo and half a pack of Marlboro Reds. Mrs Parsons leans out to ask about the noise. Then every building on the planet comes down at once, and everyone who stayed inside one is gone.
beats.gist: Carl cracks his Seattle apartment window for a cigarette; Donut the show cat climbs a tree.

beats.headline: Seven achievements and an obvious trap
beats.text: At the bottom of the stairs I am Crawler 4,122, and the cat, somehow, is 4,119. Then the achievements land in a wall: Crazy Cat Lady, a Legendary Pet Box for being first in with a cat, Early Adopter, Empty Pockets, Why Aren't You Wearing Pants, Unarmed Combat, and Loner, which pays nothing and says I am so dead. I walk into the first dark alley with a sign pointing into it. A Goblin Murder Dozer comes out. Both Crocs go. I kill a goblin with my fists and the floor while a rat behind a chained door explains that rules are rules.
beats.gist: Carl is Crawler 4,122 and the cat is 4,119.

beats.headline: Three goblins and a boiler
beats.text: The rat says the goblins will bring the whole clan in an hour, so I go back out. I climb the dozer's bone ladder barefoot, throw one goblin over the driver into the spinning blades. The engineer comes at me with a knife and tells me I'm not speaking my language at all, that they programmed it into my brain, so I hit him with his own pot while he's still talking. Then I jump on him from the top of the machine, and I weigh 230 pounds. Boiler Breach Imminent, twelve seconds. I make the door. Mordecai says it could hold off a star destroyer and he has never seen anything shake it like that.
beats.gist: Carl climbs a bone ladder barefoot, throws a goblin into blades, and hits an engineer with a pot.

beats.headline: Intelligence three
beats.text: My stats come up: Strength 6, Intelligence 3, Constitution 5, Dexterity 5, Charisma 4. I take the three personally and use my buddy Billy Maloney as the example, the one who peed on a cop's bicycle last week. Billy is dead. He was in jail on a failure-to-appear warrant. Mordecai says wisdom isn't on the list any more and not to worry about a three unless I want magic. I get a healing spell anyway. It costs two of my three mana points. I cast it at full health, glow red, and nothing else happens.
beats.gist: Carl has Strength 6, Intelligence 3, Constitution 5, Dexterity 5, and Charisma 4.

beats.headline: I was going to sell it
beats.text: Mordecai says feed the Enhanced Pet Biscuit to the cat now, inside the guild, or sell it for a couple thousand gold. Over a hundred possible effects, half of them good. Donut is a cat. She is not a mastiff. She would be a liability out there, and a couple thousand gold buys shoes and pants. I also know I'm all she has left in the world. I'm rolling the thing between my fingers, most of the way to the sensible answer, when she jumps up and eats it out of my hand and hits the floor as a wet, hairy puddle.
beats.gist: Mordecai tells Carl to feed the Enhanced Pet Biscuit to Donut or sell it for gold.

beats.headline: Dressed for nothing, and stuck that way
beats.text: An hour past the stairs and I have a Goblin Pass Tattoo on my left forearm, a Trollskin Shirt of Pummeling, a Nightgaunt Cloak of Stoutness clipped to the jacket and a Toe Ring of the Splatter Skunk. What I do not have is shoes. I have asked. The dungeon has heard me ask, and the dungeon has an opinion about it.
beats.gist: Carl has a Goblin Pass Tattoo, Trollskin Shirt, Nightgaunt Cloak, and Toe Ring, but no shoes.

beats.headline: Frogger, skill eight
beats.text: The skills menu has a search box, so I type in Frogger. My old man had an original stand-up cabinet in the basement, and my mom locked me down there with it whenever his friends came over to drink and get loud. The machine tops out at 99,990 and then cycles. My record was 879,460. The dungeon lists it: Frogger, 1981 video game cabinet version, skill 8. That machine is down here somewhere now, or the atoms of it. The whole dungeon is made out of what we built.
beats.gist: Carl types Frogger into the skills menu search box and finds he has skill 8.

beats.headline: Promoted to bodyguard
beats.text: Her stats come up and she's stronger and smarter than me: Strength 11, Intelligence 11, Constitution 2, Dexterity 8, Charisma 25. She says I'm her manservant and explains to Mordecai that I'm a little slow. Highest stat total makes her party leader, so she renames the party after herself and changes my title to Royal Bodyguard. Mordecai says the titles don't mean anything. Then he gets serious: stick together, at least until the ninth floor. I can always leave the party. The crown is on her head, not mine.
beats.gist: Donut becomes party leader with a Charisma of 25 and renames Carl her Royal Bodyguard.

beats.headline: Smush
beats.text: By the time we find a safe room I've killed every rat and Scatterer with my bare feet, punting one and stomping the other. Level three brings Foot Soldier, for kicking, and a second skill called Smush. The voice that reads it is lower than usual, and I can hear him breathing. Killing with your feet. Your bare, beautiful feet. I make the mistake of telling Donut. She guesses we're not getting me shoes, then. We are, I say, as soon as possible. She says the computer fancies me and we should take advantage of it.
beats.gist: Carl kills rats with his bare feet to reach level three and the skill Smush.

beats.headline: Four point three million
beats.text: The first screen over the counter counts crawlers. 4,322,395. It was ten million a few hours ago, and it's still going down while I watch. Tally makes me murgh vindaloo, spice level four, and it's the best thing I've ever eaten. When I pull out a cigarette, a firm "Nope" comes from behind the counter. So here's the plan: we stay. There's a Scatterer nest next door. We clear it for experience, sleep here, eat here, and go looking for the stairs once they appear.
beats.gist: Carl watches a screen count crawlers drop from ten million to 4,322,395.

beats.headline: The other guy and the gym bag
beats.text: Ten hours of sleep, a shower, bacon and eggs, and the board says 4,148,111. Nine cigarettes left. By the time we reach the nest's door we're both level five. Donut peers into the dark and says it smells like the bag I take on the days that other guy comes over to the apartment. My gym bag. Some guy was coming over while I was at the gym. I should have broken up with her long ago. I suddenly feel very reckless. I light the goblin dynamite, throw it as hard as I can, and run.
beats.gist: Carl eats bacon and eggs, sees 4,148,111 on the board, and has nine cigarettes left.

beats.headline: The Hoarder
beats.text: The dynamite takes out the nest and opens up my scalp, and then the door re-forms and bars itself. Boss battle. She comes out of the garbage fifteen feet tall, a woman in torn sweatpants with half her face burned, begging in Spanish. I think she's a person. Then she vomits Scatterers at us. I loop a steel leash off a mummified dog around her throat and pull until it breaks. At the end she closes her eyes and says something in Spanish, crying. I don't understand a word. I tell her I'm sorry, and I punch her until she's dead.
beats.gist: Carl kills a fifteen-foot woman in torn sweatpants with a mummified dog's steel leash and punches.

beats.headline: Kneepads, not pants
beats.text: The Gold Crowd Control Box finally puts something on my legs, and it is not pants. Enchanted Spiked Kneepads of the Shade Gnoll Riot Forces: ten per cent damage reflect on all my armor, momentum attacks cancelled, and eight-inch needle spikes that pop out when they're needed. The Bronze Boss Box gives me a Tome of Wisp Armor I can't afford to cast, so I hold on to it. Donut looks me up and down and asks Mordecai if there's a worst-dressed award. He says sort of.
beats.gist: Carl gets Enchanted Spiked Kneepads of the Shade Gnoll Riot Forces and a Tome of Wisp Armor.

beats.headline: Rebecca W and an apple core
beats.text: The corpse on the edge of the neighborhood is a crawler called Rebecca W, level three, about thirty, sitting against the wall with nothing on her. The box names the crawler who killed her, and there's a single gunshot through the moth tattoo on her chest. He took everything and left an apple core. Out of nowhere I think of the last day I saw my father, laughing: I don't need you to like me, but you will respect me. Nobody is ever going to know her story. I want to find the man who did this.
beats.gist: Carl finds the naked corpse of Rebecca W with a moth tattoo and an apple core.

beats.headline: Earth, as advertised
beats.text: The premiere plays on the screen over the counter with 4,006,002 of us left. They cherry-pick Earth: shanty towns, garbage dumps, a scene from Godzilla, a dead horse, people shooting up. Then forty minutes of people dying. Donut says she didn't realise Earth sucked so badly. It didn't. They're making themselves the good guys, saving us from ourselves. We get no screen time at all for the Hoarder. Donut wants a city boss for the next episode. I want an exit, and we have three and a half days to find one.
beats.gist: A premiere shows 4,006,002 survivors and footage of garbage dumps, a dead horse, and people dying.

beats.headline: A vehicle, on credit of meth
beats.text: A level two green slime eats my right glove and the sleeve off my leather jacket, so we turn back, and that's when I get the idea: we need to cover ground, and the goblins build vehicles. The tattoo turns their dots white. The shamanka refuses the gunpowder, the torches, the potions, the biscuits. Then I offer the llama's two baggies of meth. Lorelai tastes it and says it's dungeon made. I trade them, plus where to find more, for a chopper that won't blow up, coal to run it, and some of the Bomb Bards' grenades.
beats.gist: Carl trades two baggies of dungeon-made meth for a chopper, coal, and Bomb Bards' grenades.

beats.headline: We started a meth war
beats.text: The chopper has an alligator-skull seat and a permacube for water, and the engineer says it will tell me when it's too hot. I take three piles of 999 coal. Lorelai offers me a good time; Donut declines for me. Rory wants to know where the drugs came from, and Donut tells her: the llamas across the road. Every goblin in the room gears up and rolls out. Did we really just start a meth war? Then Donut asks about the chieftain. Killing him after they helped us would be about the lowest move there is, and really dumb. Yeah, and then we kill the chieftain.
beats.gist: Carl takes three piles of 999 coal and a chopper with an alligator-skull seat.

beats.headline: A cart of black powder and scrap
beats.text: We strip the workshop: coal, tools, wick, tables, almost a ton of black powder. Four barrels go on a cart, topped with nuts and bolts, and each gets a lump of Hobgoblin Pus with a magical trigger in it. I waste one of the three detonators testing it. The obvious one sits on top, so if the chieftain has time to react, he'll hopefully dig at it instead of the four buried in the barrels. Donut opens the door, I hit the cart like a football sled, she slams the door, and we run through three turns. I press the button. She mentions there were a lot of babies in there, too.
beats.gist: Carl strips a workshop of coal, tools, wick, tables, and almost a ton of black powder.

beats.headline: Babies in the boss room
beats.text: It worked. A bronze star, level eight, a wall of notifications I don't want to open. Donut says there were goblin babies in there, some in little oversized jackets, and old ones and pregnant ones, and she thinks I hit one with the cart. It makes me feel like a jerk, and I don't like feeling like one. The coal pile has caught and a wall of fire blocks the boss chamber, so there's no map, and I'm relieved. A line of white dots is coming our way. They won't be white for long. We run north into a quadrant we haven't seen.
beats.gist: Carl reaches level eight. He hits goblin babies with a cart. He runs north from white dots.

beats.headline: You're not going to break me
beats.text: The safe room is a dingy bus-station waiting area with an experience cookie and a number on the board: 3,594,517, clinking down like a dripping tap. I get an IED skill and a Demolitions Workshop menu I can't open without a Sapper's Table. My Desperado tattoo goes on my neck. Lying on the cot I work it out. The room was built for exactly what we did. Those kids existed only to die. Someone carved AMW into the ceiling tile, somewhere these aliens stole. You might hurt me, or kill me, but you're not going to break me.
beats.gist: Carl stays in a dingy bus-station waiting area and gets an IED skill and Desperado tattoo.

beats.headline: He ate the cookie for 9.8
beats.text: Frank Q's story is good, and it is wrong in three places. The dead woman he calls a trafficker was level three and carrying an apple core, so she had been to a tutorial guild before any firefight. He eats a cookie and gets 9.8 experience instead of 10, which means a live partner somewhere. And his finger is twitching on the chair: he is typing. So I turn my back and fiddle with my kneepads. They both pull the trigger in a safe room and freeze. We run, and I leave a rat corpse behind with lit dynamite in its inventory.
beats.gist: Carl finds three errors in Frank Q's story and eats a cookie for 9.8 experience.

beats.headline: Stairs + People
beats.text: The AI gives us an achievement for being attacked in a safe room, and the reward line says bitches don't get rewards, and for the first time down here I laugh at one. We ride east for hours. My father was a weekend motorcycle guy; I have not heard from him in over twelve years. Then a sign in red spray paint, still tacky: two crossroads east, three south, stairs and people. Chilly goat corpses with fifteen different crawler names on the kills. A second sign on the floor: do not go deeper into the spiral.
beats.gist: The AI gives Carl an achievement for being attacked in a safe room.

beats.headline: A worthy cause
beats.text: Thirty-eight people at the drawbridge, and all but five of them are elderly residents who cannot walk, let alone fight. The cops and firemen went into the maze and never came out. The ones who went looking for other stairs were picked off one by one. Then an old man in a veteran's cap pats a crying woman on the back, and I decide that if I'm going to die, it might as well be for something. I tell Brandon we grind today, sleep, and go in after. Imani asks how. I tell her I have an idea.
beats.gist: Carl sees thirty-eight people at the drawbridge and tells Brandon they grind today and go in.

beats.headline: Sharks and minnows
beats.text: On the way out I paint over their signs, and the ones I cannot cover I change: two blocks south becomes twelve. Imani is level ten because she had to kill her own patients, and I do not want to find out what somebody else would do to a camp full of old people for the experience. Donut asks what if good guys come. There are no big groups of good guys out here, I tell her. It's only sharks and minnows. She asks which one we are. I don't answer.
beats.gist: Carl paints over signs and changes directions to protect a camp of old people.

beats.headline: A second potion, on myself first
beats.text: My fog scrolls last fifteen seconds each against the Juicer's flaming plates. I swing a half-stripped barbell, then a hundred-pound plate, until he gets me by the throat. Donut opens his neck and I finish him, and she is in a heap with a broken leg and a sliver of health. My Heal Critter scroll will not target her. She took a mana potion minutes ago, and I do not know what an early one would do. So I drink one, then drink a second by hand before the timer ends. Poisoned. Nullified. I give it five more minutes before I risk one on her.
beats.gist: Carl uses fog scrolls and swings a barbell and a hundred-pound plate against the Juicer.

beats.headline: A fist that turns to steel
beats.text: The brawler box is the best thing I have won since the shirt: a charcoal bracer that becomes a spiked war gauntlet of orcish steel if I hold a fist for two seconds. Three strength in fist mode, two more levels of Iron Punch, a small chance to stun, and a warning in red about when to take it off. The boss box gives me a hundred throwing stars with a Bloodlust enchantment, eight per cent more damage against a monster type for each hit, compounded, Mordecai checks. And very fragile. My knuckles stop breaking.
beats.gist: Carl wins a charcoal bracer that becomes a spiked war gauntlet of orcish steel.

beats.headline: The Speedbump, and the pop
beats.text: Five hours building it: goblin tables on their sides, weight benches bolted on like shutters, barbell poles for braces, and Brandon's idea, fifty throwing stars thrown into the wooden front ramp. The ball hits it, wedges between our roof and the ceiling, and the roof starts to give. We stab up through the lattice until something pops. Then it rains tusklings in tuxedos and gowns, dazed, with no idea where they are. Their dots are red and the clock is running. I kick one until her health bar goes, and I might be crying.
beats.gist: Carl spends five hours building a speedbump from goblin tables, weight benches, barbell poles, and fifty throwing stars.

beats.headline: The last cigarette
beats.text: The boss drops a Borough Field Guide, which adds the monster types to the quadrants around the arena on my map. I loot everything, down to a pig harness and a tent-sized tuxedo jacket. Then Donut says what I was going to do before I do it, and I light my last cigarette and it tastes like ash. What's the point of living if I can't live with myself. I drop it unfinished and grind it out. Agatha is gone, and the stairs have turned into a ramp. Brandon asks me to find her. We go down, I push the door, and I feel myself fall.
beats.gist: The boss drops a Borough Field Guide, and Carl loots a pig harness and a tent-sized tuxedo jacket.

beats.headline: Goddamnit, Donut, on cue
beats.text: A plush blue room on a boat somewhere in a winter ocean, a fruit basket and a porthole that won't open. I tell Donut these people are not our friends. Then a crab-bodied host with a mantis head and a chest that rests on her desk wants my catchphrase, and I don't know I have one until she plays at least fifteen clips. I say it. They cheer. They show me in my kneepads under the words WORST DRESSED and I pretend to laugh. Donut promises them style, and I watch her face and see a hunger there.
beats.gist: Carl and Donut meet a mantis-headed host on a boat in a winter ocean.

beats.headline: Pugilism ten, and still behind
beats.text: On the second floor I smear Agatha's dead grub across the floor until its X leaves the map. From now on we leave as little behind as possible. The boss box has a Cheat Code Potion that expires in seventeen minutes; I drink it and my Pugilism jumps three levels to ten. My fists hit as hard as Brandon's lightning maul now. But I remember Lucia Mar running up walls on the recap, and the crossbow woman throwing a tentacle monster into the air, and I wonder whether I am falling behind.
beats.gist: Carl smears Agatha's dead grub across the floor and drinks a Cheat Code Potion to reach Pugilism ten.

beats.headline: Carl's Jug O' Boom
beats.text: The clurichauns carry clay jugs of toilet-grade moonshine, a hundred and eighty proof and highly flammable. I pour a splash out, add goblin oil, and one of Donut's short torches corks the mouth perfectly. The dungeon names it after me: created by an unstable, pantsless man who talks to a cat. Incendiary Device Handling jumps to five. The first one we throw burns blue to the ceiling for a minute and fifteen seconds and leaves ash. We make ten more, and burn every other room.
beats.gist: Carl makes an incendiary device from moonshine, goblin oil, and a torch called Carl's Jug O' Boom.

beats.headline: We were going to move down
beats.text: The second fairy screams it from the ceiling, just before she hits me in the chest with a magic missile: not fair, they were going to move down to the third floor. Forty dead at once and I hit level eleven, and I feel like hell about it. Mordecai said the deeper mobs would be less sympathetic. The real enemies are the Syndicate, Borant, the kua-tin. You're not going to break me, I whisper; it has become a mantra. I decide to leave the boss alone. Then the door with Live, Laugh, Love on it blows open, and the boss comes out.
beats.gist: A fairy hits Carl with a magic missile, he hits level eleven, and the boss emerges.

beats.headline: One part moonshine, one part fairy
beats.text: The recipe from the dusty box: a third of the glass moonshine, one laminak fairy corpse, blend until pink. I cram her in headfirst and pedal a child's exercise bike while tentacles full of screaming mouths break through the walls. Ten doses of immunity, and it makes you drunk. Donut raises a clurichaun and I send it running at the boss's door with a lit jug over its head and dynamite down its overalls. My health is in the red. I put a table over us and wrap myself around the cat.
beats.gist: Carl blends glass moonshine and a laminak fairy corpse while tentacles with screaming mouths break walls.

beats.headline: Boxers with little red hearts
beats.text: The alchemy table I hid behind comes out of that fire cool to the touch. I think those tables cannot be destroyed. That is a bug, and bugs get patched, so it stays in my head. Then the boss box gives me a pair of white boxers covered in little red hearts, and Mordecai laughs, and then says that is actually a really good prize. Enchanted BigBoi Boxers: plus two Constitution, and a level-15 Protective Shell once every thirty hours. My old pair falls apart in my hands.
beats.gist: Carl gets white boxers with little red hearts that give plus two Constitution and a Protective Shell.

beats.headline: Not on your schedule
beats.text: The admin is a two-foot fish in a diving suit, and she tells me to line up a major boss fight for the end of the floor, because that played well last time. Something in me lets go. I tell her we are fighting for our lives, that we will smile and joke on their shows because we have to, and that we are not going to fight or survive on her schedule. Mordecai looks terrified. Zev tells me they are all afraid. Then Donut says this is just like season three of Gossip Girl, and I laugh, and I cannot stop.
beats.gist: Carl tells a two-foot fish admin in a diving suit he will not fight on her schedule.

beats.headline: Protective Shell, first cast
beats.text: Jack pees on the wall and the wall makes a monster: level 93, smoke and claws. Yolanda stands her ground, and it unravels her and Randall both. I hit Protective Shell as a claw comes in, and the thing bounces off like a dog at the end of its leash. Then gravity flips and I am running on the ceiling. Mrs. McGibbons is up there under her own wheelchair. I carry her like a sack, fall when I cross the edge of the spell, and dive through the safe room door with a claw missing me by millimetres. Then I go back out to throw a boom jug.
beats.gist: Carl uses Protective Shell to bounce back a level 93 smoke and claw monster.

beats.headline: Mother of All Bombs
beats.text: I spray-paint Mother of All Bombs on the launcher. Brandon calls it the Bomb Chicken, and so does Donut. Five hours of work: a ramp on a trailer behind the Chopper, and wheeled bombs we call babies, rolling on free weights. Imani opens the door, the elemental teleports away, and we ride. Donut drops babies, then the chain, then the oil. The boiler is about to breach and I open the throttle anyway; Donut sprays the oil, and we jump and let the Chopper go into the stairwell. One more baby at the edge of the hole, Puddle Jumper, and the thing goes in. No experience. We did not kill it.
beats.gist: Carl spray-paints Mother of All Bombs on a launcher and rides a Chopper with Donut.

beats.headline: A substitute admin
beats.text: Zev is in a time out, says an admin called Mukta, who is her substitute. Mukta has overridden the round-table Zev booked and put us on something that pays a higher fee. I remind her we were promised the right to refuse. You seem to be under the impression that you have a say in this, crawler. Then the chat is gone, with no way to answer. I brush Donut for the first time down here, the way Bea taught me, and then we are on a boat the size of a walk-in closet.
beats.gist: Mukta replaces Zev and puts Carl and Donut on a high-fee boat the size of a closet.

beats.headline: We are expensive
beats.text: The segment is called Death Watch: two crawlers guess who lives to buy their friends' lives. I climb over the table and walk out. A voice threatens to drown us; Mukta threatens to accelerate us. So I ask one thing: as long as I participate, is there any consequence for what I say? They paid for our appearance, nothing else. Fine. We are not stronger than this host. We are expensive. On air I demand the points to send us into that fight, call him pork boy, and dare him. He sends the two men back instead, and I have already told them to run.
beats.gist: Carl walks out of a table during Death Watch and demands points to call the host pork boy.

beats.headline: Boots, in a box
beats.text: The parting gift is a cardboard box, and in it is a brand-new pair of Bates zip-up tactical boots, identical to the ones I wore on active duty, in my size, with socks. My soles have acclimated, several of my buffs only work barefoot, and the orc knows it. I tell him I love them, they will be really comfortable in a safe room, and I hope they were not too expensive. On the way out I tell him I look forward to beating him again on the ninth floor. That gets a reaction from the crowd.
beats.gist: Carl receives a cardboard box containing Bates zip-up tactical boots and socks.

beats.headline: Four kills, less fees
beats.text: A new tab: Accounts. A creator's fee on Carl's Jug O' Boom, one gold coin per kill by other crawlers. Current kills: four. The fine print takes two coins plus twenty-five percent, rounded up, and forfeits the lot if I die. Cash out now and I get one coin. Highway robbery. I have slept on Maggie, too. She is hell-bent on hunting us down, so we are not running. I would rather be ready for her than have her sneak up behind us, and her invisibility is not nearly as powerful as I first thought.
beats.gist: Carl sees an Accounts tab and a creator's fee of one gold coin per kill.

beats.headline: Sorry, Ralph, and a stamp
beats.text: The kobold boss chamber is a dog pound with the music so loud we talk by chat. Dingoes in the cages, scarred and beaten, and between songs I hear cheering from the pit. A fighting ring. I toss a pet biscuit into a cage and the red dot turns white. Donut calls it a betrayal most foul. The boss comes out of a carrier: Ralph, a frenzied gerbil. The one-eyed dingo swallows him, and he comes out through its head. I punch him, the stun lands for the first time ever, and I put my bare foot on him.
beats.gist: Carl punches a frenzied gerbil named Ralph and puts a bare foot on him.

beats.headline: I wanted the grub
beats.text: The dungeon groans when I stamp on the gerbil, and the blood will not come off my foot. Along the back wall of the fighting arena is a pet reward room: ten cages, one key. I want the white-tagged brindle grub; I have seen what the hornets do. Donut only has eyes for the last cage: seven inches of raw chicken with pink feathers, a Mongoliensis, red-tagged. Thirty seconds until the cages close. I open his, grab him, and he fights me while she feeds him. The dot stays red. I knew we should have gone with the grub.
beats.gist: Carl stamps on a gerbil and enters a pet reward room to get a brindle grub.

beats.headline: The footwear situation does not improve
beats.text: The second floor finally addresses my feet. It hands me an Enchanted Pedicure Kit of the Sylph. So now I am still barefoot, but my feet are shiny and they glitter, and the audience has noticed, and the audience does not let things go.
beats.gist: Carl receives an Enchanted Pedicure Kit of the Sylph, making his bare feet shiny and glitter.

beats.headline: Primal, and a Compensated Anarchist
beats.text: Class selection, on the way into the Over City. I take Primal for the race and a monk-rogue hybrid nobody has picked before, and the AI writes me up as "a trapmaking, bomb-making, social-media dynamo" who "will happily throw a Molotov through a window one moment and step in front of a camera to plead for the violence to stop the next." I'd argue with it if I could think of the argument.
beats.gist: Carl selects Primal and a monk-rogue hybrid, and the AI labels him a Compensated Anarchist.

beats.headline: A sign that grows out of the ground
beats.text: At the gate Mordecai gives me the first rule: don't cross the level-75 guards; there is no jail, only the death penalty. Then he points at a discoloured rock just outside it. Focus on it, and a holographic sign grows out of the ground like a tree: arrows and distances in kilometres to saferooms, restrooms, stairs six kilometres off, and a medium-sized settlement 34 out. Then the rest of the rules. Don't go into the ruins at night until he says so. Stay away from girls with horns. Then he makes a beeline for a pub.
beats.gist: Mordecai gives Carl rules and points to a rock that grows a holographic sign.

beats.headline: A quest, and a stilt clown
beats.text: A lemur in a painted human skull throws a knife at my head, and the cloak turns it off my chest. Then a Quests tab, trumpets, streamers: The Show Must Go On. Find out why this circus still exists and end it, for a gold quest box. I ask Mordecai whether to take it. He answers with something about his mother's ashes; he is drunk after fifteen minutes. A boom jug sets the building alight, a giraffe flings lemurs at us, and Donut drops an eleven-foot stilt clown so I can land on its chest.
beats.gist: A lemur in a painted human skull throws a knife that a cloak turns away.

beats.headline: A cactus and eighteen westerns
beats.text: My Silver Earth box: a three-inch cactus from Home Depot, $3.99 price tag still on the pot, and a shrink-wrapped pack of eighteen L'Amour paperbacks, the Sackett Family Saga. My dad had a whole shelf of them, and I used to read them under the covers with a flashlight. I haven't read these. My hands are shaking and I'm not sure why. Donut's gifts were deliberate: a candle and a cat tree. I don't know why they picked the cactus. The hobby potion gives me level three in Cesta Punta, whatever that is.
beats.gist: Carl's Silver Earth box contains a three-inch Home Depot cactus and eighteen L'Amour paperbacks.

beats.headline: Rings off a dead crawler
beats.text: Three dead crawlers near where the lemurs hit us, left out as bait. Three women, sisters or close family, all level 8, all killed at the same time. Their inventories are gone and they've been stripped in a hurry, but two rings are still on one of them, both +2 strength, and a wooden anklet on another. I rub the blood off the rings and put them on. I take no joy in looting crawlers. I can see the allure of being a player killer, though. This game gives a lot of loot.
beats.gist: Carl finds three dead level 8 women used as bait and loots two strength rings.

beats.headline: A pinky against a charm
beats.text: The woman from the circus poster is standing in the street, level 60, an Elite, and I want her. It comes on sudden and almost overwhelming, and I take a step toward her before I understand it's a spell. Mordecai calls it Puppy Dog, a buff that comes with a charisma past a hundred, and there's one surefire way to break it: fracture your own finger. I bend my left pinky back until it snaps. It's like a bucket of cold water. She looks at my finger, amused. I drink a health potion.
beats.gist: Carl snaps his left pinky to break a Puppy Dog spell cast by a level 60 Elite.

beats.headline: A lion's heart in my hand
beats.text: Six Mold Lions on the rooftops and Signet in her arms-out pose, not moving. I have one contingency worked out and haven't explained it to Donut. Protective Shell, with Signet inside it; Donut's last scroll of Confusing Fog. One lion bounces into a wall and hangs there, pinned by the shell. I punch until something gives, then reach into its chest and pull. I'm sitting on the ground holding a lion's heart. "Second Chance!" Donut raises it, and our zombie lion kills the next one.
beats.gist: Carl punches a Mold Lion and pulls out its heart while Donut uses a Second Chance scroll.

beats.headline: Fifteen hours on a couch
beats.text: We're heading for the next town and I'm telling Donut we'll stay as far from elites as we can, and then: stunned, paralyzed, unconscious, and the AI quoting Of Mice and Men at me. I wake on a mildewed couch with all my gear and no Donut on the map. Fifteen hours gone. An achievement called Lazarus, for surviving a spell over level 15. Then Signet's hand on my leg. I called her a name and broke my promise. Donut is under Water Lily, and if Signet dies, so does Donut.
beats.gist: Carl tells Donut to avoid elites before the AI paralyzes him and quotes Of Mice and Men.

beats.headline: Heather, and the custard
beats.text: My first solo boss: Heather the Bear, level 19, on roller skates. Her worm claws wrap me like a tetherball and start burrowing, and voices in my head call me delicious Primal flesh. Protective Shell cuts them off. Moonshine and a torch set her alight, and she keeps coming. I scratch the lottery ticket and it lands on Custard, which heals her, and the healing kills the worms. The skates and the hat fall off. What's left is an old bear who wants it over. Two punches, and my foot.
beats.gist: Carl fights Heather the Bear, a level 19 boss on roller skates.

beats.headline: The smell of the circus
beats.text: Inside the big top the smell hits me: peanuts, cotton candy, roasting corn, hay, animal musk, cheap plastic toys. The circus on my fourth birthday, when my mom had run off with me to her parents' place in south Texas. She cried that day, and until this second I always thought she was crying about my dropped hotdog. I have so little of her, and this place just took that too. I stop caring about the plan, or about saving my life. I just want to tear it all down.
beats.gist: Carl smells peanuts, cotton candy, roasting corn, hay, animal musk, and cheap plastic toys in the big top.

beats.headline: Poisoned blood on the vine
beats.text: The vine fills the centre ring and swallows the pole: a city boss, level 85, and an elite. Not one crawler this season has faced a city boss and survived. Nobody inside even looks at me, so I sit in the bleachers by a root, take off the cloak that gives me poison resistance, and double up on health potions to poison myself. I cut my palm on a lemur's knife and let it drip. Heal, antidote, breathe. The blood's almost gone. I have no idea if it worked.
beats.gist: Carl sits in the bleachers, poisons himself with a lemur's knife, and uses health potions.

beats.headline: A cone of worms, on purpose
beats.text: The Wisp Armor spellbook is the one Donut asks me for about once a day. I read it myself on the way down the bleachers, because it blocks mind control and I am about to eat Apollon's ice cream cone, which is worms. A six-minute timer starts. Then I am outside with Signet on one side and Grimaldi in my throat, saying his half of the argument out loud for him. With less than a minute left I drink Mordecai's double healing potion and throw up a never-ending stream of dead worms. Quest complete. Level 15 to 18. Then Mordecai: Donut's health just dropped below 20%. Go now.
beats.gist: Carl reads the Wisp Armor spellbook to block mind control and eats Apollon's worm ice cream cone.

beats.headline: This is my family
beats.text: A Heal scroll gets the spikes out of Donut; for Mongo it takes one of Mordecai's recipes. The street urchins came for the barricade I built around her, not for her, so I clear it into my inventory and they lose interest. Then there are hours of night left, and Mongo, much too big for it now, curls up on my lap and snores. Donut breathes against the back of my neck. I think about my mother, my father, Bea, Billy Maloney and Sam, the guys at the boatyard. All gone. All I have left is right here. This is my family.
beats.gist: Carl uses a Heal scroll on Donut and a recipe on Mongo.

beats.headline: What Bea's mother said
beats.text: Donut makes rash-looking decisions that are almost always the right ones, and I have started to think her camera self is an act, hiding how sharp she is. I remember Thanksgiving, on Bea's parents' couch with Donut asleep on my neck, listening to Bea's mom tell her you have to make them think you're dumber than you are. That attitude, wearing a mask even with family, I never understood. Now I am afraid Donut picked it up from the two of them. We are always camera-facing, and I have no idea how to talk to her about it without sounding like an ass.
beats.gist: Carl thinks Donut hides her sharpness behind a camera act, like the advice from Bea's mother.

beats.headline: Freeballing
beats.text: The first thing I am going to buy tomorrow is pants, I say. Then I read a Scroll of Upgrade and it picks my Enchanted BigBoi Boxers. Plus five dexterity, plus five intelligence, three more constitution, and a benefit called Freeballing: double damage on attacks from below the waist, and those skills train 20% faster. The catch is that only a single layer may cover my crotch, and I am already wearing it. No trousers. I look up at the ceiling. Well played. Mordecai and Donut laugh hard enough to wake Mongo.
beats.gist: Carl reads a Scroll of Upgrade that grants his Enchanted BigBoi Boxers Freeballing and stat increases.

beats.headline: A quest outside the gate
beats.text: Just past the town wall, GumGum is tossing corpses onto a pile of about fifteen dead women, all twisted like dish rags. She finds more in the alleys every morning, blood mostly drained, nobody knows from where, and the guards don't work at night. Can we help. The quest arrives: The Sex Workers Who Fell from the Heavens, a Silver box. I notice wounds on the shoulders of two of them. We'll see what we can do, I tell her. Then I tell Donut we had a good day and I am not letting a quest derail it. That's what you said last time, she says.
beats.gist: Carl finds GumGum tossing fifteen twisted corpses of women onto a pile and receives a Silver box quest.

beats.headline: A kick in the alley
beats.text: Mongo bolts screaming into an alley and we chase him. A burning hand, three flying women's heads trailing their own organs, and GumGum on the ground with her chest torn open. Donut's Torch sends the heads corkscrewing away. The fourth one, an elf, teleports in front of us and starts announcing the final battle and how he has trained his whole life for this moment, and he knows our names. I kick him in the nuts at the same moment Donut's missile hits his neck. His head comes off. Mongo takes it.
beats.gist: Carl kicks an elf in the nuts and Donut's missile removes the elf's head.

beats.headline: Oranges against the door
beats.text: The Cesta Punta skill from that Earth hobby potion was never a martial art. It is jai alai, and the thing in my box is the scoop you wear to play it. I strap it on. A pull-ring folds the scoop into a bracer over my forearm, and my gauntlet fits right over the end of it. Fitz brings the oranges I asked him for. The first one hits the centre of the safe room door and disintegrates. The slingshot rocks are too uneven to throw. I message Zev. You win. No more slingshot.
beats.gist: Carl straps on a jai alai scoop and throws an orange to disintegrate the safe room door.

beats.headline: Off a dead boss and onto a roof
beats.text: It goes dark before noon and a dozen red dots close in. A green bolt snuffs Donut's Torch. My first pre-lit hob-lobber sinks into something big, the second takes out an elf. I throw two sticks of dynamite and one bounces back off a shape at least twelve feet tall, so I jump backward into the empty pool, where the bloated corpse of a dead boss is lying. That is the last thing I remember. I wake up on a roof across the street, level 19, and Donut is firing missiles over the edge.
beats.gist: Carl jumps onto a dead boss's bloated corpse and wakes up on a roof at level 19.

beats.headline: The frog in the pot
beats.text: I have had an answer ready for this. All it takes is a little seed. When the host asks about the Skull Empire's unrest I tell the frog story: boiled slowly, it never jumps. If it used to be okay and it isn't any more, do something about it. Kick them out and set up your own. Tucker says advocating sedition is a crime. Then you're all in that same pot. Besides, what are they going to do, throw me in the dungeon? Barely two minutes pass before the shot comes. It was meant for Donut and me.
beats.gist: Carl tells the host a story about a boiled frog to advocate for sedition.

beats.headline: Set up, and the pawns with us
beats.text: Manasa is dead in the trailer we were meant to be in, and I don't trust luck that tidy. Stalwart had his statement ready and the camera pointed at the army outside the window before I opened my mouth. So I say it in chat, never out loud: we were the bait, and so was she. Someone knew the orcs meant to kill us and set up the switch on purpose, or jumped on it. If the Valtay lose an ally, maybe go to war with the Skull Empire, they won't have time to take over the Borant system. Borant benefits. But we have so little information.
beats.gist: Carl finds Manasa dead in a trailer and tells chat they were bait.

beats.headline: I punch a level-75 guard
beats.text: The elves are glowing on acorns when a pregnant fathom dwarf named Eunice lays their leader out with a rolling pin. An Icer freezes her solid, and two level-75 swordsmen lift their blades over her and the boy lying across her. So I punch the nearest one. It is like punching a Sherman tank: I dent it, and it does not stagger. Warning: branded a troublemaker, attacked on sight. Then Mic Drop: a one-armed kid under my arm, a boom jug in the air, Puddle Jumper to a roof across the street. The remaining eight elves are crisped. The temple burns, and the house next door with it.
beats.gist: Carl punches a level-75 guard like a Sherman tank and burns a temple and house.

beats.headline: Talking to the letter
beats.text: Mordecai works it out. The Mysterious Letter from GumGum's inventory is a spent Suppurating Eye scroll, a lich spell, and the blood on it is the caster's. Out of my inventory, whoever cast it can see and hear what's near it. That's how he answered me with a dead woman on a roof. Donut says we use it. So on a rooftop at night I set it on the tiles and we perform: stuffed animals worth stealing, a filing cabinet to loot, a hole to hammer through the ceiling of the office. Donut overacts. It's too late to fix that. The letter goes back in my pack.
beats.gist: Mordecai identifies the Mysterious Letter as a spent Suppurating Eye scroll that lets the caster see.

beats.headline: Magistrate of a town that ignores me
beats.text: Three achievements scroll by after the blast. Assassin, for a ranking town official. Ultimate Extreme Power, a Platinum Tyrant's Box, and control of the whole settlement. CockBlock, for killing an NPC another crawler needed. My title goes from Royal Bodyguard to Magistrate Carl, until the floor collapses. I don't laugh. The quest is still sitting in my menu, which means we may have just killed the wrong bird. Two of the town's bird people hover over the roof and I tell them I'm on magistrate business. They tell me, less politely, to go back to the Desperado.
beats.gist: Three achievements scroll by after the blast, making Carl Magistrate Carl until the floor collapses.

beats.headline: Fireball, for once
beats.text: The muted room fills with krasue peeling their heads free, trailing organs; one slaps me in the face with a still-beating heart. We back out into the smoke of the living room and I pull the Fireball or Custard lotto ticket. Last time it cast custard. I scratch it expecting custard again. Fireball. Spicy! It rolls through the doorway, shatters the jamb on both sides and goes off against Featherfall's corpse in its hoop of bone. The floor buckles. The room turns to Xs and half drops to the level below. The red dots circling Donut on the roof all disappear.
beats.gist: Krasue slap Carl with a beating heart; Carl casts Fireball, destroying a floor and red dots.

beats.headline: A forester
beats.text: Donut asks what I'd do if I could do anything. Not fixing boats. Not the Navy, either; it was the Coast Guard, whatever Bea told people. I think of the college applications I started and never finished. The forestry service, as a forester. I've seen enough ocean to last a lifetime. I'd be happy alone in the woods, watching for forest fires. She says she and Zev will be a television writing team, Gossip Girl with an intergalactic slant, and maybe if the shows are good enough people won't be so interested in watching real people kill each other. You surprise me every day, Donut.
beats.gist: Donut asks Carl what he would do; he wants to be a forester watching for fires.

beats.headline: A case for the gem
beats.text: The epicentre is the gem, not Remex, and I have one thing that might hold it: the glass case Miss Quill's Kimaris came in. It protects against most, not all, forms of abuse, and every opening carries a 1.5% chance of blasting you with fire, which I read after opening it. I close it around the floating gem without letting my hands touch it, hook the latch, and try to pull it into my inventory. Yeah. Nice try, asshole. So I let go, and it hangs there around the gem, the cracks spreading, two and a half minutes on the clock.
beats.gist: Carl closes Miss Quill's Kimaris glass case around a floating gem and fails to inventory it.

beats.headline: Naked, running east
beats.text: Mordecai says every magical item off, now. Everything I wear is magical except the jacket, underwear included, so it all goes into my inventory. I post the two ways out in the quest chat, and three crawlers answer the same way: the back room at the Desperado Club disappeared when the saferooms closed. That leaves the stairwell three kilometres east. Katia jogs up with a handful of strangers. Magical gear off, I tell them; sixteen minutes, full speed. One of them finally asks why I'm naked. I point east. Go.
beats.gist: Carl puts his magical gear in his inventory and tells Katia and strangers to run east.

beats.headline: Congratulations, unanswered
beats.text: Mordecai is in his room, safe. He'll sit and twiddle his thumbs for three days; we won't notice the difference. The guards came back on the second burst with a single life point each, and he'd have me killing them if I were there. Then I tell him congratulations. He doesn't answer. Donut works it out: we make the fourth floor, and he gets to go home once the dungeon is over. I think of Remex, about to finish his duty too. Of Signet, Quint, Pustule, GumGum, Miss Quill, and little one-armed Ricky Joe. I wonder if his mom ever had her baby.
beats.gist: Carl tells Mordecai congratulations, but Mordecai does not answer.

beats.headline: All about progression and training
beats.text: Odette runs the footage of me crossing the city in a one-armed leather jacket and nothing else while I sit on her couch in a loincloth of toilet paper. Then she explains how we were robbed: a Syndicate court said pay us, and Borant burned its one veto of the season so it wouldn't. I laugh. It doesn't matter how hard we work, we keep getting screwed. We messed up chasing quests when we should have been grinding, and we're not going to make that mistake again. It's all about progression and training. The explosion still counts: I go from twenty-one to twenty-seven.
beats.gist: Odette shows Carl footage of him in a one-armed leather jacket while he wears toilet paper.

beats.headline: A shield left behind on the tracks
beats.text: My pedicure buffs have lapsed, and a Drek baby finds that out by gnawing on the sole of my foot. Then they get through the first door, and the alarm trap plays Fergalicious loud enough to hurt. I check the map for a straight run of track and cast Protective Shell. The shell stays where it's cast. The train doesn't. It sweeps back through cars sixteen to twenty and off the end, pushing every mob in the way ahead of it. Car sixteen is all blood after that, with a Psycho Sticker so flat it doesn't even show on the map.
beats.gist: Carl casts Protective Shell on a track, and the train pushes mobs into it.

beats.headline: The magistrate’s necklace
beats.text: The Tyrant's box holds ten thousand gold and the Enchanted Necklace of the Haute Bourgeoisie. One poor sapphire on it, for the town I ended up magistrate of on the third floor, worth 432 gold in taxes every ten days if I keep it. Plus five dexterity and Talon Strike, which turns the side of my bare foot into a slashing weapon with a two percent chance to cast Eviscerate. It sits heavier than it should under my shirt. We didn't wear dog tags in the Coast Guard. The boss box is a tome for Bang Bro: fire and electric damage on my gauntlet.
beats.gist: Carl takes ten thousand gold and the Enchanted Necklace of the Haute Bourgeoisie from the Tyrant's box.

beats.headline: Messages from deceased Crawlers
beats.text: Brandon's message was sitting in a folder I never noticed: Messages from deceased Crawlers. He and Henry held the line against the shade gremlins so Imani, Elle and the others could get away, with ten minutes on the clock and the stairwell twenty off. He'd fought with his brother Chris, who left the party. If I see Chris, I'm to tell him Brandon's sorry, and that he loves him. When I close it, Brandon comes off my list. Mordecai says to apply my buffs first, and I tell him where to go. One hour of Bare Knuckles on the wooden dummies.
beats.gist: Carl reads a message from Brandon, who held the line against shade gremlins for others.

beats.headline: A bucket of pink glitter
beats.text: First time at a workbench. I point the Goo-inator at a swordsman's breastplate, pick Freeform, and bend iron like dough. The achievement is Martha Stewart, and the Bronze Crafter's Box holds pliers, a tape measure and a bucket of pink glitter. Not a vial. A bucket. Some of it's on the floor before I can store it, and I know from experience it's there for good. Mordecai says the shaping tool weakens what it shapes, and that a saferoom may keep you from dying at a bench, but botch it badly enough and you'll wish you were dead.
beats.gist: Carl uses the Goo-inator to bend a swordsman's breastplate and receives a bucket of pink glitter.

beats.headline: Five westerns for five books
beats.text: Limp Richard, the mole man at the general store, has read his Andre Norton a few dozen times. Shopkeepers get no entertainment feeds, he says, only books and comics, and he has fifteen, sixteen counting the one with its last chapters torn out. I trade him five westerns I've already read for three Nortons, The Lathe of Heaven and The Forever War. Donut says I'm a terrible negotiator. The Coast Guard taught me what books are worth to a bored man who has run out. In a couple of days he'll be jonesing, and once we can backtrack, we swing by again.
beats.gist: Carl trades five westerns to Limp Richard for three Nortons, The Lathe of Heaven and The Forever War.

beats.headline: The Gangway Chock
beats.text: I've built two kinds of defence at the engineering bench. The Gangway Chock was a swordsman's breastplate, thinned to a fifth of an inch and big enough to wedge the gap between cars. The door blocks are weight benches turned into wedges, with crossbars through the handholds, and I made them too slim. At Phantom Kangaroo a pollyslog walks into one, finds it can't board, and goes berserk. The doors on this train do not bounce back. One loses both arms and the other is cut in half. I measure the doorway while there's time.
beats.gist: Carl builds a Gangway Chock and slim door blocks at an engineering bench.

beats.headline: Vernon’s loop
beats.text: Vernon, the yellow line's dwarf conductor, drinks in the break room because the engineer ignores him and the janitors try to eat him. He talks freely once he notices Donut is royalty. Everyone gets off at 435, he says; then it goes fuzzy, and he's standing at station 10 with the train reset. A drawing of his wife in his pocket stays with him through every reset while the original waits in his cabin, so now there are dozens, and ten gold coins have become hundreds. The one time he's heard of an engineer leaving his car was a derailment. When Donut's suitcase opens on his counter, the ants take him.
beats.gist: Vernon, the yellow line's dwarf conductor, talks freely once he notices Donut is royalty.

beats.headline: There is no wife
beats.text: Katia's sorry for Vernon, saving up to buy his wife a house. There is no wife, I tell her. He wasn't lying; he believed it. This floor has been open one day. When they generate a floor, the NPCs are given artificial memories as part of the story. Before this he was probably a dwarf doing whatever the fourth floor was the last time they ran it. No home, no wife. And they aren't computer programs. They're living creatures who believe this is the real world. It's just as bad as what they've done to us.
beats.gist: Carl tells Katia that Vernon has no wife and that NPCs receive artificial memories.

beats.headline: Nine prizes on a carousel
beats.text: The fans vote to let me pick. Two potions with no description, five hundred bombs, two thousand books, a pair of chaps. My father's 1965 Harley, with the dent in the tank from the day I knocked it over, the one time he beat me, bloody, with a belt. My own tool chest from the shop, and I think it's empty. A thick book with the anarchy symbol on the cover glints as the carousel turns. The last time I caught a glint of light, it saved my life. I'm a Compensated Anarchist. I pick prize six.
beats.gist: Fans vote for Carl to pick from nine prizes on a carousel; he picks prize six.

beats.headline: The twenty-fifth holder of the Cookbook
beats.text: Twenty-four crawlers carried this before me. Different seasons, different species, worlds that aren't there any more. Whatever I do from here, I'm finishing somebody else's work, and most of them never got to finish theirs.
beats.gist: Carl is the twenty-fifth holder of the Cookbook, following twenty-four crawlers from vanished worlds and species.

beats.headline: The explosives chapter first
beats.text: The book is sorted into chapters: potions in one, explosives in another, and a list of monsters and what they are weak to. Some of the people who wrote in it filled pages. Some managed a line. I go to the explosives first, obviously, and the first note that catches my eye is about infusing bombs at a sapper’s table.
beats.gist: Carl reads a book with sections for potions, explosives, and monster weaknesses to find sapper's table infusions.

beats.headline: A dirty trick, well executed
beats.text: Most viewers never see Mordecai; managers are edited out of the feed. People with press passes, like Odette, can. So somebody made the connection between him and Chaco and floated the idea of trolling the vote. I look up into the air and tell whoever's watching: that was a dick move, but brilliantly executed. Good job. Then I get over it. Most crawlers don't have a manager at all. Bautista and the Cookbook have shown me what crowdsourcing is worth, and bounty or not, I need to add as many people to my chat as I can.
beats.gist: Carl tells the viewers that trolling the vote was a brilliantly executed dick move.

beats.headline: One spin of the wheel
beats.text: The comp chip I've been carrying is a hundred thousand, the maximum bet, and every bet over the minimum takes a red spot off Tito's wheel. With the chip, two are left: Nothing! and getting stabbed in the stomach by the croupier. I bet it anyway. The wheel stops on Spin Again, right beside the half-million sliver, and on the second spin it hangs one click from Nothing! and settles on green. Scroll of Upgrade. My toe ring goes from plus three strength to plus ten and adds five to Powerful Strike. Tito asks if I want another go. Yeah, no.
beats.gist: Carl bets a hundred thousand comp chip on Tito's wheel to remove red spots.

beats.headline: Which rail is hot
beats.text: I have no multimeter, so I make one: a curved rod wired to a hob-lobber fuse, thrown across the rails one pairing at a time. The fuse only blows when it touches the third rail and something else, which is how it should be. Donut's clockwork Mongo confirms it by exploding. I spray a big X on the side of the next train so Meadow Lark and Bautista's crew know it's the last one down the line for a while. Then I lower two Jelly Bombs onto the track with a fishing pole: a plunger idea from the cookbook, changed just enough to look like mine.
beats.gist: Carl makes a multimeter from a curved rod and hob-lobber fuse to find the third rail.

beats.headline: What the engineer says about the gate
beats.text: The derailment works: level twenty-nine, and the engineer climbs out of his tipped-over car. Gore-Gore thinks we were passengers, so he answers. Stop 434 is barren. At 435 the other employees take a portal back to the depot, and it does something to their memory. He drives his engine car into a gate past 435 and comes out at the depot; the other nineteen cars are gone. Passengers who ride through get deep-cleaned. Sometimes there are bones. The engine car isn't cleaned. Nobody rides in it but engineers, and he'd be honor-bound to slay us.
beats.gist: The derailment works on level twenty-nine and the engineer climbs out of his tipped-over car.

beats.headline: Ten and a half percent
beats.text: Gore-Gore goes into the church-like club by the station for mead and comes out calling us saboteurs, blades out of his wrists. Magic missiles bounce off him. Every punch I land adds one and a half to the chance my gauntlet calls his god, and nobody said it stacks. I'm at ten and a half when he gets me by the throat. Protective Shell throws him down the stairs, and since he's still holding on, it throws me too. Then he says he feels it in his chest, and there's a timer over his head. I drop-kick him onto the third rail.
beats.gist: Carl drop-kicks Gore-Gore onto the third rail.

beats.headline: Surprise Three
beats.text: The Dismemberment Limited has one pair of doors, by the driver, and Levi the Seventh begs us not to get on. Then the quest: don't let the Fleshers eat him, or every crawler aboard becomes one. Katia and I brace a slab of metal against the back door while Donut and Mongo rip at the flaps of skin curling round its edges. Dismember the war mage leans on the other side, explaining what he'll do to us. On three, Donut opens a Hole in the plate, I pull his head through by his silver hair, and she closes it.
beats.gist: Carl and Donut stop the Fleshers from eating Levi the Seventh on the Dismemberment Limited.

beats.headline: Neural Enhancer #544
beats.text: After the recap a Bronze Benefactor Box arrives from the Valtay Corporation, stamped Keeping the Best of You Alive. Inside is a blue and yellow capsule: a permanent change to my brain that installs Identify and Analyze Subspace Portals. I put it in my inventory first, to make sure nothing's living in it, then swallow it with cold coffee. A new tab, Third-Party Upgrades. The doorway out to the coffee shop glows purple, and when I ask for a visual it shows me Nodd the bopca behind the counter, picking his nose. I can see through doorways now.
beats.gist: Carl swallows a blue and yellow capsule from the Valtay Corporation to see through doorways.

beats.headline: Fist bumps all round
beats.text: I get the dance floor's attention and ask every crawler in the club for their chat details. We should all make a habit of it, so information can move: there are probably lots of ways off this floor, and everybody needs to know them. There are about twenty of them, most around level twenty. Bomo looks close to a heart attack, but I fist-bump the whole room, add twenty-two names, and make Donut do the same. Now a guy named Koki has found a way to message everyone on his list at once, and my inbox is a mess.
beats.gist: Carl asks every crawler in the club for chat details and fist-bumps the room.

beats.headline: Stealing the Nightmare Express
beats.text: The plan: Donut Puddle Jumps us up the track, I hit Protective Shell as the train reaches us, and the shell clears every car. Donut's jump won't land as close to the platform as we wanted, and the train speeds up instead of slowing. I jump. I don't make it. Two potions on, I'm lying above the cowcatcher. I punch through the cab window: two bodies in the gore, and the boiler about to go. A demon woman in the firebox talks me through the valves. Level thirty-two, three boss boxes, and I have stolen a train.
beats.gist: Carl steals a train after punching through a cab window and talking to a firebox demon.

beats.headline: The pit at 436
beats.text: Abyss Station has one steep stair, and it takes almost an hour to climb. At the top is a burning pit at least a mile across, its walls covered in portals. For a moment I'm at the Grand Canyon with my mom, her hand tight on my wrist. Then a train bursts out of a portal and falls, and there's no engine car. So the colored trains don't loop back in time: the cars get thrown in here, the engines go home, and they build new trains. The portal analysis says three things I'm carrying count as keys. One of them is that stupid conductor hat.
beats.gist: Carl climbs a steep stair at Abyss Station for almost an hour to find a burning pit.

beats.headline: You can't save them all
beats.text: I send what we know to everybody on my list: four ways back to the early stations, two sure and two maybe. The replies all tell the same story. Trains out of service at an alarming rate, people stranded, dozens of miles to hike, almost six days left. Mordecai's voice in my head: you can't save them all. York's last entry in the back of the cookbook won't leave me: the hive, protecting those who are yours even if you never knew them, and the consolation of dying for a cause worth it. I'm not sure I agree with that last part. I fall asleep thinking there's something more to be done.
beats.gist: Carl sends four ways back to early stations to his list, but trains are out of service.

beats.headline: Widget, briefly
beats.text: Station and Repair Hub E: a yard of engine cars, a shaking fence, and thousands of ghouls. A grease gremlin named Widget rides a basket down a chain from his tower, takes one look at us and asks what happened to CrackJack. I tell him. He doesn't mind much, as long as Brandy is fine. He says a train called the Escape Velocity goes to all the stairwells; you catch it at 89, up the Tangerine line. He unhooks our wrecked cars and waves, and the spider ghoul Donut shot gets back up and takes his head off.
beats.gist: Carl meets Widget, a grease gremlin, who says the Escape Velocity train leaves from 89.

beats.headline: Six mimics at Terminus
beats.text: Madison, from human resources, can't tell me how to get to Yard A, or whether she's ever been to her own apartment. Mandatory overtime, she says. The back of the cookbook has an essay on this: challenge an NPC when they don't know what they should, kind but firm. So I push, and she tells me what she does know. She tells employees overtime is mandatory, and she's benefits manager for the six Station Mimics at Terminus, which get cranky if not enough passengers go into them. Bautista is nearly at 433. I message him: don't get off at Terminus. It's a trap.
beats.gist: Carl pushes Madison, a benefits manager, to reveal that six Station Mimics at Terminus trap passengers.

beats.headline: My name on the back
beats.text: Katia gets me alone at station 24 and hands me a black ticket with a gold skull on it. A PVP coupon: kill the crawler named on the back and collect three gold boxes, a platinum box and a player level. The back says Crawler #4,122. Carl. She watched Donut stuff it under the track. Imani tells me the first player killer in a party gets a coupon for every member, and that Donut already talked it through with her. So this is the only one anybody saw Donut throw away. I'll ask her, but up in the production trailer, not down here.
beats.gist: Katia gives Carl a black ticket with a gold skull to kill Crawler #4,122.

beats.headline: Not reading this one
beats.text: Planet Beautiful parks us in a submarine and a real sound booth, and hands me a script on beauty pageants written by an AI consultant they got at a discount, because Borant started the season before it finished scanning us. Chad-class males. Roasties. A video of me eating a roast beef sandwich. I tell Bin, the producer, I'm not reading it. He says his little show is suddenly a ratings powerhouse and Titan is all over him, and offers me mechanized warfare, video arcades or pasteurization. I take the video games. On the way out I steal the fridge shelves, the makeup table and the couch.
beats.gist: Planet Beautiful puts Carl in a submarine and a sound booth with a beauty pageant script.

beats.headline: Why I never told Donut
beats.text: Odette warned me about Hekla, and I never passed it on to Donut or Mordecai. Standing in our own space with thirty of her Daughters, I finally admit why: part of me thinks Donut would be better off with them. Then I look at Eva, the one at Hekla's shoulder, with thirteen kills' worth of skulls over her head, and that thought goes. I tell Donut in chat to watch Eva and to keep an eye on Hekla too. I put an invisibility potion and Mordecai's Special Brew on my hotlist. Then I say yes, out loud.
beats.gist: Carl tells Donut in chat to watch Eva and Hekla after seeing Eva's thirteen skulls.

beats.headline: A floor that feeds itself
beats.text: A head on the cab floor growls and I stomp it. The next one is a torso reaching for the fairy, and I read it before I crush it. Blister Ghoul, level twenty, spat out by a soul-crystal ghoul generator at stop 72: every non-undead mob that dies on this floor births one, and every mob on the floor is sick with something that will kill it. Soul crystals again, like the one in the bomb I still haven't dared take out at my sapper's table. This isn't a maze. It's an almost perpetual engine, and in a day these things will be everywhere.
beats.gist: Carl stomps a head and crushes a level twenty Blister Ghoul.

beats.headline: The bait was a bakery owner
beats.text: Donut pins the healer who was hiding in the engineer's apartment, and I talk instead of fighting. Silfa admits it was Eva, not Hekla, who told her to stop healing Katia. My read: Katia dies, I lose my temper on the nearest target, Hekla has to put me down, and Donut, with Mordecai, has nowhere to go but the Daughters. Silfa says her own daughters, the two mages at the door, had orders to kill me first if anything went wrong. She owns a bakery. She just wants to go home.
beats.gist: Donut pins a healer in an engineer's apartment while Carl talks.

beats.headline: Seven hundred hats
beats.text: At station 75, with Katia kept out of sight, I shout for hats and keys, and I expect people to hang on to them for resale. They don't. They coordinate and spread the word, and in twenty minutes I have over seven hundred hats and fifteen colored-line keys for the crawlers stranded at the pit. There is hope for us. Not a lot, but it's there. Donut whispers that we could sell them for three and a half million gold. If we save those people without the hats, I tell her, absolutely.
beats.gist: Carl shouts for hats and keys at station 75 and receives seven hundred hats and fifteen keys.

beats.headline: A portal on the front of a cart
beats.text: Station 75's yard has ten rapid-response interdiction carts that never ran. The blade across the front is a portal: it throws everything on the line to a trainyard or into the abyss, and the cart only starts with gnoll hands on two plates eight feet apart. Every gnoll corpse in the station has been chewed to nothing, and that is no accident. So, two carts per line: the first set to the abyss to clear the track, the second fifteen minutes behind, set to the trainyard, for the crawlers standing on the rails. It needs Growler Gary's hands.
beats.gist: Carl finds ten interdiction carts in Station 75's yard with portal blades that require gnoll hands.

beats.headline: The first cart plays "Physical"
beats.text: Six rapid-response carts, Growler Gary's hands roped to the pedestals because we have no duct tape, and an alarm trap on every one, because the carts barely make a sound and the people at the end of the line need to hear them coming. The test cart gets a one-minute delay, the rest thirty. The trap plays anything that ever charted on the Billboard Hot 100. This one picks "Physical" by Olivia Newton John, loud enough that I take damage. I push the throttle and jump. It hits the portal and is gone, and I can still hear it, far below.
beats.gist: Carl pushes a throttle and jumps as a cart playing Physical by Olivia Newton John takes damage.

beats.headline: The vermillion engine sent home
beats.text: The ghouls out of 72 are piling up behind the dead Vermillion train outside station 36, so I send our battered vermillion engine down the line at them. Hobgoblin dynamite roped to the rear shelf, and a long pole with an impact hob-lobber on the end, set high enough that only one of the big stage-three monsters will trip it. I ease it to full speed, and on the way out the front window I find one of Eva's sabers in the gore and take it. The blast knocks everybody at 36 off their feet. Level thirty-five, explosives handling eleven. Imani would rather I didn't do that again.
beats.gist: Carl sends a battered vermillion engine at ghouls with hobgoblin dynamite and an impact hob-lobber.

beats.headline: A crossing gate on the track
beats.text: Bautista's second cart never reached him, so we take one down the Mindaro line ourselves. Five crawlers are running on the track, and one of them fires an ice bolt at us before we plough through them and send them to trainyard E. Then, outside station 433, a red and white crossing barrier with a stop sign, blinking, where no barrier should be. I stare at it for two seconds, and that's enough. I go to flip the portal back to the abyss, and hesitate. A fleshy appendage runs from it up into the station. We hit it, and the whole station mimic goes to trainyard E.
beats.gist: Carl takes a Mindaro line cart, ploughs through five crawlers, and hits a station mimic.

beats.headline: A stairwell under the mimic
beats.text: The recap shows a group in a dark, dripping cave with a single stairwell, glowing below the ground and corkscrewing up into the dark. That's station 433, where we took the mimic away. A city boss sitting on a stairwell hides it from the map, same as Grimaldi did, so there's a way down for anybody still stuck on that side of the tracks. Donut wants to know if we could have just gone back down there. Probably. Katia points out they still have to find it, and there are five more mimics up there.
beats.gist: Carl and Donut recall station 433, where a city boss hides a corkscrewing stairwell from the map.

beats.headline: Smacked, and the ring comes off
beats.text: Mordecai smacks me. Right on the side of the head, and he doesn't freeze or get teleported for it. My father used to do the same, harder. He says he shouldn't have, and keeps going: crawlers ride out the ninth floor with their heads down; a Divine Suffering ring on the finger of a man the whole universe is watching is idiocy we don't need; and if I keep it he'll tell Donut to stay away from me on the sixth floor. I pull it off and feel my strength drop. We'll talk about selling it on the fifth floor. Don't touch me ever again.
beats.gist: Mordecai smacks Carl on the head and removes his Divine Suffering ring to protect him.

beats.headline: A cart hung over the hole
beats.text: The Def Leppard cart won't fit the hallway into station 36, so Zhang shrinks it and we roll it in. Five legs of welded metal, one between each pair of stairwells, meeting overhead: it looks like a campus art installation, and it's a crane. Imani's magic chain lifts the cart until it hangs nose down, the portal half an inch off the marble, tuned to the abyss. At one day left the Iron Tangle announces its own self-destruction. All over the floor the centres of the stations fall away and the Krakaren pour up into the rooms. In ours they pour into my portal.
beats.gist: Zhang shrinks the Def Leppard cart to fit the hallway into station 36.

beats.headline: Pulled in by the foot
beats.text: Two neighbourhood bosses guard the employee line, and my gauntlet can bring Grull out of one of them. So I lure them into the tunnel. Katia pins one and Li Na chains it unconscious. The other gets torn up by Li Jun, Mongo and Donut before I can stop them, and I punch it until the notification blinks. Ten seconds. It clamps onto the track, so Zhang brings the portal to it. We drop it at one second. It has let go of the track and wrapped that hand around my foot, which I can't feel, because it's numb. Then I'm through.
beats.gist: Carl lures two neighborhood bosses into a tunnel where Katia, Li Na, Li Jun, Mongo, and Donut attack.

beats.headline: Death Challenge
beats.text: The world freezes, heavy metal starts, and my face goes up in the air with Death Challenge stamped across it. On one side a level-ninety Mimic Rex with over twenty-three thousand kills; on the other Grull, sponsored, the announcer says, by the Maestro. I go invisible for thirty seconds, which is my intelligence times two. A hob-lobber through a Jibber-Jabber's mouth. Grull splits the mimic in half as if it were nothing. Then Mordecai's Special Brew: thirty seconds of almost-invulnerability, during which Grull steps on me and a train car rolls over me, and I heal every time.
beats.gist: The world freezes, heavy metal starts, and Carl faces a Death Challenge against Grull and a Mimic Rex.

beats.headline: I will break them
beats.text: Fire Brandy went into the pit so she would not lose any more children. Tizquick went because his daughter was a lie. Everyone here jumped into certain death to save me, and I finally see how much I need other people. Level forty-one. At the stairwell, in the cookbook's hidden pad: the NPCs and the mobs are victims as much as we are, and killing them is the best thing we can do for them. But all twenty-four before me only talked about burning this place down. We need to start killing them too. I will break them all.
beats.gist: Carl reaches level forty-one and vows to break those who run the game.

beats.headline: Every bounty on me, doubled
beats.text: The stairwell drops us into a sandstorm and an achievement. The Quarry Sees Another Spring: a Gold Venison Box, which is just money, and every bounty against me now and in the future gets a times-two modifier. Nobody warned me. Not Mordecai, not the cookbook. I can't even swear about it properly, because every time I open my mouth it fills with sand. Tens of thousands of crawlers didn't make it through the last few hours of the fourth floor. We lean into the wind toward a town we can't see, talking in chat.
beats.gist: The stairwell drops Carl into a sandstorm and a Gold Venison Box.

beats.headline: What a god leaves behind
beats.text: The Grull achievements pay out. Being stepped on by a god earns me a Platinum Spicy Box, because the AI is a pervert, and inside is a toe ring with two benefits, Sticky Feet and Super Spreader. Wiping out the wall monitors earns me a tattoo only a cover-up sleeve will hide: a little lizard foot under my left eye, and lizards hit me twenty percent harder now. Surviving a god's attack earns me a Legendary Deity's Box. Pawna's Tears. Plus five to any spell or skill I choose. Mordecai's talon shakes when he holds it.
beats.gist: Carl receives a Platinum Spicy Box for being stepped on by a god, containing a toe ring.

beats.headline: A dead boss in a broken egg
