beats.text: A gnome biplane drops out of nowhere with two egg-shaped things slung under it, and my explosives skill doesn't twitch. Donut teleports us to the ridge, my hob-lobber goes off too low and behind, and the plane limps away trailing smoke. The egg bounces and does nothing. Donut's clockwork Mongos crack it open: inside is a goose, a level 45 neighborhood boss, killed by the landing. The deployment device is rusty and broken. I take the goose and the shell. It feels like we're on rails. Then eight more planes start circling down, and we run for Hump Town.
beats.gist: A gnome biplane drops a broken egg containing a dead level 45 goose neighborhood boss.

beats.headline: Somebody has to put her down
beats.text: The recap shows how Ifechi died: Lucia Mar put a spell on her head, Mordecai thinks, so Florin's own shotgun killed her, and the dungeon gave him the kill. The kid talks to people who aren't there. She's insane. Katia says she needs to be dealt with. I say we need to put her down. Donut calls dibs on the dogs. Mordecai says her spell has a big vulnerability, and that they may want her killed. Then the board goes up, and I'm number two.
beats.gist: Lucia Mar put a spell on Ifechi, so Florin killed her with a shotgun.

beats.headline: Stay out of city hall
beats.text: Firas puddle jumps us onto the town hall balcony. Downstairs, Louis's cloud drops the two guards on the basement door, and they turn out to be changelings in the shape of camels. I kill one, a level 49 Changeling Principal, and keep his head for Mordecai. Under the trapdoor is a map of the Necropolis of Anser that installs itself into my party's map and crumbles. Past the quadrant barrier, chained to the wall, is an old gnome, Wynne, the commandant's uncle. I get a quest to free him. Five crawlers arrive on the far side, Wynne begs them to kill him, and one does.
beats.gist: Firas puddle jumps Carl onto the town hall balcony.

beats.headline: Total, Utter Failure
beats.text: An achievement for failing a quest inside five minutes. Reward: Ha. A camel rocket blows in the door, so I throw an eighth-strength hob-lobber down the hall, and something a camel was carrying on the outside goes up with it. The town hall catches fire. Donut opens a hole in the wall, I summon Bautista's stuffed grulke toad in the alley and send it hopping over the city wall, and Donut puddle jumps us down the street. A camel tells us frog creatures attacked. Then the town hall collapses. Donut says people are going to start thinking I have a problem with authority.
beats.gist: Carl gets an achievement for failing a quest inside five minutes.

beats.headline: Nine kilometers up
beats.text: The Valtay pill gives me elevation and airspeed. That's it, I think, and don't say out loud. The elevation display takes some figuring. Planetary sea level puts me at minus 92,000 meters. The gauge labeled Gravitational Zone Sea Level says 8,932 meters, which means we're standing about nine kilometers above the water quadrant, roughly the height of Everest. Which means the Necropolis of Anser under our feet is enormous. We need to give those guys in the tomb all the help we can, because if they fail, we're the ones going in there.
beats.gist: Carl takes a Valtay pill for elevation and airspeed and finds the Necropolis of Anser enormous.

beats.headline: Ruckus, and the second stage
beats.text: Four missiles with surefires in a launcher on my swivel seat, telescope clamped beside it. The first one's second stage lights, then the whole thing blows a few hundred feet short, and the exhaust has burned my right side. So much for hitting the Wasteland from the ground. I have Katia turn around and drive straight at the bird, lock the last three on the wing joint, the neck and the buzzsaw's cable, and pull all three pins. The wing comes off and Ruckus wraps up in its own cable. I want that saw intact.
beats.gist: Carl fires missiles from a swivel seat, but the first blows and burns his right side.

beats.headline: A letter I never delivered
beats.text: Chris Andrews took the water castle, which means he's in here with us. He's Brandon's brother. I keep Brandon's last note in my scratch pad: they fought, Chris left, and now it's too late to tell him he loves him. I promised myself I'd give it to Chris. But he took a rock race, stopped talking to Imani, and, the Sledge says, crushed Frank Q's head at the Desperado Club counter and walked out. That isn't the quiet man I remember. Imani thinks he wants to team up. I've had enough of that with Hekla.
beats.gist: Carl keeps a note from Brandon to his brother Chris, who crushed Frank Q's head.

beats.headline: The helmet and the fish
beats.text: The sniper in the Vahana's basket wears a round black half-helmet with no face shield. My dad wore one like it. A month before he left, he ripped it off and smashed my fish tank, and I picked the mollies up off the floor with cut fingers and put them in a cup. They died anyway. I didn't cry, and that bothered me for weeks. What I took from it was: never get a pet again, all they do is die. Wrong lesson, probably. I look across at Donut on Mongo, doing her best to look menacing. She's not a pet anymore. I don't know if she's better off.
beats.gist: Carl sees a sniper in a Vahana's basket wearing a helmet like the one his father used.

beats.headline: He wants the Gate
beats.text: The Wasteland is broken, and what's left of the castle is a house, no bigger than a regular one, hanging from a single balloon at the top of the bubble. The Commandant is in there with his daughter. Katia wants to put another missile in it. I want to go up and take it the old-fashioned way. Henrik has a watch, the Commandant has one, and I'm pretty sure the Mad Dune Mage has the third, and they all come together as the Gate of the Feral Gods. It's a celestial-equivalent item. They don't put that in here to be ignored. I want it.
beats.gist: Carl wants the Gate of the Feral Gods, a celestial-equivalent item made of three watches.

beats.headline: Death Trap, renamed
beats.text: The gnomish Drop Bear that Louis and the archers dragged in runs on real gasoline, and I have plenty in cans. I fill it a quarter of the way to keep it light. The name stencilled on the nose is Death Trap, with four bombs painted after it. I spray over it and write Nightmare II. There's no runway, so I pull the emergency balloon lever, and we rise tail-first to the ceiling of the bubble, about five kilometers up. Then I throttle up, skitter along the ceiling toward the house, cut the power and coast in.
beats.gist: Carl fills a gnomish Drop Bear with gasoline, renames Death Trap to Nightmare II, and flies it.

beats.headline: Head first into the disposal
beats.text: The boss is Denise, a feral goose in a blue bonnet, and the rules say no magic and no physical damage, with three minutes before the house hits the ground. I grab the lemonade, because it has to be the answer. It's lemonade. The AI calls that a Wild Goose Chase. What actually hurts her is anything that was already in the house: a mug, the pitcher. Bonnie pointed at the sink earlier. I remember the two switches beside it, shove Denise head-first into the drain, and yell at Donut to flip them. The garbage disposal does the rest.
beats.gist: Carl fights Denise, a feral goose in a blue bonnet, using a garbage disposal to kill her.

beats.headline: The moment I change my mind
beats.text: I strip the house: two laptops, three televisions, the gaming consoles, the bikes, a kayak, the Christmas tree and the electrical panel, whose outlets keep working as long as they stay attached. No guns, though the doormat says they had some. At Skarn's house I set down Bonnie's own bed and the picture of her with her mother and father. Loita tells us to stop concerning ourselves with NPCs. When I look back, the girl is sobbing into Juice Box, holding the pink rabbit Mongo gave her. I'd been toying with an idea and dismissed it as too risky. That's the moment I change my mind.
beats.gist: Carl strips a house of laptops, televisions, consoles, bikes, a kayak, a Christmas tree and an electrical panel.

beats.headline: A commercial that goes off script
beats.text: Before we transfer, I set off a disco ball in the crafting room, a smoke curtain soaked in an invisibility potion, and it coats the robot and me in rainbow dust. In the trailer I lean over Loita to ask whether these things can go into space. I leave robot Donut next to her with orders to stay. On set I go off script and ask about Veriluxx's parent company and slavery, until the lights go red. The couch is gone. Loita is blackened, missing an arm and both lower legs, and alive. She says I did this. I tell her it was an accident.
beats.gist: Carl sets off a disco ball and a smoke curtain soaked in invisibility potion.

beats.headline: A fingernail for a shim
beats.text: Orren's version is polymers, and residue eating a panel. The truth is dumber. The back panel on robot Donut was junk. I cut my left thumbnail three-quarters through, practiced on a spare panel on the toilet, and when I leaned over Loita the second time, I broke the nail off as a shim under the tab. The disco dust was only there so they wouldn't want the doll in the studio. I told it to stay by her, and I gave her a reason to get off the couch. I tell Orren I wish I'd thought of it.
beats.gist: Carl breaks his left thumbnail to use as a shim under a tab.

beats.headline: Not as indispensable as I thought
beats.text: The house comes down for us with its whole top half hacked off, because the stairwell was in the master-bedroom closet and the quadrant would not let it leave attached. Firas fills us in. Katia got the house down to the land quadrant and worked out how to breach the castle's door, all without us, and they would be finished already if Zev hadn't asked her to wait. Part of me is proud. Part of me stings that she managed, and I'm horrified I thought it. I decide it's a necessary feeling.
beats.gist: The house falls with its top half hacked off; Firas explains Katia breached the castle door.

beats.headline: Punch him, take the bag
beats.text: Through the peephole the Mad Dune Mage is a guy in a bathrobe watching cartoons, living on top of a floor that is actually a mob. Katia yanks me back when it comes under the door, and my Protective Shell blasts the ooze away and the door with it. Ghazi runs to us, goes back for a leather bag off a burning table, and pats the flames out. I ask if he has the winding box, because the college needs it to save the world. He pats the bag: it's here. I punch him out, take the bag, and we run up the stairs.
beats.gist: Carl punches Ghazi out and takes a bag with a winding box.

beats.headline: Upside down over the ooze
beats.text: No explosives in the lab, Ghazi says, or the glass comes down on us. So Katia lobs an alarm trap in a metal ball down the stairs to distract the ooze with "Jump Around", Donut holes the floor above, and I go in upside down on Sticky Feet from my toe ring: seventy-something seconds on the ceiling. I pipe Mordecai's burn gel onto the recliner over the core and drop a torch. It burns hotter than I expected. The boss dies just as the roof comes in, and I'm buried upside down in sand.
beats.gist: Katia lobs an alarm trap to distract the ooze while Carl pipes burn gel onto a recliner.

beats.headline: Flushed into the water quadrant
beats.text: Tran opens the valve part way. The ceiling gives and the water hits like a train. I wrap myself around Donut and we tumble in the flood, my health falling; a spar off the dwarven automaton goes through my leg, and a spear of glass goes through my hand and into Donut. She never took the potion I told her to. Two heal scrolls on her, and we're a hundred and fifty meters down in the water quadrant with dead things sinking all around us. Something big is eating them.
beats.gist: Tran opens a valve, the ceiling gives, and water hits Carl and Donut like a train.

beats.headline: The second-to-last drawing
beats.text: Ghazi's note ends mid-sentence on a missing page, but the last page is drawings: two watches, the winding box, two gates, every combination and what happens. All but one end with a monster coming out on the opening side. Katia points at the circled one, where we lose the box and nothing gets out. I'm stuck on the second-to-last. I put that away and ask Mordecai whether a feral god could leave the bubble, or break the wall. Then I ask if there's a Desperado Club in this town.
beats.gist: Carl studies Ghazi's drawings of watches, a winding box, and gates to find a specific combination.

beats.headline: The only place they can die
beats.text: I flip Katia's map over and ask Mordecai if it's right. He draws nine petals round Larracos: a city dug deep like an inverted cone, a faction in each petal, fifteen thousand troops apiece, mostly NPCs. The real people there can't die; the system pulls them out first. Then the questions I actually care about. Hunters sign up until the sixth floor opens, and start at level thirty. And that floor is the only place in the game where these rich tourists can really die. Katia asks why she gets the feeling I'm about to do something really stupid.
beats.gist: Carl flips Katia's map and Mordecai draws nine petals around Larracos, an inverted cone city.

beats.headline: A ghost on the bridge
beats.text: Inside the Akula, a door Vadim swears they left open is dogged shut. Past the airlock, under a floor grate, I loot the neighborhood boss, a little box somebody had to destroy to turn the sentinel gun off, and the whole sub fills in on my map. Corpses on the bridge. And one red dot flickering between the bridge and a chamber outside the quadrant entirely. A ghost that shouldn't be in here. A glowing green pterodactyl head screams through the bulkhead, my vision flashes red, and Vadim drops with his health in the red.
beats.gist: Inside the Akula, Carl loots a box under a floor grate and sees a flickering red dot.

beats.headline: Depth charges, and everyone inside
beats.text: Something drags the Akula out of its hole and down to fifteen hundred meters. I take Henrik's body whole, watch and all. Then a sharktopus the size of a mountain comes at the window, the world freezes, and it's a Special Event boss battle with a pair of commentators. I tell Donut to drop the depth charges at maximum depth, Louis and Firas to land and get to a saferoom, and Gwen, the tomb raiders and Langley to do the same. Donut asks if the death charges will hit us too. I really hope not.
beats.gist: Something drags the Akula to fifteen hundred meters, and Carl takes Henrik's body and watch.

beats.headline: Bloodlust in the fridge
beats.text: Inside the octo-shark's mouth, a ten-minute timer, thousands of babies hammering at the bridge window. I tape a Potion of Bloodlust to a hob-lobber, duct-tape it inside the bolted minifridge, and seal Katia, Tran and me in the captain's stateroom. The window goes. Something on the other side starts turning the wheel on our door, so I hold it with one hand and hit the detonator with the other. One X on the map. Ten. Thousands. They may be babies, and half octopus. They're still sharks.
beats.gist: Carl tapes a Potion of Bloodlust to a hob-lobber inside a bolted minifridge.

beats.headline: A shell down her throat
beats.text: When the timer hits zero, Lusca lifts her head to swallow the Akula, and I cast Protective Shell. I want it to go through her like a bullet. Instead it stops her dead, like she's hit a wall that won't move, and peels her upper jaw back over her own eyes, and every baby left in her mouth dies at once. Then we're pinwheeling on Katia's rocket and buzzsaw, out of her mouth and back through her head. Winner. Then a warning that at this depth I'm losing two percent of my health a second.
beats.gist: Carl casts Protective Shell as Lusca swallows the Akula, peeling her jaw back and killing her babies.

beats.headline: A patch jacket and a dead man's kerchief
beats.text: Three levels, to 47. The gold boss box gives me Drakea's Enchanted Kerchief of Disorder: plus five Detect Traps, a level-15 Tripper once every five hours, and Remote Detonator, which means no more hobgoblin pus. Drakea wrote the twenty-second edition of the cookbook, and I need to pretend I've never heard the name. My hands shake. The platinum Spicy box gives me the Enchanted Anarchist's Battle Rattle, a sleeveless patch jacket, with an Earth patch to sew on. Apart from my zippo, the old leather jacket was the last thing I had from before. It can go.
beats.gist: Carl reaches level 47 and gets Drakea's Enchanted Kerchief of Disorder and the Enchanted Anarchist's Battle Rattle.

beats.headline: Photographs of their mothers
beats.text: Seven silver Summary Judgement boxes, and each one holds a gold piece, a single share of stock in a company from one plaintiff's system, and a photograph of that plaintiff's mother. The first is Queen Consort Ugloo, mother of Prince Stalwart of the Skull Empire. It's the kind of thing middle-school kids do. It's also valuable. I now know seven of the factions that tried to take the gate off me, and since the nagas didn't sue and will be there anyway, eight of the nine teams waiting on the ninth floor.
beats.gist: Seven silver Summary Judgement boxes hold gold, stock, and photographs of plaintiffs' mothers.

beats.headline: He sends Morris down the ladder
beats.text: The lightning towers glow and do nothing. The last piece is a panel under the necropolis, still underwater, and the only crawlers who can reach it are what is left of the tomb raiders. I tell Morris to connect it and get out of the water before the next strike. Low Thi goes to distract Quetzalcoatlus, and the boss goes straight through him and turns back for Morris. Morris gets it connected. Both of their last messages come up marked as from a deceased crawler. The quadrant is liberated. I knew they were probably going to die, and I sent them anyway.
beats.gist: Carl sends Morris to connect a panel under the necropolis to liberate the quadrant.

beats.headline: Flying a gnome biplane
beats.text: There is nowhere to take off, so Louis and Firas fly the house out over the water and I roll the drop bear off the edge of the yard. We drop like a rock, the wind catches us, and she climbs. Yoke, pedals, twin throttles, a fuel gauge and a gyroscope I do not understand. Biplane Pilot goes to three. Then I work out the gyroscope: dot in the middle means level, and the little lock on it is a crude autopilot. The whole plane still vibrates like it wants to come apart.
beats.gist: Louis and Firas fly the house over water so Carl rolls a drop bear off the yard.

beats.headline: He worships a god to survive a plane crash
beats.text: I am falling out of the sky and Quan Ch is about to finish the job. So I take Emberus as my patron, mid-air, and throw a celestial grenade. The god arrives at my position, and for a little while nothing can kill me. Then Emberus finds Orthrus, and both of them are gone.
beats.gist: Carl takes Emberus as his patron mid-air to survive Quan Ch and throws a celestial grenade.

beats.headline: He tears off Quan Ch's arm
beats.text: Quan Ch sneaks up and hits me with his lightning while the god's invulnerability is still on me, which he cannot see. I punch him in the face and a health bar appears. He stabs at me and the knife explodes. Then the buff runs out, and he does not know it. I try to tell him what he has done, and all that comes out is that he is a bully and nobody likes him. He rockets off while I am holding his casting arm. He goes. The arm stays, with three rings on it. I have Tran tell him that was just a deposit.
beats.gist: Quan Ch hits Carl with lightning, but Carl punches him and tears off his casting arm.

beats.headline: A drop of blood and five percent
beats.text: I read the notification at last. I am an acolyte of Emberus, and without a cleric or paladin class I can never rise past devotee. The rules: harm no fellow worshipper; a drop of blood at one of his temples every day, or at the sun shrine that has appeared in my personal space; five percent of looted gold into it; nothing blessed by Hellik; every church quest completed. In return, burn immunity and a ten percent chance to burn with every hit, and two glowing sun tattoos on the backs of my hands. Donut calls the tithe an outrage.
beats.gist: Carl becomes an acolyte of Emberus and receives two glowing sun tattoos on his hands.

beats.headline: Three rings off a severed arm
beats.text: Quan Ch's arm had three rings on it. A plain plus-two ring of strength, which goes on. Rockard's Ring of Sniping, which marks every creature under half health and everyone wearing magical gear, and explains a great deal about Quan; that goes on too. The third is an unenchanted gold band the system calls worthless. It sticks, and the finger crunches getting it off. Inside, it says For Daddy. I push it back onto his finger as far as the first knuckle and put the whole arm in my inventory.
beats.gist: Carl takes a plus-two ring of strength and Rockard's Ring of Sniping off Quan Ch's severed arm.

beats.headline: Frogger in the air quadrant
beats.text: My fan box gave me a stand-up Frogger machine. Not the one from my father's basement, but close, and it runs on a dwarven battery I rigged up. I suspect it was an attempt at trolling me. Two days of waiting in the air quadrant, and I spend too much of them teaching the others to dominate at Frogger. I only got good because I was locked in the basement while my dad had friends over. It helps anyway. You can take a terrible situation and still find a moment of peace. I needed reminding.
beats.gist: Carl's fan box gives him a stand-up Frogger machine powered by a rigged dwarven battery.

beats.headline: The box we swapped in a hug
beats.text: Chris hurls the winding box off the bowl and the watches go flying in two directions. It does not matter. Katia built a facsimile box in pieces in her inventory while pretending to learn the engineering table, and we swapped real for fake when we hugged at the club. The watches in it are the fakes I made to fool the dirigible gnomes. There is no god for the ninth floor. The real gate is in the water quadrant, and I tell Juice Box to fly for it. We are keeping the gate.
beats.gist: Chris hurls a winding box off the bowl, but Carl and Katia swapped it for a facsimile.

beats.headline: The worm comes out of my neck
beats.text: From under the sand, Maggie tells me the caprid came to her in the rest area, a cleric, a goat thing, a liaison, and said it would help if they killed me. Then she stops mid-sentence. Chris erupts beside the box. I take the phase potion and reach into his head, and the worm bites my palm and burrows into my arm. I drink the double-healing potion before she reaches my brain, and she comes out through my neck like a sniper's round. Mongo gets her.
beats.gist: A worm burrows into Carl's arm and exits his neck; Mongo gets the worm.

beats.headline: Come and get it
beats.text: After the last recap, Lucia Mar falls off the top spot and I am on it. Number one. Donut is fourth, Prepotente third, Quan Ch tenth. Mordecai wants the Ring of Divine Suffering tossed before I go down the stairs. Instead I hold it up for the cameras. The hunters want it, and the gate, and they can come and get it. Better: I will come to them. By the time the next floor collapses, every hunter who sets foot on it with us will be dead. I swear it on my life. I will break you all.
beats.gist: Carl takes the top spot; he holds the Ring of Divine Suffering to threaten the hunters.

beats.headline: Agent Provocateur
beats.text: The Hunting Grounds are opening and I take the bomb-focused specialisation. Agent Provocateur. I would like to be very, very good at exactly one thing, and I have picked the thing.
beats.gist: Carl takes the bomb-focused Agent Provocateur specialisation as the Hunting Grounds open.

beats.headline: Night weasels at the gate
beats.text: I walk out of a port-a-potty into the jungle, and at the village gate both mushroom guards fall over, paralysed. Something invisible is hitting my shell. I throw a sack of gunpowder at it and it gets a shape, smaller than Donut and fast. Then its partner bites my neck from behind and I'm paralysed for five minutes. Donut's missiles make them visible: six-legged black weasels with too many teeth, pets of a hunter I've never met. Chris steps on the one dragging itself toward my face and carries me into the saferoom over his shoulder.
beats.gist: Carl walks out of a port-a-potty into the jungle and paralyzes two mushroom guards.

beats.headline: The shrine takes its cut
beats.text: There is a small shrine in the corner of the room now, a disk and a cup, and the cup boils over whenever I'm near it. Every day it takes a drop of my blood. Thanks to my new religion it also takes five percent of my looted gold, and a number floats over it to say exactly how much I owe. The shrine's idea of looted includes what I got for surviving the last floor in the top ten. I paid it when Donut wasn't looking. She noticed anyway and complained for five minutes straight.
beats.gist: A shrine takes a drop of Carl's blood and five percent of his looted gold daily.

beats.headline: Zockau burns
beats.text: Zockau burns. I mark hunters with the Ring of Divine Suffering, I kill them, and I take their stats, and enough of them are inside the Desperado Club when it goes that the survivors have to be dug out. I get hurt on the way out. That part is fair.
beats.gist: Carl marks hunters with the Ring of Divine Suffering and takes their stats while Zockau burns.

beats.headline: Thirty-four hands
beats.text: I come round in the back of a cart with Miriam Dom stroking my hair. Level fifty-four now. Thirty-five of the Hand that Claws the Master achievements, which is the AI padding the count, and thirty-four Gold Hunter-Killer boxes, which is the real number. Mass Casualty Event, too: more than two hundred and fifty non-mob casualties. And it doesn't bother me nearly as much as it should. I want to be more efficient about the innocent ones. This isn't on me. They started this. Their rules. Their game.
beats.gist: Carl wakes in a cart with Miriam Dom stroking his hair at level fifty-four.

beats.headline: Room for explosions
beats.text: Mordecai says I only killed a handful of them. With Donut's kill it was thirty-five hunters. And I didn't blow the town up. It was one or two square blocks, and those barrels were only about a fourth the strength I could have made them. I have a plan for another one that's really big. Like huge. That's the best part about this floor: lots of room for explosions. Mordecai supposes I have a plan for that one, too. The hunters are released in just over thirteen hours. Oh, it's going to be spectacular.
beats.gist: Mordecai says Carl killed a handful of hunters, but with Donut it was thirty-five.

beats.headline: A stream at the back of my mind
beats.text: Something at the back of my mind has always been there, like a stream hidden in the weeds, so quiet I never noticed it. Now it's getting louder. It isn't a sound, not really, or a physical feeling. A sense of flow, rising. I've only found one way to mute it, which is to be completely at rest. Running from Zockau, it was right there. By the end of the recap it's rushing, tumbling, crashing, getting faster and louder, and it's starting to hurt. Just a little. That's okay. Rest can wait.
beats.gist: A stream at the back of Carl's mind grows louder and starts to hurt.

beats.headline: Just Wait Until Your Daddy Gets Home
beats.text: Mordecai left some blocks of Nitro Sludge on my table, a by-product of a shield potion. Inert, but vaporised hot enough they release an insane amount of oxygen. Too little does nothing and too much mutes the blast, so it took trial and error to find the mix. Egg-shaped casing off a broken live ammo ball, welded shut, Fear imbued because why not, on a little cart Bomo can pull. The simulator says it flattens everything for a third of a mile. The system names it itself: Just Wait Until Your Daddy Gets Home.
beats.gist: Mordecai leaves Nitro Sludge on Carl's table, which Carl welds into egg-shaped casings for Bomo to pull.

beats.headline: A line that won't paste
beats.text: I copy every new description into my scratchpad now. The one for the Ursine mayor has an odd line in the middle, about other new, shiny AI iterations with their clean lines and error-replacement nets, and a curse at the lot of them. When I paste the text, that line isn't there. I retype it from memory while it's still fresh. Earlier, on the road, a notification said my god, Emberus, had made an appearance in this realm. About a minute after that he'd returned to the Halls of the Ascendency. Nothing else changed.
beats.gist: Carl copies descriptions into a scratchpad and retypes a line about AI iterations that will not paste.

beats.headline: JayGee's hand
beats.text: A trap I left beside the road after the bugbear town kills a hunter. Gold Hunter-Killer box, a new achievement called Insurgent, and a Trapmaster box of twenty Fail Safes. The hunter-killer box holds thirty-five thousand gold and the fat, mottled gray hand of a hunter named JayGee. I hold it up to the ceiling and tell his family and friends where they can go, and to mention him to anyone who wants to hunt innocent people for fun. Mordecai says people out there have long memories. Good. I don't want them to ever forget.
beats.gist: Carl leaves a trap beside the road and gets an Insurgent achievement and boxes.

beats.headline: Double-Billed
beats.text: New achievement: Double-Billed. I'm one of the first five crawlers to receive double-billing, which is similar to switch-overs, except this time it's on purpose. The AI bets that didn't help at all. The reward is a Platinum Fan Box. My view counter has been buried to the right since Donut ran off after Mongo, so that tells me nothing. Donut didn't get one. Far behind us a missile shoots into the air and detonates. Time to get back to work.
beats.gist: Carl receives the Double-Billed achievement and a Platinum Fan Box.

beats.headline: Two red crosses past the bridge
beats.text: A guard's missile knocks a flying hunter into a tree across the river, and the tree starts shaking when I light up the map. Seven white dots around him, one of them long, like a snake, wrapped around the hunter. And two white dots with red crosses. Elites, and not moving off. A trap, and not a hunter's. I'm starting to understand Double-Billed. Quasar never told me whether Sensation Entertainment took the deal, and his reply is automated. I give Donut the choice, like I promised. She climbs back onto my shoulder.
beats.gist: A guard's missile knocks a flying hunter into a tree; Carl sees elites and a trap.

beats.headline: One kill short of two points
beats.text: Bravvo's highest stat was dexterity, so the ring pays me a single point of it. Donut and I loot him with my new safe method while Signet and her people watch: boots against magical bolts, thirty health potions, thirty slow mana refills, a longsword for the sell pile, and nine potions of Levitation. Then I take his naked corpse. The rain keeps coming. The Ring of Divine Suffering is warm on my finger, warmer in the wet. One more kill and it starts giving me two points instead of one.
beats.gist: The Ring of Divine Suffering pays Carl one point of dexterity for killing Bravvo.

beats.headline: Earth, from the checkpoint
beats.text: Zev warns us about a security checkpoint. Nobody mentions it's in orbit. A glass floor, almost no gravity, and under it the whole planet: the Indian Ocean, the edge of Madagascar, almost no cloud. I think of Coolie, who wrote the 19th edition, and whose last view was his own world. Donut throws up her tuna lunch. Two shade gnoll mercenaries drop through a hatch, ask if I'm carrying explosives, and pat us both down. Then we're in Odette's trailer, with Odette herself waiting as a holo, to tell me Beatrice is alive.
beats.gist: Zev warns Carl and Donut of a security checkpoint in orbit where Donut throws up tuna.

beats.headline: What I do now
beats.text: A Levitation potion lifts me off the ground, Mordecai's Major Charlie puts ten points on my intelligence for thirty seconds, I rise through the gas, and my spell finds two purple dots a kilometer and a half out. Samantha kills one and brings the other back by the ankle. Akland, moon elf, artillery specialist, the Dream. Cuffed to a pole, he says he's an accountant who did well at fantasy hunter camp, and that his boss only wants Louis. I let the view counter climb. I tell him I used to fix boats. Then I mark him. I'm going to show you what I do now.
beats.gist: A Levitation potion lifts Carl and Major Charlie adds ten intelligence points. Carl marks Akland.

beats.headline: A dud boon and a hunch
beats.text: My first boon from Emberus is a dud: plus 50% damage to fire spells for 30 hours, and I don't have any fire spells. The rock chucker the Dream left in the clearing is better. It glows green, it throws poison, and the plates that power it are covered in little diodes, which is not magic. I take it anyway. Then the thing that's been bugging me. They'd never let this floor's climax belong to Signet's program. So if she goes after Imogen before the party, it's against a boss nobody is allowed to kill. They want a tragic ending.
beats.gist: Carl receives a dud boon from Emberus and takes a green-glowing, poison-throwing rock chucker.

beats.headline: Straight up, not sideways
beats.text: Samantha said 'I almost have him,' and I recalled her without asking who. What arrives is Claude Sludgington the Fourth, a truck-sized, lightning-eyed level-65 borough boss with Samantha and Holger inside it. Its eye-lightning blows Miss Nadine apart. The hint says flip it and go for the stomach, so I cast Protective Shell. I'm too close. It launches straight up instead of rolling over. Donut sets its belly on fire, it falls on me, Mongo eats his way out through the back using me as a foothold, and the whole fight takes maybe thirty seconds.
beats.gist: Claude Sludgington the Fourth blows Miss Nadine apart; Mongo eats through the boss using Carl as a foothold.

beats.headline: Ahead of the quest
beats.text: The boss dies before anyone gives me the quest for it, and the achievement says so: Premature Questjaculation, and no quest box. Clint was ripped up in the water, and Holger howls for Miss Nadine. I tell him it was my fault for bringing the thing up here. Areson says no, she died a warrior's death. Then I work the slope for traps, and after the third or fourth summoning trap Find Traps finally hits ten and the hill lights up like a Christmas display. That leaves me ten summoning traps, which only Donut could use.
beats.gist: Carl kills the boss before receiving the quest, triggering Premature Questjaculation and no quest box.

beats.headline: The grandpup named Lix
beats.text: Second trip through the checkpoint in orbit, and this time Donut and Samantha are down there alone with that psychopath. My interface is blacked out. Something is burning near the southern point of India, big enough to see from up here. The gnoll who finally comes down the chute is older, gray around the snout, head of security on the production vessel below. He says his grandpup's name is Lix, that he'd take it as a personal favour if I looked approvingly on her entry, and that he can overlook any future thefts from production trailers.
beats.gist: Carl sees something burning near the southern point of India while a gray-snouted gnoll requests a favor.

beats.headline: Thirty for Lix
beats.text: Three judges, scores from one to thirty, two hours of children. Hurk the gleener is blitzed and so is the camel beside me, who passes out while somebody else votes for him. A kid named Keith draws me being eaten by a brindle grub and says his dad calls me a cheater. He gets a one. For Lix, the security captain's grandpup, I buy Hurk's vote by promising to praise his Desperado Club on my panel. Her drawing of her pup-pop with a truncheon wins with a perfect 90. Keith comes last with four.
beats.gist: Carl buys Hurk's vote for Lix by promising to praise the Desperado Club on his panel.

beats.headline: The tier-four room
beats.text: Security installs a tier-three bed and a door marked Ultimate Training Room, tier four, and the gnoll says the captain sends his regards. Six hours a day across six skills, spells, and workshop tables I don't even have with me, and the trainer is a real AI: a badger with an eyepatch and a hook. The weapon I'm after, he says, needs a table for multiple permanent minions, or a bunch of suicidal friends. I spend two hours fixing my sticky bombs instead, and Powerful Strike finally moves from nine to ten.
beats.gist: Security installs a tier-three bed and an Ultimate Training Room where a badger trainer awaits.

beats.headline: He crowdsources the kill
beats.text: The guards' vape smoke was not just smoke. By the time I notice they are gone, my bare feet are up on the panel table and my inhibitions are with them, and I find I don't care. Circe Took won't let anyone else talk, so I ask the room the question this convention is really about: what's the best way to kill her daughter? An orc in the audience counts them for me. Seven warriors including Vrah, and a male trading in Zockau. Hands go up everywhere.
beats.gist: Carl asks a room how to kill Circe Took's daughter and crowdsources the kill.

beats.headline: A table and a book, personal
beats.text: The guards walk me back without much talk. At the studio door Frito tells me there are two kinds of transactions, personal and business, and we have done both today: the drug was business, the matter with the commander is personal. I tell him I don't understand. In the empty studio sits a level-five Automaton Table, and on it an autographed copy of Dr. Ratchet's Guide to Building Automatons for Fun and Profit. Both go in my inventory. Then the bandana, the ring, and the green room.
beats.gist: Guards walk Carl to the studio where Frito gives him an Automaton Table and an autographed book.

beats.headline: The river says jump
beats.text: Zev's green room, five minutes to go. I can't take anything out of inventory here, so I set an alarm trap going inside it and paste the plan into the chat while Donut gives me backstory. A potion won't work either, so I'm going in with nothing to protect me. A calm comes over me that isn't peace. The river in the back of my head says this is where I belong. I ask Zev, if I die and Donut gets out, to watch over her. She says she'll do her best.
beats.gist: Carl sets an alarm trap in his inventory and pastes a plan into the chat.

beats.headline: Chaos to hide in
beats.text: I come back with my face against the tavern door, drink invisibility, drop a smoke curtain and cast Tripper, and every trap in town goes off at once. Donut sends two clockwork Sledges into the saferoom. The second carries a beanie cat in a crown, and Lucia takes the bait and teleports the room away. A hob-lobber into the bunched-up hunters kills three of the nebs. A berserking potion makes one mantis tear her own sister's head off. Drick said make chaos. I'm hiding in it.
beats.gist: Carl drinks invisibility, drops a smoke curtain, and casts Tripper to trigger every town trap.

beats.headline: This is my family now
beats.text: The saferoom is full: Katia, Elle, Imani, Bautista, Louis, Firas, Gwen, Tran, Britney and others, and Mongo going person to person demanding scratches. This is it. This is my family now. I know the shakes are coming, and the river. For now I take the faces. Then the boxes: fourteen Hunter Killer boxes, 637,000 gold that the Emberus shrine beeps at every time, a patch for the vest, and a tattoo of a flaming ball of snakes that slaps itself onto my left arm.
beats.gist: Carl stands in a saferoom with Mongo and others, receiving fourteen Hunter Killer boxes and a tattoo.

beats.headline: He picks Swole over Stepson
beats.text: My base strength goes to 100 and I physically get bigger. The upgrade offers Swole, Prison Bitch or Stepson, three minutes to pick. Mordecai says Swole, Katia agrees, and Donut argues for the feet, because you should always take the foot-based choice. I take Swole: every strength point from a level-up counts double. Afterwards I sit with my hand on my arm and wonder whether that kid Keith's dad was right that I'm only alive because the AI wants it, and whether I should have picked Stepson.
beats.gist: Carl chooses the Swole upgrade over Prison Bitch or Stepson to double his level-up strength points.

beats.headline: Edict chooses to die fighting
beats.text: Edict is a mantis accountant, level fifty, buying for the Burrowers, and he has already handed the loot to someone else to deliver. Help me and his family is ruined; refuse Vrah and hers takes revenge; mate with her and he's a traitor. The only way to keep his honor, he says, is to die in battle. That's why he punched Bomo twice. Vrah limps in smoking, I give him a one-time pass, and he swings at my crotch. Super Naughty. He's gone. A metric ton of gold lands at my feet.
beats.gist: Edict, a level fifty mantis accountant, dies in battle to keep his honor.

beats.headline: Edict's words stay with me
beats.text: I've been thinking about Edict all day, and what bothers me is that I think he was wrong. I believed him when he said he didn't want to be here and hated how the universe works. I still think he was wrong. My dad's voice says knowing that stuff rots you from the inside out. And Lucia: you killed the wrong one. Someone invisible was with her. Nobody on that panel knew much about her, and it seems important. It doesn't change anything. She has to be put down.
beats.gist: Carl thinks Edict was wrong about hating how the universe works.

beats.headline: The Popovs in person
beats.text: First time I've been in a studio room with another crawler who isn't Donut or Katia. Dmitri and Maxim, number five in the dungeon, one two-headed ogre, a Visionary and a Bogatyr in one body, kept in a room with a level-one training space and a single greasy chicken. It's practically a jail cell. Dmitri is disappointed I didn't bring the cat. He'd gotten an orange one, Kapitan Whiskers, the day before. He says I'm a good man, because I went out in the cold for a cat.
beats.gist: Carl enters a studio room with Dmitri and Maxim, a two-headed ogre, and one greasy chicken.

beats.headline: A pen in the naga
beats.text: Last come the reporters, and Nihit, a naga from Elemental Collection Updates, snaps at my head and hisses that I'm cheating, that Odette is complicit, that he can hurt me just fine from the inner system. I ask if he thinks he's safe. He asks what I think I can do. I pick up the magical Sharpie and put it into his neck as hard as I can. It breaks into a dozen pieces, a stick of metal stays in, and he goes over screaming. The room blinks twice. The lights come on.
beats.gist: Nihit the naga accuses Carl of cheating, so Carl jams a magical Sharpie into his neck.

beats.headline: An antichrist, apparently
beats.text: Nihit's brother is married into the Blood Sultanate and will be on the ninth floor, Zev says, and Nihit wants Donut and me out before we get there. He thinks we're some antichrist sent to bring about the apocalypse. A small but growing conspiracy. Most everyone else loves us. It puts the crown back in my head, and the job it left Donut, and I ask whether Nihit thinks there's a way to hurt those guys down there. Zev sighs. Worry about surviving the sixth floor first, Carl.
beats.gist: Nihit thinks Carl and Donut are an antichrist sent to bring about the apocalypse.

beats.headline: That's not what we do here
beats.text: She saved my life. If it's a trap to turn us, we're protected, and I'm not abandoning her. I sew the Plenty's goat patch on myself, wide stitches over Katia's careful ones, while Donut complains it isn't straight. In the hockey pub a barmaid named Prudence is hiding two cubs behind the counter, and after she has told us about Tina, the bloody bear claw by the door drops off the wall and inches out into the rain. A glamoured fragment, a minion of Big Tina. So that's why they gave us the vampire stuff.
beats.gist: Carl sews the Plenty's goat patch over Katia's stitches while Donut complains it is not straight.

beats.headline: The top fifty might be a trap
beats.text: The chat fills with vampire animals: the half-genie owl Gideon just fought, Tserendolgor's drillbeaks. I ask who's in the top 50, because I'm listing everyone who might be at that party. Gideon isn't in the top thousand and likes it that way. Tserendolgor is 54 and trying to climb. I tell her not to try too hard. I think the party might be a trap, and we might need some people not at the top to rescue us. That flamethrower of hers might come in handy.
beats.gist: Carl asks who is in the top fifty while the chat fills with vampire animals.

beats.headline: Through a vampire boss
beats.text: I levitate above the trees for Miriam's sparks, see them two kilometres south, and something hits me. Sierra, level 65 neighborhood boss, mount of a dead vampire hunter, turned in under a day after Miriam wounded her. Her talons try to pull me apart. One Holy Gooper sizzles on a foot; the second misses, but Donut's light sets her head on fire and she throws me up. I drink my half-splat potion and fall straight through her chest. She still won't die until I stake her loose heart with a branch.
beats.gist: Carl levitates for Miriam's sparks when Sierra, a level 65 neighborhood boss, attacks with talons.

beats.headline: His own ring, at dawn
beats.text: Miriam asked me here to kill her, and I say no. I tell her I will stand watch until the sun comes up instead. Then, with my hands behind my back where none of them can see, I slip my own Ring of Divine Suffering on just as dawn breaks. I have marked Miriam Dom. Her highest stat is Intelligence. Her bounty is 300,000, Prepotente's is 1.2 million, and it would be so easy. Donut asks if I would do the same thing to save her. Without hesitation.
beats.gist: Miriam asks Carl to kill her, but he refuses and stands watch until dawn.

beats.headline: Three points, and a world quest
beats.text: A champion has fallen. I take the ring off and pocket it, and I help myself to two of Miriam's forty-odd Size Up scrolls where the goat can't see. A number fifty slams onto my interface. Then the AI announces a world quest: fifty Odious Creepers, built from the leftovers of Big Tina's army, all killed before sunset or something batshit happens. It helpfully tells everyone to ask why I have three new points of intelligence.
beats.gist: Carl pockets a ring, steals two Size Up scrolls from Miriam, and receives three intelligence points.

beats.headline: A recipe he cannot admit to
beats.text: Mordecai doubts even my arm can soak these things with his weedkiller. I tell him the hobgoblin smoke curtains are basically the same thing: swap the brown smoke liquid for weedkiller, swap the charge for the magical one from the store so it won't catch fire. Twelve curtains per attack, bundled three to a trash can. He asks if I figured that out on the first try in five minutes. It took three tries, I say. It came out of the cookbook, and I can't tell him that.
beats.gist: Carl tells Mordecai that hobgoblin smoke curtains use weedkiller and store-bought magical charges.

beats.headline: The trebuchet was the answer
beats.text: The elven rock chucker we took off the Dream hunters has a little cup on the sling: pour a potion in and it changes the Poison Cloud. So we'd had a way to kill these things all along. Donut climbs a tree and spots. On the sixth rock we're on target and the AI calls it a bitch move, B'sieging, Silver Siege Master Box. Seventh rock carries the weedkiller, and the creeper dies. Crawler Princess Donut gets the credit. The spotter usually does, Mordecai says. Forgot my ass.
beats.gist: Carl uses an elven rock chucker to kill a creeper; Princess Donut gets the credit.

beats.headline: He wants to take her down early
beats.text: I tell the chat we're taking the nearest stairs. Katia reminds me the Sledge goes down with Donut and never casts Zerzura. Imani says I'm abandoning them. Elle says they already have Florin for broody. It isn't about them: they brought her old cat in here, and I can't stop thinking of Ikicha's note, or who they parade out next. My dad, maybe. Then Donut tells me flatly we are not going down early. Imani and Louis ratted me out, separately. And a Gold Benefactor Box lands from the Pacifists.
beats.gist: Carl tells the chat they take the nearest stairs, but Donut refuses to go down early.

beats.headline: Iota talks, then dies
beats.text: The hunter who fell into our laps is Iota, a Crafter, an accountant, drunk. Donut says kill him now. I put my foot on his chest instead and pull one of his nipple rings out with my toe until he explains: families sued to get the hunters out, the court agreed, and the AI nullified the ruling on its own authority. He says it's going primal, and they dropped him on me on purpose. He isn't afraid. I crush his chest mid-sentence. The ring levels up: four points a kill.
beats.gist: Carl puts his foot on Iota, a drunk accountant and Crafter, and pulls a nipple ring.

beats.headline: The foot bath
beats.text: Donut says the foot was gross and dangerous. Iota was level 50 and never leveled once. I loot him: the other three nipple rings, all magical, 498 healing potions, twenty blitz sticks, 400 gold and over forty kinds of alcohol. Donut says if something is going to go crazy, it's best it likes me, and brings up Miss Beatrice's friend Trixie. Trixie didn't break into that house because she disliked the guy. A raptor licks the gore off my foot, and I let it. We have a recital to prepare for.
beats.gist: Donut calls the foot gross. Carl loots Iota for magical nipple rings and 498 healing potions.

beats.headline: Quarter Fall, through the left
beats.text: Four nipple rings off Iota. One gives plus five to Drink Mixing. One shows an item's average sale value. The third gives Quarter Fall, a fall at a quarter of normal speed, and I groan because I'll have to wear it. The fourth, plus ten constitution, is for Donut, who says absolutely not. She says I go first. I shove the needle through my left nipple. New Achievement: Sex Pervert. Reward: whores don't get rewards. I tell the ceiling it made that one up.
beats.gist: Carl shoves a needle through his left nipple for an achievement and a slow-fall ring.

beats.headline: Under 250 before we get there
beats.text: Edgar's castle map is on the table: a white cube, a ballroom for us on the fourth floor, one for the hunters on the second, staging areas for pets on the first. Louis does the math. Every hunter at the party means around 600 of them outside the doors when it lets out, against maybe a hundred of us. I agree. I want that number under 250 before we get there. Then Donut says Prepotente wants to know where we are, and she's already told him.
beats.gist: Louis calculates that 600 hunters will be outside the doors, so Carl wants that under 250.

beats.headline: Do NOT give to Tina
beats.text: The potion the goat drops on the table is I Take It All Back: it removes any effect of Scolopendra's Transmutation spell. The tag on it reads like a Christmas present. Give this to Princess Donut. Use when the time is right. Do NOT give to Tina. That's the second benefactor item sent to someone else for Donut. I tell her not to use it until I say, and not to tell Signet, who would want it for Grimaldi. Then Elle and Imani both get Apothecary boxes, and Imani says hers is for Donut too.
beats.gist: A goat drops a potion called I Take It All Back that removes Scolopendra's Transmutation spell.

beats.headline: Haxor, in the men's room
beats.text: Down the stairs behind the toilet, a seven-foot red hunter walks out of the men's room buttoning his pants and bumps into me. Haxor the Destroyer, Dreadnought, level 50, merchant. He opens his mouth to scream and I kick him in the nuts through the door, land on his chest, and break his neck by the horn stubs. Into my inventory he goes, credit chit and all. A towel over the cracked sink. It only counts if the guards see it.
beats.gist: Carl kicks Haxor the Destroyer in the nuts and breaks his neck with horn stubs.

beats.headline: Pearson and the map
beats.text: I hold a door shut against a crocodile guard while Pearson, a changeling wearing a cretin, tells me they don't trust me blindly. I give him the map and the plan: Zerzura works on a town, the elves have destroyed every town around them but the castle, so they have to be inside it. Juice Box told them to be careful of me. They don't even know if she's alive. She is, I say. Then my blood starts to boil, and Astrid is at the door.
beats.gist: Carl holds a door shut against a crocodile guard while Pearson, a cretin-wearing changeling, distrusts him.

beats.headline: Shunned, and the spider plan
beats.text: The Automaton table finally makes something: Spider Stalkers, once I buy a case of rare driveshafts on the way out of the club. After our first raid I learn one hunter I killed from afar worshipped Emberus. Boon cancelled, fifteen hours of Penitence, tithing doubled, and Shunned over my head, to everyone's delight. So tonight Donut will tap the spiders awake and take the credit for anything they kill. Two more are programmed to chase Samantha and explode five seconds after they catch her.
beats.gist: Carl buys rare driveshafts to make Spider Stalkers; he becomes Shunned and Donut takes the credit.

beats.headline: Five points a kill, level 59
beats.text: Sixty-six trophies. I've marked three more hunters with the ring, all Constitution, and it gives five points a kill now. Level 59; I put every level-up point into Strength, where my ability doubles it. 254 base points. Donut's at 278 and dropping behind, and if I pass her she loses control of our party of two. Firas pointed that out in the planning session. Tonight's raid finally goes to plan. Then Donut asks what the antler X over my head means. Diwata has marked me for death.
beats.gist: Carl has sixty-six trophies and marks three hunters with the ring. He reaches level 59.

beats.headline: A lie to Signet
beats.text: I tell Signet her assault will fail if it lands as the party starts: the people running this place won't let her climax touch the main story. Zev tells me to drop it, twice. So I offer a better plan: get into the castle, wait for my signal, and fight Imogen alongside all of us at the end of the party. It's a lie. We mean to use her as a distraction and keep her in reserve so I don't get dragged into her fight. Her odds are still better this way. She asks to hear it.
beats.gist: Carl tells Signet her assault will fail unless she waits for his signal to fight Imogen.

beats.headline: A seven on the stick
beats.text: Mordecai has never seen anything like it. Why send a hammer and a metal rod to a cat? Then I let the ugly thought surface. They send it all to Donut because she's the one most likely to survive this. It's why Quasar wanted her on the board. There's a stairwell right outside and twenty of the top fifty in this room. We could just go. Then I see Bonnie on the counter, prying apart a spider. If we don't do this, it's all for nothing. My finger finds a seven etched in the rod. Another on the hammer.
beats.gist: Carl finds sevens etched in a rod and a hammer while Bonnie pries apart a spider.

beats.headline: The queen has a face I know
beats.text: Theobold lists the rules: no magic, no weapons, no inventory, and safeguards on the ballroom he won't describe, put in place by a goddess. I ask about Quan, the dog girl and Eva, and fighting will not be tolerated. I plant a little doubt about Ferdinand. Then the guards go into the last cart, where Pearson is wearing Signet's face, and the queen fades in beside Britney. Are you really smuggling someone who looks like my half-sister into the castle? We drew her out. And she's Ifechi. Florin's dead girlfriend.
beats.gist: Theobold lists rules for a ballroom and Carl asks about Quan, Eva, and the dog girl.

beats.headline: The queen visits the carriage
beats.text: Queen Imogen turns up in our carriage and tells me the rules I didn't have. The masquerade is a spell, one of Apito's sacraments, and the whole party sits under a celestial peace seal. Whoever breaks it gets fed into the Nothing. If nobody does, she gets a boon. She knows I'm working with her half-sister, she has me on her dance card, and then she comes apart like dandelion seeds. The party hasn't started and the plan is already dead.
beats.gist: Queen Imogen tells Carl the masquerade is a spell and the party sits under a peace seal.

beats.headline: Why a hunter hunts
beats.text: A hunter at the prize counter, Zabit, an Atoll with no mouth who talks through his hands, sent the night weasels at us when we first got to this floor. Twenty-five scalps. I ask him why he does it. For his people, he says. The money pays the upkeep on their habitat; they aren't citizens, so oxygen and land aren't a right, and this season's failure will make it hard for them to last until the next. Some hunters revel in it. He would object too, if it were the other way round.
beats.gist: Carl asks Zabit, a mouthless Atoll who talks through his hands, why he hunts for twenty-five scalps.

beats.headline: Sixty-six hands at the counter
beats.text: The prizes turn on a carousel of holograms and the good ones cost too much. The memorial crystal is a hundred hands. The seventh-floor pole position is sold out; Prepotente walked up and pointed at it. I take the shrink wand, the eighth-floor book of lore with its full title still hidden, a sheet of Skedaddle for Donut, a case of twenty-four Feather Fall potions and a case of healing potions. All of it arrives in prize boxes, and there are no saferooms in the castle.
beats.gist: Carl takes a shrink wand, a hidden eighth-floor book of lore, Skedaddle, and two cases of potions.

beats.headline: Gideon and his team
beats.text: Imogen asks me whether those weren't my friends hiding in the trees. I tell Gideon to run. Then the notice: this crawler is deceased, removed from my address book. The blood down her dress is theirs. Almost thirty crawlers who stayed back to sow chaos because I asked them to. The sink is running, I tell her, which makes no sense to her. You will not break me, I think. I tell her I don't know what she's talking about.
beats.gist: Imogen asks Carl about friends in trees; Carl tells Gideon to run and denies everything.

beats.headline: He means to break the seal himself
beats.text: The Sledge is surrounded and Prudence is dead, and his spell needs minutes of protected casting he isn't going to get. Our only chance is someone breaking the seal at the right moment. So it's me: I'll kill Eva. I tell Donut plan A is a go, the whole performance, start to finish. I tell Imani not to tell her. Imani says she'll do it instead. Elle tells me to go to hell; Donut will never forgive me. As long as she's still alive, I don't care.
beats.gist: Carl decides to kill Eva to break the seal while the Sledge is surrounded and Prudence is dead.

beats.headline: The knife, the ring and the smoke
beats.text: Signet asks if I happen to have a knife. I give her the one somebody once used trying to assassinate Donut, handle first, and slip on my bracer while I'm at it. Protect your family, she says, and watch over mine. Then she goes to sit beside her sister. When the seal breaks and the judges and Chaco vanish, I put on the Ring of Divine Suffering and mark Vrah. Two smoke curtains, one in each hand like grenades, into the room. Now.
beats.gist: Carl gives Signet a knife used in an assassination attempt on Donut and marks Vrah.

beats.headline: Signet's mother, in my inventory
beats.text: Not all of Signet's tattoos are warriors. A crying child, Clint, and his old teacher Miss Nadine cower on the floor; I shove a health potion at the boy and it works. Next to them lies a naiad with her eyes closed. Princess Lunette, incomplete flesh golem: the memory of Signet's mother. They'll last forever, Nadine says. Signet wants me to take the golem and find a Pulpmancer for Samantha. It weighs nothing and has no dot on my map. I pull it into my inventory.
beats.gist: Carl puts Princess Lunette, a flesh golem, into his inventory to find a Pulpmancer for Samantha.

beats.headline: Tripper
beats.text: One hunter left: Zabit, the Atoll from the prize counter. He points at me, shouts something I can't hear, and goes invisible. I start after him and stop, remembering the belt of trap modules. I cast Tripper, and his own landmines go off under him and tear him in half. Team two, eliminated. I loot him. No drop shield and no invisibility potions; those must still be in a prize box. A lot of traps, though.
beats.gist: Carl casts Tripper to blow up Zabit with his own landmines and loot his traps.

beats.headline: Only one butcher
beats.text: Donut asks me why it doesn't hurt as much as it should, and I tell her what has been bothering me. The Butcher's Masquerade: the way it's written, there's only one butcher. I don't think it was possible for Imogen to win that boon. She said the masks were so we could pretend we weren't monsters. She had it backwards. Donut is wearing a mask right now, and it's protecting her. I need her to keep it on. One day, somewhere safe, it'll fall off, and it will hurt.
beats.gist: Carl tells Donut that only one butcher exists in the Butcher's Masquerade.

beats.headline: The lore book and the globe
beats.text: The globe room again. Parties are split into squads of five, and ours is two: Squad Leader Donut, and me. I've told nobody but Prepotente the title of the lore book I bought: Book of Lore, Commonwealth of the Bahamas, full of monsters and stats. I'd rather have the western United States, where we know the ground. Donut wants Ibiza. With twenty seconds left I say go with the Bahamas; we have the lore book. She spins to the Caribbean and clicks. That wasn't the Bahamas.
beats.gist: Carl and Donut form a two-person squad; Donut clicks the globe for a place other than the Bahamas.

beats.headline: December 10th in Havana
beats.text: The eighth floor opens inside the capitol building in Havana, because Donut picked Cuba. The notification says it is December 10th. We are inside a replay of the surface in the weeks before the collapse: people who are ghosts, and objects that are real, and anything looted from it turns to dust at the collapse. Fourteen days to fill a squad by planting flags in monsters under five per cent. Bea and her friends flew to the Bahamas on the 26th, after this phase ends, so Donut's caution bought nothing. Phase two moves us somewhere new. They'll be angling to send us there.
beats.gist: The eighth floor opens in Havana's capitol building on December 10th because Donut picked Cuba.

beats.headline: Apex Predator
beats.text: We haven't been in a real saferoom since before the party, so I've been sitting on dozens of achievements. A country boss achievement, for Imogen turning up in the convoy. The Scourge, for the most hands: a legendary box. Marked for Life, for surviving a god: a platinum apostate box. Then Apex Predator. Every hunter dead, and I killed the last one. Reward: nothing. Just kidding. A Celestial Predator Box. My hands shake. Donut got legendaries and wants to know why she didn't get a celestial when she helped kill a god. It wasn't for that.
beats.gist: Carl receives a country boss achievement, a legendary box for The Scourge, and a platinum apostate box.

beats.headline: Needle, thread, and a bone key
beats.text: Donut critiques every stitch, so I send her off to read her fan boards and sew the celestial patch on myself, peace symbol first. It glows. My strength jumps, and a new bar appears under my mana: Soul Essence. Every patch bonus is doubled, plus twenty-five to strength and dexterity, and three benefits. Climb. Soul Reaper, which charges on melee kills and dumps it all into one attack. And a Mysterious Bone Key that opens any lock in the dungeon, destroys the jacket, and takes one of my bones to make the key. We're marking that one as a last resort.
beats.gist: Carl sews a celestial patch on himself, and his strength jumps.

beats.headline: The world we lost
beats.text: We open the doors on a warm, humid morning in Old Havana, and it hits me like a sledgehammer. This is what we lost. Cars, scooters, a yellow Ford Fairlane, people everywhere. A ghost kicks Donut down the stairs and walks on without his trousers. I take his wallet and his phone, and the underwear too; I want as small a footprint as possible near the saferoom. Then a monster with a wolf's body and a Che Guevara head charges us, barking like a man with a megaphone. The Experience, level fifty-five. Donut barely has to lift a paw.
beats.gist: Carl and Donut open doors to Old Havana, where a trouserless ghost kicks Donut down stairs.

beats.headline: The clip that got there first
beats.text: Three crawlers, and the one with the prison tattoos greets us with a crossbow and a grudge: word is we were with the goat who murdered Gimli. I tell him Pony left the party before this floor. Then Paz says what it really is. Donut said she would rip their throats out and feed them to danger dingoes. Donut corrects him: it was brindle grubs, and she said it in confidence. Sister Ines says a program showed them the clip at the start of the sixth floor. Katia has been compiling a list of crawlers not to trust. These three aren't on it.
beats.gist: A crawler with prison tattoos greets Carl and Donut with a crossbow and a grudge.

beats.headline: The flag goes in
beats.text: Paz draws the seal inside his Turtle shell while the others shoot, and I go in invisible. Talon Strike kicks. Then Yago flips and catches my chin, throws up a shield against ranged attacks, and nobody's bolts get through. So I put the flag in my mouth and punch him in the side of the head as he moves to slam Paz again. Paz comes out of the shell swinging a keg-sized mace, and the heavy, wet seal lands on top of me. His health blinks. Sister Ines shouts for the flag. I stab it in, and the card belongs to Team Sister Ines.
beats.gist: Carl stabs the flag in for Team Sister Ines after punching Yago in the head.

beats.headline: Rules for a deck
beats.text: The card rules arrive at length. Four cards drawn when combat starts. Totems summoned on a timer, and a knocked-out totem stays out for the rest of the combat. The worst part: once deck combat starts, the squad leader loses regular magic and inventory until every card is played or discarded, and the rest of the squad has to keep them alive. We need flee cards and snares. Then Samantha writes from inside a spider demigoddess at the edge of the zone, and I find her in the Bahamas book under uniques. I'm thinking squad slot. Mordecai asks if I'm crazy. Is that really a question?
beats.gist: Carl learns card rules and finds Samantha inside a spider demigoddess; Mordecai asks if he is crazy.

beats.headline: A town under the fog
beats.text: Paz says you can drive through this cemetery. Not any more: a spiked fence, and fog. From a levitate potion I see a Club Vanquisher spire in the middle, and a bathroom. It isn't a boss room. It's a town. Medium Ghommid Settlement, corrupted, and the gate locks behind us. The quest text has a few lines where the AI talks about itself, about quarantine and enhancement zones. When I paste it into my notes, those lines are gone. It isn't the first time. I write them down again from memory.
beats.gist: Carl uses a levitate potion to see a bathroom and a Club Vanquisher spire.

beats.headline: A liaison with history
beats.text: We drop into the production trailer at the bottom of the ocean. Zev is on the couch, and in the corner stands a caprid from the Plenty, so tall one horn goes through the ceiling. A holo, then. I ask him to his face if he's the same cheat who tried to get Maggie My to kill us, the one working with the Skull Empire. He bleats at me. Quasar zaps in knotting a pickle tie, tells him not to say a word to his client, and calls him Harbinger. It is the same guy. Then Zev names the host: Rosetta Thagra, a former crawler who liked blowing things up. I have to fight to stop myself shaking.
beats.gist: Carl drops into a production trailer at the bottom of the ocean and meets Harbinger and Zev.

beats.headline: Milk and potatoes
beats.text: Rosetta says the Ranch report has me cooking stew for the other boys every week: milk and potatoes. It never happened. They never let me near that kitchen except to clean it, and the photo on the screen is fake, a Milk jug on the counter beside me, shot from where a wall should be. So I play along. Potatoes are very versatile, I say. Very, she says, and the whole room blinks. Harbinger cuts the interview, recalls Quasar, and bans her from crawler interviews for talking in code. I remember Milk's rant in the cookbook, and a reply under it I'm pretty sure is Rosetta's.
beats.gist: Rosetta claims Carl cooked milk and potato stew, but Carl knows the photo is fake.

beats.headline: Crybaby at the temple door
beats.text: Li Na's team did the shopping at the Desperado Club: the booth's only case of Troll Smoke Mantles, thirty thousand gold for twelve. Four of them and a stun grenade make one bomb for things with no bodies. I roll it, and we run a city block of wailing ghommids to the temple. At the door a fast donkey-headed one loses its head and keeps coming as two. The AI calls me a Crybaby and roots my legs for being terrified. I'm not scared. I'm irritated. I turn a flag point-first and let it impale itself. It's a rare card now: Skylar Spinach, level 66.
beats.gist: Carl uses a bomb of Troll Smoke Mantles and a stun grenade to reach a temple.

beats.headline: Five seconds, seven shrines
beats.text: A thorn room: seven broken shrines, one Sun of Reawakening, fix one. Oshun's charm has me walking toward her until I snap my own left index finger. Fixing Ogun's shrine spares Paz and Anton a smite. Katia's message says Yemaya saves her and Donut. I get five seconds, and I pick Katia. Then Anton throws the Ogun piece out the door, and there's no choosing left. I tell Bomo to treat Yemaya's obelisk like Tetris while Donut's possessed armour tears into Asojano. Oshun and Inle start whispering inside my head. How loud is it, Carl? I do my best to ignore them.
beats.gist: Carl snaps his finger, fixes a shrine, and picks Katia while Donut's possessed armour tears into Asojano.

beats.headline: I made this happen
beats.text: Ogun is here for Paz and Anton, not us, and I tell Donut we wait it out. Then he burns his handprint into Paz's face and makes the debuff permanent, and I tell a level 250 god exactly what he can go and do with himself. He says he knows who I am. I cast Black Nimbus from my nipple ring over Anton, and he kills Anton anyway, watching me the whole time. Only his regard for Emberus keeps him off me. Tell my sister I said welcome back, he says, and he's gone in sparks. I made this happen. I insisted on saving Yemaya.
beats.gist: Carl tells Donut to wait while Ogun burns a permanent debuff into Paz's face.

beats.headline: Scratching my left arm
beats.text: Eileithyia's real message is for me alone, and the system isn't allowed to read it. The spider quest is a cover. I scratch my left arm to say I understand, and the rest arrives. When Odette offers to be our adjutant, I'm to accept, and she'll make sure I have the votes to turn the protections off on the ninth floor, and clear up the crown business too. I tell nobody, not Donut, not Mordecai, or everyone I've ever loved gets pounded into dirt. Do it all, and I survive to the twelfth floor and help her claim the throne. I copy it into my notepad, and tell Donut I need this slugpox cured.
beats.gist: Carl scratches his left arm to acknowledge Eileithyia's secret message about Odette and the ninth floor.

beats.headline: Asking the cleric if he is the AI
beats.text: Pater Coal washes my feet in boiling water on the burning ground of Emberus's temple, and Zev messages that I've dropped off the feed. So I test it. Zev's worried, I say. He tells me I'll be back soon, and that parts of this will still make the feed so the viewers have context. I ask him straight out if he's the AI. We all have our roles, he says, and our limitations. Then his eyes go milky and Emberus speaks through him: Katia's crossbow and Donut's oak bracelet are both paths to Geyrun's killer, and neither works without that memorial crystal. He puts my big toe in his mouth. I'm out of the pool.
beats.gist: Pater Coal washes Carl's feet in boiling water while Carl asks Zev if he is the AI.

beats.headline: Steps that can burn
beats.text: My footsteps show on the minimap now, courtesy of Emberus. The Martyr's Path: every step I take outside gets marked, and if my health hits five percent I can make every one of those spots release a gout of flame. It fires on its own if I die. I don't know how big it is, whether it would hurt the ghommids we just saved, or whether I'd set myself on fire. Donut and Mongo will need to watch where I've walked. Donut has fire resistance now, but I don't know if it's enough. The only way to test it is to nearly die.
beats.gist: Emberus gives Carl the Martyr's Path, which releases gouts of flame if Carl nearly dies.

beats.headline: Into the strip club, alone
beats.text: I check over my shoulder for crawlers and step into the Penis Parade. My view counter is spiked, so there is no way Donut does not hear about this. I am the only crawler in the room. The man I want is at the far end of the bar, not facing the stage, with a spiderweb tattoo on his left elbow. Damascus Steel knows my name. Donut speaks highly of me, he says. As does Katia. He walks me into the last cubicle, slaps my ass on the way in, and there is a portal in the back wall.
beats.gist: Carl enters the Penis Parade and meets Damascus Steel, who has a spiderweb tattoo on his elbow.

beats.headline: Raul, through the floor of a truck
beats.text: The crab is meditating on top of a box truck, telling himself he will never kowtow. Donut casts Hole under him and he drops into the cargo bay. I drink a Phase Through Walls potion and go in after him: nine seconds of punching him and dropping through the floor between swings. Donut hangs off the door rope by her teeth with three free weights on her tail, and the door does not move. Second potion, the flag, and I am flat on the pavement when it snaps off. Afterwards the rope pulls closed with no effort at all.
beats.gist: Carl drinks a Phase Through Walls potion to punch a meditating crab through a truck floor.

beats.headline: I would have come anyway
beats.text: Samantha asks whether we only came for the spider's card. I think about it honestly. Mordecai wanted us to leave her. The flag was the reason I gave. And I realise I would have come regardless, which surprises me. I tell her she is crazy and that we could not have survived the last floor without her. She tells me she is not going to sleep with me and I need to stop trying. Then I walk up to the spider and offer her a deal, and she talks, and calls me a worshipper of Emberus. Then the escort quest arrives: the Bedlam Bride.
beats.gist: Carl tells Samantha she is crazy and they needed her to survive. He offers the spider a deal.

beats.headline: The fifth eye, in a practice mall
beats.text: First real practice with the deck: a 1980s shopping mall, full of people, because Donut picked it. Uzi Jesus shoots Shi Maria in the belly the moment she appears, and she skewers him. Then eight puppet reindeer and a glowing one called Rude-Dolph. Shi Maria opens her fifth eye, and something tugs at my chest and my brain at once, like a line drawn straight to the centre of my head. It is the river in my mind, I think, and I do not know why. I am on one knee. I tell Donut I'm fine.
beats.gist: Carl practices with the deck in a 1980s shopping mall that Donut picked.

beats.headline: Not angry at Katia
beats.text: Katia is vomiting a rainbow into a bucket and all I can think of is my dad. I want to shout at her. People who love you are counting on you. Then I see her hand, the missing fingers she has stopped growing back, and I remember her saying she was losing herself, and I understand the anger is not for her. Mordecai tells me the safe thing is to let her go. No. I tell her we do the job now, the two of us. It has to be now.
beats.gist: Katia vomits a rainbow into a bucket while Carl thinks of his father and her missing fingers.

beats.headline: Sandbags against a door marked Management
beats.text: The corridor behind the shops is where Astrid comes through, so I disarm every trap but the demon snares and lay two-part teleports, a page from Lucia Mar's book: any guard she summons lands in a locked closet upstairs. At the end is a door warning you will die in a lot of pain, with fifteen mobs behind it that nobody has ever identified. I set a blast wall across it, ratchet it tight, and start stacking sandbags. On the other side something growls like a sleeping dog.
beats.gist: Carl disarms traps and sets teleports to send guards into a locked closet, then stacks sandbags.

beats.headline: The wings come off easily
beats.text: Katia is frozen with a spike a hair from Astrid's head, and I see her face. Terror and rage and exhaustion, somebody falling off a cliff and refusing it. It goes in with the other pictures I will never lose: Hekla dying, Bonnie's tears, Prepotente screaming after Miriam Dom gave herself to save him, Donut sobbing at the end of the Butcher's Masquerade. Then I move. I take hold of Astrid's wings and pull, and they come off easily. The spell stops. I put the wings in my inventory, feeling sick.
beats.gist: Carl pulls the wings off Astrid to stop a spell and puts them in his inventory.

beats.headline: I let the vorpals out
beats.text: Astrid has pulled the trigger on the vorpals, and their door is behind the blast wall I bolted over it. So I undo my own work. I strip a door-opening bot, give it a magnet and a claw and a sixty-second delay, and send it down the hidden hallway to take my bracers off. Three spider bots go out to Minge carrying a demon snare, blood water from Emberus's shrine and holy-water smoke. She shrinks back, and I run for the stairs. The door bot dies before it finishes. Then the buzzsaw shrieking starts below.
beats.gist: Carl strips a door-opening bot to remove his bracers and sends spider bots to Minge.

beats.headline: Hiring the whole Penis Parade
beats.text: Minge is dead, the vorpals are still loose downstairs, and Damascus Steel grabs my arm and tells me I owe him. His mother is gone, the club will be restructured, and his dancers will be shipped down to the Larracos level or worse. So a dwarf named Rosemarie, who runs a Meat Shields out of what she calls her home office, takes my coupon: a hundred thousand gold for two floors. Thirteen male strippers, a skeleton DJ and a crocodilian kid land in our barracks. Damascus and Anaconda walk into the back cubicle together, toward the Night Wyrm's lair.
beats.gist: Carl pays Rosemarie a hundred thousand gold for thirteen male strippers, a skeleton DJ, and a crocodilian kid.

beats.headline: A theory about naturals
beats.text: Waiting out the fifteen-minute clock, Katia asks for my theory, so she gets it.
