The Night Wyrm, Astrid, Damascus and Anaconda are a family, stuck in here a very long time, and not generated NPCs. More like the bopcas. Indentured, maybe, each wearing a different race. Astrid made assistant manager and parked her sons at the Parade where she could watch them. And the Night Wyrm had us kill her, I think over money. Mordecai once said it was illegal to change the memories of naturals. I am fairly sure he added: unless they signed away their rights.
beats.gist: Carl tells Katia his theory that the Night Wyrm, Astrid, Damascus and Anaconda are indentured naturals.

beats.headline: They should be thanking me
beats.text: Five teams have filed complaints that blowing up the club and forcing the mass exit counts as an attack. On Odette's couch I tell the galaxy those guys sat in the bottom of the Desperado for weeks, drinking and gambling away their citizens' money, when they could have died and been regenerated out any time. Now they get to play. They should thank me. Before the interview Harbinger warned he would stop it if we gave anything privileged away. If he does, Odette never asks about the adjutant, and the deal to save Katia is void. Only I know that part.
beats.gist: Carl tells the galaxy that five teams should thank him for blowing up the Desperado club.

beats.headline: The interview was a press conference
beats.text: Odette will not be our adjutant. She has sponsored a deity and is stepping into the dungeon herself, and I keep my face still while the crowd goes nuts. She knew. She knew Huanxin was planning something and was never going to let her have the upper hand, so she goes in on an equal footing instead. This whole adjutant business was never about us. It was a press conference. I hope to God it is enough for Huanxin, that she sees I had no control over this, and that she still saves Katia.
beats.gist: Odette sponsors a deity and enters the dungeon instead of becoming an adjutant to oppose Huanxin.

beats.headline: There is no we
beats.text: Zev blinks out to an all-hands, a spy probe has been shot out of orbit, and Odette has fifteen minutes off the record. I tell her she screwed us by not taking the chair. She asks if she should have let me set her up to be assassinated. Huanxin will want Katia more than ever, she says; make Katia eat the orchid soon, force her hand, and we must be delicate with her. That is where I lose it. There is no we. Every corner we turn, somebody new is waiting to use us, and she is always involved. What about you, Odette?
beats.gist: Zev blinks out, a spy probe is shot out of orbit, and Carl tells Odette she screwed them.

beats.headline: Iowa, stacked on a reef
beats.text: Donut's Torch goes up like a stadium light and shows me what is west of us: a sheer wall of crumbling earth, taller than I can see, wider than the island, dirt already sliding off into the sea. The key is on top of it. I tell Zev this is a cay, an island built on a reef, and that pile will be washed away in a day. Zev says they are aware. The first opponent of our own is a Babababoon in a Santa hat, standing frozen in the light of a parking lot. One sticky hob-lobber. Token number two.
beats.gist: Donut's Torch reveals a wall of crumbling earth on a cay where the key sits.

beats.headline: You will not break me
beats.text: Somebody on Donut's feed says they will drop it if she keeps being so whiny. I turn the screen off before she sees it, light her candle, and we take an old-fashioned nap in the chair. She sleeps. I cannot. I think of Mordecai at his table and the baggage he carries, heavier each year. Odette and her guilt. Frank Q, the Ring of Divine Suffering, and how crushed he said he felt. Just like Donut. Just like me. I think of the climb, and the man I know I will find up there. You will not break me.
beats.gist: Carl turns off Donut's screen, lights her candle, and they nap in the chair.

beats.headline: Two rules, broken at once
beats.text: The moment combat starts I get a warning: my equipped cloak has aggravated the Nightgaunt. I throw a quarter hob-lobber at invisible monsters on a roof in an unstable environment, breaking both of our rules at once, and a truck slides off the mountain. The demon never plays a card. It only wants me, or my cloak. Mordecai warned me it would; he did not say how much. Token seven. Walking to the barn afterward, my arms are shaking, and I hold my left hand with my right and pretend they are not.
beats.gist: Carl throws a quarter hob-lobber at invisible monsters, breaking two rules and sliding a truck off a mountain.

beats.headline: They starve us
beats.text: Sharp-Elbows rolls into me like a truck, and her spikes go through my arms, stomach, legs, neck and both of my eyes. I am blind, drinking potions, her rotted teeth against mine. She whispers. They starve us. When we are not here, we are there, and there they make certain the hunger festers. You can stop it. You can satiate us all, Carl. Then Raul snaps her staff, a Heal gives me my sight back, and her eyes are right there, pleading, sad, afraid. I have seen those eyes before. Raul takes her head.
beats.gist: Sharp-Elbows spikes Carl's arms, stomach, legs, neck, and eyes; Raul snaps her staff and takes her head.

beats.headline: Say hi to dad
beats.text: I wake from the river and the ogre's eyes, and Donut is talking too fast and too stiff, offering to fight the keyholder alone. Then she tells me why. The motorcycle. She saw how it hit me when it came around on the prize carousel, and she knows who is in that trailer. I remind her of Ferdinand, how badly I wanted to skip the Masquerade, and that if we had, even more people would have died. And don't try to be like me, I tell her. You need to be like you. Let's go say hi to dad.
beats.gist: Carl wakes from the river and the ogre's eyes; Donut offers to fight the keyholder alone.

beats.headline: A yard from last summer
beats.text: The vending machine wants nine tokens for one fight, and it carries his silhouette. His Harley is in the yard, a 1965 Electra Glide Panhead with expired Georgia plates, the thing he never shut up about. Everything up here was under snow this morning, but this yard has weeds and flowers and dust, and a kid's bike cut in half at the property line. It is spliced in from another time. Summer, maybe. They want me to see something. I pick up the motorcycle, and it does not go into the temporary items. It is mine.
beats.gist: A vending machine sells a fight for nine tokens and shows Carl's silhouette.

beats.headline: Asher
beats.text: He is in a hospital bed in the living room, maybe a hundred and forty pounds, yellow, cursing a Mariners game. Twelve years, and it looks like forty. Then a boy looks around the hallway corner. Six, maybe. That nose, those eyes, that hair. The boy wants the TV; my father wants his cigarettes, and yells after him to get back here, you little shit. Asher. His name is Asher. On the curio there is a photo of him on my father's lap, one year old. I have a brother.
beats.gist: Carl remembers his brother Asher, who is six years old and looks like Carl's father.

beats.headline: Exactly what I needed to see
beats.text: My stepmother has been hiding morphine in the flowerpots. I lean in closer to him than I have ever been and tell him he is a bully, that two women tried to kill him, that nobody will care. I will not watch him die. In Ash's room I tell the boy he will not be forgotten, and my hand goes through his head. I take the gun, the keys, and a Centipede cabinet, light the allium curtains, and tell the ceiling that if they meant to hurt me, this was exactly what I needed to see.
beats.gist: Carl finds morphine in flowerpots, burns allium curtains, and takes a Centipede cabinet.

beats.headline: Nine heads, most of them known
beats.text: The heads are labelled. Tami-Lynn, my stepmother. Monobrow Sam. Bea's mother. My boss Dick, my landlord Mr. Roth, Sally who did billing, a Persian called Sugar Cube, Judge Lucian holding the cards, and the youngest, Asher. Asher's mouth fires lightning at me. Mordecai says find the fire head, cut it clean, cauterize. It is Bea's mother. I lock a snap collar round her neck, hit it with the shrink wand, and the head flies off. Then I smash a moonshine jug on the wound, and the fire splashes back onto my chest.
beats.gist: Carl identifies labeled heads, including Tami-Lynn and Monobrow Sam, before Asher fires lightning at him.

beats.headline: The last head
beats.text: Alpha Male Carl, a totem wearing my face and my father's voice, puts his bare foot on my chest and tells me a good son would have stayed by his father's side. Mongo hits him from behind. The hydra is burning down to one conscious head, my stepmother's, and she meets my eyes. She says she does not regret it. She saw what happened to me and did not want Ash to go through the same thing, so she made sure it was done right. Judge Lucian dies. The body breaks open like a bag of spaghetti.
beats.gist: Alpha Male Carl puts a bare foot on Carl's chest, then Mongo hits him.

beats.headline: A brother Bea never mentioned
beats.text: Donut knew every head on that hydra except my stepmother. The boy was Asher; Bea kept his picture on her phone and talked about him with her mother. He was my half-brother, and I learned he existed today. Donut also tells me Bea ran my Facebook on my Megatron12 password, and got a coworker fired for asking me out. Tami-Lynn probably wrote to me there. Bea saw it and never said. Until now I was never angry at her.
beats.gist: Carl learns he has a half-brother named Asher and that Bea managed his Facebook account.

beats.headline: A drawing on the wall
beats.text: My room has always been bare, and tonight that bothers me. A fern from the trailer goes on the table. One of Asher's crayon airplanes goes on the wall with duct tape. The Centipede cabinet goes in the corner and lights up. Then boxes. The platinum one is a skill potion, Find Crawler at level five, and I drink it without asking questions. The patch is a burning book: Intelligence, and once a day I can make an opponent forget a spell.
beats.gist: Carl puts a trailer fern on the table and duct tapes Asher's crayon airplanes to the wall.

beats.headline: A guard dog on Christmas
beats.text: I ride north past midnight on my father's motorcycle and stop at a closed gas station for a map and some jerky. Last Christmas I played video games with Donut on my lap and never once felt lonely. Now I'm alone, and I finally understand the difference. There's a memory-ghost bloodhound asleep in the back, Lightning Lou, left with two bowls of food to guard an empty building. My hand goes through his head. Merry Christmas, buddy.
beats.gist: Carl rides his father's motorcycle north past midnight and stops at a closed gas station.

beats.headline: Written in Syndicate Standard
beats.text: The shelter is dark, and my map and my spells find nothing. On the second walk around, among the gang squiggles and the penises, I find three sentences in runny red spray paint: look for me at breakfast every morning, I wear the red hat with the flaps, coffee then speech. It's Syndicate Standard, not English, and it's been there a long time. I kick in the glass door and wait among the sleeping memory ghosts, and fall asleep. At six the men get up, and one of them wears a red trapper hat.
beats.gist: Carl finds red spray paint in Syndicate Standard among penises and gang squiggles in a dark shelter.

beats.headline: Paulie, whose real name is Goff
beats.text: He isn't talking to me; it's a memory, a speech he gives every morning in case a crawler is standing here. Biologically he's gondii, living in a man named Paulie. Several thousand of his kind are waiting on Earth to pass their knowledge to the new AI, and the mudskippers call them Residuals. Monsters won't touch them until they hand it over. There's a war among his kind, he says. Let me tell you how to shut off the... And the world flashes.
beats.gist: Carl hears a memory of a speech from Goff, a gondii living in a man named Paulie.

beats.headline: A plan that costs a bone
beats.text: If Imani doesn't get a key, I make her fight us and Donut plays our Flee card, and the key is hers. I still have the jacket with the bone key benefit, so we can open the door anyway. I'll lose the jacket and one bone. Maybe not an important one. Donut says they're all important. We'll all still be alive. When she asks whether we're going to fight people we like, I tell her the truth: we'll do what we have to.
beats.gist: Carl plans to make Imani fight them so Donut can play a Flee card.

beats.headline: A ring on a church loan
beats.text: Days ago, in Club Vanquisher, instead of the healer: a ring. A million gold. The Temple of Emberus spots me 990,000, interest-free, asterisk. I can't renounce my religion while I owe it. I trade in my strength ring, the first ring I got down here, and the satyr dunks it in lava. It comes out looking the same, but it strips health-seeping and disease debuffs if I worship Emberus, and it curses anyone who doesn't. The achievement is about Columbia House. This is fine.
beats.gist: Carl trades his first strength ring to a satyr who dunks it in lava.

beats.headline: Anchors in the automatons
beats.text: Florin can't set a trap in the stairwell chamber, but nobody says the anchor half of a teleport trap has to stay put. I fix anchors to the backs of the little spider automatons and shove them into Samantha's neck, one red one carrying Donut's trap, and the anchor of one last set stays inside her. The triggers go in the clearing, the first keyed only to me. Ren says Quan is at the Capitol. I throw Samantha fifteen kilometers and step onto the plate.
beats.gist: Carl fixes teleport trap anchors to spider automatons and shoves them into Samantha's neck.

beats.headline: Every last one of them
beats.text: Four minutes, and every option ends with Ren or us. She sits down. She tells me I'm an idiot, and a symbol, and that I can't give my key away. I should have let her finish Quan. I should have kept a trap for Donut. My view counter spikes, and eases once it's clear nobody's going to fight, and I hate that. She gives me her gear and her pet. I tell her I'll kill every last one of them. Every one.
beats.gist: Ren tells Carl he is an idiot and a symbol, then gives him her gear and pet.

beats.headline: Everything Quan carried but the ring
beats.text: Quan has more crap in his inventory than I do, which is saying a lot. Swords, spears, war hammers, a magical chainsaw, a bowler hat you throw like the one in that Bond movie, and a sock full of nickels that is somehow one of the most valuable things on him. Almost five million gold, and I wonder if he ever bought anything. It is all the loot off the crawlers he killed. It transfers with one button. I leave the single golden ring clutched in his hand. I keep his arm. I'm not sure why.
beats.gist: Carl takes everything from Quan's inventory except a golden ring, including a sock full of nickels.

beats.headline: Three questions for a man named Rezan
beats.text: In the chat, Rezan's partner Masoud gets touched by a possessed zombie polecat and explodes. Mandla explains it: like the first-floor bathrooms, your gear goes through the portal, you aren't allowed to, so you pop. I ask Rezan three things. Did the demon go? Did the hole close right away? Did it only take what Masoud was touching? Yes, yes and yes, and he's running for his life, thanks. The big demons' portals last a minute and need two souls. Then I ask everybody about Build Trench scrolls. I've got about fifty. Mandla has a ton.
beats.gist: Carl asks Rezan three questions after a possessed zombie polecat makes Masoud explode.

beats.headline: Not on their schedule
beats.text: The plan is mine and Pony's: everyone who lost a key isolates their stairwell chamber, blows everything off and around it, and trenches in underneath. Katia and Elle spread it, and people tell them they're full of it. So I tell the biggest chat myself, and Prepotente backs me at fifty percent, then forty, then thirty-five. Somebody breaks a door before Osvaldo's people can get through it, so they have to stay and dig. I tell them all I was wrong about this being hopeless. We will not die on their schedule, so stop fighting. Katia says she's with me. Elle, and Li Na. Then the timer appears.
beats.gist: Carl and Pony plan for people without keys to isolate chambers, blow surroundings, and trench underneath.

beats.headline: It had always been loneliness
beats.text: Blue dots walk out of the church. Imani, Katia, Bautista, Louis, Britney, Tran, the Lis, Zhang, Chris, Elle, a few Meadowlark people I barely know. Over twenty of them. Tran and Britney are smiling, the first time since the Masquerade, and I think the first time ever for Britney. Since that floor there has been an extra layer of darkness on everything. I understand now what it is. It's loneliness. It had always been loneliness. Nothing about our situation has changed. We are likely screwed. But we are together, and Elle wants to know what we've got to do.
beats.gist: Over twenty people, including Elle and Britney, walk out of the church together.

beats.headline: The Missing Piece, and eight cards
beats.text: The first quest completes and a new one replaces it, with a ten-minute timer. Ysalte has hold of Amayon. If she still holds him when the timer runs out, they both go to the Ascendency, and everyone without a key is dead. To break free he has to start casting his spell home, and the stronger he is, the bigger that spell has to be. At full power it covers the world. Then, since this is the eighth floor, four cards clank into place in front of the goddess and four the size of garage doors in front of the demon. Really? Really.
beats.gist: The first quest completes and a new one starts with a ten-minute timer.

beats.headline: A Kombucha! achievement
beats.text: A succubus hits me with the force of a bus and we slide past Katia and Donut, nearly into the stair hole. She goes for my neck with vampire fangs just as my new tech shield comes up, and her teeth shatter like crockery. Without thinking, I click a healing potion in my inventory. A terrible taste floods my mouth. A Kombucha! achievement. Ysalte's debuff turned it to vinegar, and normally potions taste like nothing. I cast Heal instead. She has me pinned and is slamming me into the floor.
beats.gist: A succubus hits Carl with the force of a bus and her teeth shatter like crockery.

beats.headline: A crab, a beach, and a deadline
beats.text: I jump off the building and catch Samantha, and she slows us to the ground. I run between the demon's legs, and she flies me to the beach. Donut plays Midnight Express, one of the two consumable cards Ren left me, and for three minutes I'm the deckmaster. I summon Raul the crab and tell him to fertilize the eggs. The AI counted crab sperm as mobs, and that's what broke Sheol, so it has to be a crab. He can't perform without baby seals. There's a pile of dead ones. I summon Alpha Carl to beat me half to death, and he offers a hug instead. Then he yells at Raul, and it works.
beats.gist: Carl summons Raul the crab to fertilize eggs after Alpha Carl yells at him.

beats.headline: Too late by two percent
beats.text: I teleport into the trap I left inside Samantha and land headfirst in her neck hole, with the rest of me somewhere burning. The Martyr's Path wants me under five percent. My hair burns away. The timer ends and I'm at seven. I've failed. Then a button appears, I hit it, and fire bursts up along every step I've taken outside, the Scavenger's Daughter enhancing it. I drop to two percent. The quest completes anyway. The timer stopped with two seconds left, and not because of me. Paz has killed the goddess.
beats.gist: Carl teleports into Samantha's neck hole and burns his hair, but Paz kills the goddess.

beats.headline: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride
beats.text: Shi Maria has my body. I can hear her rooting through my inventory. Another voice, a man's, tells me to hold on; it says she killed him, and now he's here. She calls it a lie. Then my body burns Mongo and Katia, and puts out Li Jun's eye and eats it, and I can't stop my own hands. Don't trust her, boy, the voice says. Then I time out, and there's an eye tattooed over my sternum. It blinks, closes, and disappears into my skin. Tattoo. The Eye of the Bedlam Bride. That's all it says. How's Katia? How's Mongo?
beats.gist: Shi Maria takes Carl's body, eats Li Jun's eye, and burns Mongo and Katia.

beats.headline: Thirty-three thousand eight hundred and four
beats.text: Mordecai has turned the counter back on. The day this floor opened, 38,532 of us had made it here. It reads 33,804. Almost five thousand dead, and in any normal world a tragedy. But they built this floor for a slaughter and we found a way out of it. We're hitting the ninth floor not scattered, not broken and not afraid. Then the viewers vote the sponsors' protections away, ninety-eight percent, and I yell at the ceiling. You wanted a slaughter? It's coming. Your own citizens voted for it. There will be no quarter.
beats.gist: Mordecai turns the counter back on to show 33,804 survivors, and Carl yells at the ceiling.

beats.headline: He takes command of one of nine armies
beats.text: Thirty days. A castle at Larracos, dead centre of the map. No coming back from a death on this floor, for anyone. Supply, alliances, atrocity, at a scale where the arithmetic stops being about people I know.
beats.gist: Carl takes command of one of nine armies for thirty days at a castle in Larracos.

beats.headline: Paulie's real message
beats.text: Christmas morning in the shelter, replayed as a memory. The world freezes, a spoon hangs in midair, and Paulie keeps talking without moving his lips. The crawl is unnecessary, he says: it harvests an element grown inside everyone born on a seeded world, for money. His coffee holds an illegal enhancement. I drink it off my finger and put the cup back on its circle. It gives me a Containment Interface that can trip a fuse and turn the sun nova, killing everybody, the AI included. Then the Paulie part of him speaks: be sure it's your only option. It is still installing.
beats.gist: Carl remembers Christmas morning in the shelter where Paulie says the crawl harvests a seeded world element.

beats.headline: Fifty achievements, and a groan
beats.text: Over fifty achievements to open. Most are stupid: Kombucha, for drinking vinegar. Chickenshit Exploit calls Ren a cheater, for the card totems I teleported into her fight with Quan. She never was one. Touched by a Demon: only one ever handed out, and it's mine, with a Celestial box. Then Unbirthing, for teleporting into Samantha's neck hole, in the AI's deep, throaty voice. It groans. It says it really liked that, and that I am in trouble. Reward: a Legendary Spicy Box.
beats.gist: Carl opens over fifty achievements, including Kombucha for drinking vinegar and Chickenshit Exploit for teleporting card totems.

beats.headline: Walk on Air, already obtained
beats.text: A Legendary toe ring, left pinky toe, and the description is insistent about the toe. Heart Balance holds a potion to fire automatically. Mind Balance protects against Enslavement and Conscription. Physical Balance lists Walk on Air as already obtained. I don't have Walk on Air. Li Jun does. I remember the taste of his eye, and what Shi Maria said about gaining his skills. I message him to apologise. He doesn't answer. I put the ring on anyway, set a gold healing potion to trigger at 2% health, and get one notice: Mind Balance is currently triggered.
beats.gist: Carl puts a Legendary toe ring on his left pinky toe.

beats.headline: Tinsel on the guild floor
beats.text: Waiting on the elevator, I notice a few pieces of tinsel on the guild floor. The Christmas decorations came from the memory simulation and vanished when we got here. This tinsel stayed, so somebody looted it on an earlier floor, from somewhere real. Everything seems normal to me now, and that's the problem: real and make-believe mixed together, and the make-believe often the more dangerous. I think of Pater Coal. I think of Lightning Lou, and how close I came. Paulie's words come back: be sure. On my chest, the eye blinks.
beats.gist: Carl sees tinsel on the guild floor and thinks of Pater Coal, Lightning Lou, and Paulie.

beats.headline: Hup, hup, hup
beats.text: We step out of the bait-shop safe room into a building site: watchtowers, a palisade they are testing with fireballs, a channel being cut up toward the lake. A level 62 Fortification Engineer named Penn drops a steel beam, hugs me, kisses me on the cheek, and starts shouting. Hup, hup, hup. Then thousands of them, humans, skyfowl, crocodilians, bune, yenk, fists and wings in the air, until the ground shakes. Tipid moves to chat. This is for you. This is what you built. In less than three days we'll be waist deep in blood. Then they all go back to work.
beats.gist: Carl steps from a bait-shop safe room into a building site and meets Penn, a Fortification Engineer.

beats.headline: The scouts, over chat
beats.text: I stand in the empty throne room pretending to examine it and ask Florin in chat, because the walls may still have ears. Only someone with the Scout endorsement crosses a border in peacetime. A scout who is discovered gets teleported home and cannot go stealth again until the fighting starts, and a trap still kills them. We get eighteen. The towers are for keeping their scouts out, and they have already sent back one from the Dream and one from the Prism. Florin bets his left sack we're infested with spies anyway.
beats.gist: Carl asks Florin in chat about scouts while pretending to examine an empty throne room.

beats.headline: Mind Balance, level nine
beats.text: I clear my screen by mistake, and when it comes back the spam folder comes with it. Gloom Wraith Phase failed to activate. Prevented by Mind Balance. Mind Balance has risen to level nine. It was five a few hours ago. Pages of it. Shi Maria has been trying to cast through me, and the bombs on that ogre were non-magical. If the phase had gone off, Donut would be in pieces. The skill is getting stronger. So is she. It's a race, and she's winning it. I message Mordecai.
beats.gist: Carl clears his screen and finds Mind Balance has risen to level nine.

beats.headline: Through four skunks, phased
beats.text: The spray comes, and a blink before the cloud reaches me I go incorporeal on Gloom Wraith Phase and rush forward through four skunks with their backs to me. They come apart into ribbons of fur and flesh, and their armour clanks to the forest floor. It feels like running through a sprinkler on a fine mist. I've seen this done before. The rage elemental did it to Yolanda. Five seconds, then Walk on Air, up onto a branch above the cloud, next to Bodi.
beats.gist: Carl uses Gloom Wraith Phase to run through four skunks, cutting them into ribbons of fur.

beats.headline: Removal Order
beats.text: My half of it: the same drug with Removal Order stirred in, so I go into the spider's worst memory instead of mine, and at the end I can lock Shi Maria inside it. Nobody can tell me how the lock will look. Someone has to pull my toe ring off once I'm under, so we can't do this in the guild. The potion it needs is one Mordecai already made. Coincidences in here mean another hand. The last thing I hear going under is a warlord notification. The Lemig Sortion, offering free passage, to treat for peace.
beats.gist: Carl drinks a drug to lock Shi Maria in a spider's memory and hears a warlord notification.

beats.headline: An egg only I can break
beats.text: I wake in the Sugar Cube, standing in a circle of blood and Lemig goblin corpses, fifty or more, with eleven hours gone. Quest failed: the Bedlam Bride. Their own adjutant rules it an AI action. What comes back from the dream: a second spider. Her husband, Hapanzi, who turned into a man. He'd been a god. I have her now, son, he said. You can set her free if you must, but not unless all is lost. She's an egg inside me, and only I can break it.
beats.gist: Carl wakes in the Sugar Cube in a circle of blood and fifty or more Lemig goblin corpses.

beats.headline: They can see our dreams
beats.text: The minor quorum sits in Imogen's kitchen and plays it back. Stockade sent a Summon Ally invitation as I went under, and it was accepted the moment Imani pried off my toe ring. Shi Maria accepted it. Then the screen goes hazy, and I know what it is. Katia's nightmare. Fannar walking out of the office, telling them the truth. The faceless woman at the desk. Architect Houston turns from the screen to look at me. Turn this off, I say. This isn't yours to watch. I'm ignored. The scene changes: Annie in the crib, wired up.
beats.gist: The minor quorum watches Carl's dreams in Imogen's kitchen, including Katia's nightmare and Annie wired in a crib.

beats.headline: A bag of cat food and a hole
beats.text: Houston messages me. Mention his mother again and Donut and I spend our last thousand hours on his amplification table. Gracious pet owners accept the gifts their animals drop on the doorstep. Then the ceasefire ends, his robes fly back on a bug body with six arms, and two of them bring a rifle up at my chest. I dive, grab the bag of cat food off the counter, drop a hob-lobber from my hotlist, and teleport home with a hole punched through my shoulder. No kill message. Either he planned all of this, or he knew what was happening to Stockade and used it.
beats.gist: Houston aims a rifle at Carl, who teleports home with cat food and a shoulder hole.

beats.headline: Disconnect Containment
beats.text: Christmas morning, at the gas station, beside the memory ghost of Lightning Lou, I open the containment interface I got for Paulie's plastic tub. Not one button. Six tabs. On the Fuse page: five benchmarks, two met, and Override Conditions And Activate Fuse. I want to press it more than anything. I think of Donut. I miss you too. Then, at the end of a list, Disconnect Containment: the fuse and the failsafe go inert. Which hurts the Syndicate most, and which protects my people most? I press it. The red dot over Earth starts to grow.
beats.gist: At a gas station beside the memory ghost of Lightning Lou, Carl opens the containment interface.

beats.headline: Soul Poisoning, again
beats.text: Ten miles to the southern front, and the patch on my jacket is glowing again. Mordecai said not to keep it on long. We need the power. A pang across my stomach, a ringing in my ears. Three kids in metal skull caps run out with training spears to join us. The chariot won't take the missile launcher: I've used up my allotted Armor options. Holger sends the kids back with Jamal. Another pang. Soul Poisoning. Activate Daughter's Kiss to disperse the effect.
beats.gist: Carl wears a glowing jacket patch that causes stomach pangs and ringing ears.

beats.headline: Kill them, keep the body
beats.text: The orders I send out on the southern front: if we capture an enemy and can keep them alive but unconscious, we do. The NPCs and the mercenaries from outside get separated. There are spells that can turn the NPCs to our side. The mercenaries have another purpose. If one gives trouble, or it isn't safe to keep them, kill them, loot them by the safe-looting protocol, keep the body, and report it up the chain. The Prism scout who flooded one of our tunnels was one of D'Nadia's own relatives. He stepped on a landmine running away.
beats.gist: Carl orders the southern front to keep unconscious enemies alive but kill and loot troublesome mercenaries.

beats.headline: Over the top
beats.text: Louis drops, Elle hits the first anti-air gun, and our one trebuchet spreads Dazzlers through his craters, fifty of them playing Killing in the Name loud enough to shake the ground. Earplugs barely help. I ask Donut if she's scared. Of course, she says, but it's more numb than anything. My hand is trembling too much to pat her. She goes over on Mongo, and Imani after her. I grab the handhold, shouting something I can't hear, and pull myself up into No Man's Land with over two thousand of the Posse.
beats.gist: Louis drops, Elle hits an anti-air gun, and a trebuchet spreads fifty ground-shaking Dazzlers.

beats.headline: Build Trench, joined
beats.text: In a crater in front of their line I read a Build Trench scroll, turn the line ninety degrees and tell it to join their trench. Elevation lower. Yes. Dig. The ground goes out from under a Saccathian soldier twenty feet ahead. Craft magic, so it ignores most protections: an exploit that's been pointed out for years and never fixed. All along the line our people are doing the same. I activate Daughter's Kiss on my right foot, tell everyone to take cover, jump, and land on his chest.
beats.gist: Carl reads a Build Trench scroll in a crater, digs a trench, and lands on a Saccathian.

beats.headline: Twenty-five seconds out
beats.text: I conk out the second I kill him. Twenty-five seconds, Imani says: a soul-poisoning debuff called Post Nut Clarity, and I buried us in dirt, and don't do that again. But I blew their trench apart. I've gone up a level, and there's a message I've been expecting, which can wait. Command goes to Colonel Boomer. Louis lands, and Bonnie is standing behind his door gun. Donut gave her the last scout spot while I was under. She's older than I am, Carl.
beats.gist: Carl kills him and conks out for twenty-five seconds with a soul-poisoning debuff called Post Nut Clarity.

beats.headline: The edge
beats.text: She's bleeding against the wall, asking why I'm telling her about Signet. She told Signet her family wasn't real. I hate her more than anything in the universe. I never felt this with Maggie My, or Quan Ch, or sitting in that gas station with the button. I tell Donut I've changed my mind, I want to do it myself. She asks me to step back. The mark forms. And there it is, the edge. I'm standing on it, one foot out over open air. I take a step back. Okay, Donut. It's time.
beats.gist: Carl stands on an edge with one foot over open air and tells Donut it is time.

beats.headline: Mercy for the gnolls
beats.text: Eight gnoll mercenaries come over to the Posse with their banners blinking red, and for about a week I can order any of them to stand still while I cut his throat. My finger itches. Please, no, Donut said, so I take the Ring of Divine Suffering off, and everyone in the room watches me do it. Corporal Pillbox begs for Lockjaw and Mange, his mates on the other two teams. Mange is his cousin. The anger drains out of me like it went out an airlock. None of you have to die today, I tell him. At least not by our hands.
beats.gist: Eight gnoll mercenaries join the Posse; Carl removes the Ring of Divine Suffering to spare them.

beats.headline: Two kinds of residual
beats.text: Agatha is a residual, like Paulie at the Florida homeless shelter, except Orren told me she's the other kind. Paulie's side wants the crawl to end and goes at it through the AI itself. Tipid and Rosetta say Mantis scientists can now build AIs that are easier to control, which makes this old one the residuals' last chance, and both sides are making their move. I don't know what either side actually wants. I'm not sure anybody does. The prime minister is sticking his nose in, and she's asked for me by name.
beats.gist: Agatha is a residual, and both sides of the residuals are making their move.

beats.headline: We don't eat our own
beats.text: Reid Gunn is on the casualty list, and his dot is standing in a bunker, and the dots beside him keep turning into Xs. Brain worms. Gondii. A medic runs in with a wounded yenk between him and a mage named Charles Andrew, and Charles Andrew is listed as dead. I tackle him and punch him with a spiked gauntlet until he actually is. The worm comes out of his face, black and white, named Goldblum, and I stamp on it. Rend moves in to eat the body. No, Rend. We don't eat our own. Unleash Tina.
beats.gist: Carl punches a dead mage named Charles Andrew with a spiked gauntlet to kill a worm.

beats.headline: Fire in the hole
beats.text: We agreed I stay where I can see the whole battle, so I stay on the barracks roof. Then my trap sense lights up: somebody is arming a pile of automatons with satchel charges on proximity triggers, far right corner, all purple dots. You might be battle-hardened, I think, but you're in my playground now. Fire in the hole. I cast Tripper. It's bigger than I expected. Everyone without a Steady buff goes over, Rend gets punted off the roof, and the automatons are a crater. My eardrums are blown out again. I'm getting used to that particular pain.
beats.gist: Carl stays on the barracks roof and casts Tripper, cratering automatons and blowing out his eardrums.

beats.headline: Because I turned it off
beats.text: The king asks me to plead with his daughter for the people of Earth, and all I can do is laugh. What do we get out of helping you? The deal: his army withdraws, we don't harass it. On the walk back Donut asks if we're all about to die, and I tell her privately we're not. The failsafe isn't going to go off. I know it's deactivated because I'm the one who turned it off. I came so close that night. The AI's sphere of influence just took Uranus. I tell Donut it's a hunch.
beats.gist: The king asks Carl to plead with his daughter; Carl laughs and negotiates an army withdrawal.

beats.headline: My terms, counted on fingers
beats.text: I'm in Orren's office covered in the king's gore, and none of today's big deaths was my hand. It unsteadies me. It was Rosetta's. A cookbook author. My sister. How could I not be proud? Orren wants my hunch explained. So I count on my fingers: end the crawl, free every crawler, spend every Syndicate asset rebuilding what you stole, stop fighting my people up there, and leave our system and never come back. He says the AI would never allow it. Then he asks if I can undo it. I had that option. I almost did it, too.
beats.gist: Carl stands in Orren's office covered in the king's gore and counts five terms on his fingers.

beats.headline: So close, it says
beats.text: The AI is wearing Growler Gary. It drinks from a bottle of vodka and mentions the game we played the other day, when it let me install that interface. That was so close, wasn't it? So close, and I felt it. So it would've worked, I ask. If I'd pressed the fuse button? It doesn't answer. It just looks at me and laughs. Then it stands behind my chair and massages my shoulders, growling, and my whole body goes stiff.
beats.gist: The AI wears Growler Gary, drinks vodka, and laughs at Carl before massaging his shoulders.

beats.headline: Operation: Snake Pit
beats.text: Donut didn't really make the king into a rug. He's in my inventory, and so is a second Ring of Divine Suffering, and that damn necklace. Boomer walks me through the mess and says now might be the time to move on the Operatic castle, which is code. Operation: Snake Pit. We can't get Donut and Katia off this floor unless we beat the nagas, and not just beat them: wipe them out, down to the last snake. It has to happen when they least expect it. Katia messages that she's almost back. See you soon, I send back.
beats.gist: Carl keeps the king, a second Ring of Divine Suffering, and a necklace in his inventory.

beats.headline: Run, Little Günter, Run
beats.text: The spellbook from my 1914 box grows centipede legs, skitters off, drips black goo on the counter and begs not to be read, in a ridiculous accent. The cleaner bot sucks it up and drops it in my arms. Run, Little Günter, Run. It summons a small, fat creature with one point of health. Hit him, and he stores the attack and carries it off toward the target. It seemed impractical until I thought of the Daughter's Kiss. That's a bomb. I apply the spellbook and feel the warmth of learning it.
beats.gist: A spellbook with centipede legs drips black goo and summons a fat creature to store attacks.

beats.headline: The loophole in the listings
beats.text: Everyone at this table knows things from outside they shouldn't. Odette explains it: every team but ours and Retribution bought the news upgrade, and they're paying about 30,000 credits a go to rename shows in the feed directory, so the listings are the message. The AI loves a good loophole and won't close one without an emergency request. Donut asks Ferdinand to spend theirs. Juice Box stops him. They have two left, and so do we. She's right. It's ours to deal with, so I propose the Emergency Action Item myself.
beats.gist: Odette explains that teams pay 30,000 credits to rename shows in the feed directory.

beats.headline: Blood Hunter, and a dead army
beats.text: Odette mentions, with a wink in my direction, that the Sultanate owns a studio. Blood Hunter Holdings. The drama. We've been racking our brains over why the Naga have so few troops, why Elle and Edgar saw nobody in their territory. Now I know. They're dead. I don't know how, but most of their soldiers died when the hostilities began, and the Sultanate is trying to hide it. It also means Operation: Snake Pit is already in trouble. I start laughing and can't stop, and Ferdinand, draped over my head, laughs along without the faintest idea why.
beats.gist: Odette tells Carl the Sultanate owns Blood Hunter Holdings and hid that most soldiers died.

beats.headline: The other way of dealing with him
beats.text: Pony lands, level 99, and says it himself before I can finish: recruit me. Behind my back I'm holding a potion of Conscription, the other way of dealing with him if he refused. I put it back in my inventory, and the relief surprises me. Not like that. Never like that. My first instinct is to make him a Legionnaire. I make him a Colonel. Then he throws his arms around me and sobs that I'm his best friend, that he's been so lonely since I didn't show up at the Bahamas. I pat him awkwardly. He screams in my face.
beats.gist: Pony lands at level 99 and asks Carl to recruit him.

beats.headline: Mork, and the blasphemer's end
beats.text: The ram at the door, Mork, wants to split my bounty on Pony with Hellik, and I tell him we have a deal. When the fight starts and he bolts for the door, I break a potion of Black Nimbus on the back of his head, and he's cut off from his god on his own doorstep. Then Li Na's dread comes down the wire. Mork pulls out his own eyes and puts them back in backward. The trophy heads on the walls start screaming, the rugs move, and he digs into his own chest before he runs out of strength. Quest complete: ten seconds of Emberus laughing, and a Celestial Boon. Heathen Scald on every punch for the rest of the floor.
beats.gist: Carl breaks a potion of Black Nimbus on Mork's head, leading to a Celestial Boon.

beats.headline: The Waffle Maker at my feet
beats.text: I cast Günter, yell at him to get the god, and set the Waffle Maker off at my feet in a very narrow room. I'm flattened across the door, turned inside out, and the immortality holds my atoms together. For a moment there's nothing. I'm drowning in nothing. Then it all comes back at once, bones knitting, nerves lighting up like a power grid, and it hurts more than anything ever should. Donut says two more are dead, one to go. Then I understand what's squeezing me: Vinata, wrapped around me outside the portal, stabbing and slamming my head into the floor, staring into the eye on my chest.
beats.gist: Carl casts Günter, detonates the Waffle Maker, and is flattened across a door.

beats.headline: Without a hitch
beats.text: Donut messages from the Naga stronghold while I'm still wrapped in Milk's wings. Nothing happened there. They didn't need one of Juice Box's diggers after all; it was easier than she thought. It was easy here, too, I tell her. Went off without a hitch. Afterwards I write a note for Drakea, who hated the naga. If there's a veil, I hope she watched from the other side. I don't know what today means for the naga as a people, but I did what I could. It's getting harder every day to keep myself from drowning.
beats.gist: Carl is wrapped in Milk's wings when Donut messages from the Naga stronghold.

beats.headline: What gives me the right?
beats.text: Two hours until Open Hostilities, and the Nest is done: master quality, glowing gold, tall enough to give Donut line of sight across the whole battlefield from the top. That's the point of it. Every long-range spell and weapon out there will be aimed at it, with her sitting on top in a glittering tiara. It was my idea. Operation Ruin hits from above, from below, from the land, and from within, all at once. Even our best-case scenarios predict heavy losses. I keep thinking of the fifth floor, and the crawlers I sent down under the bubbles. What gives me the right?
beats.gist: Carl builds a master quality, glowing gold Nest for Donut to wear a glittering tiara.

beats.headline: Banned from every temple
beats.text: Varg Vikernes. That's the achievement for defiling Club Vanquisher: I'm permanently banned from the club and from every temple except Emberus's and the ones where I've been named a friend of the church. The list is strange. Hellik added me moments after I told him I'm supposed to kill him. Apito. Eileithyia, and Yemaya, who we freed. Theia. Nekhebit, who Odette drives. And Grull, which makes no sense whatsoever. Liquified, for blowing myself up while immortal, gets me a patch I won't wear. And for fighting a god in his own temple, no reward, because another god saved my hide.
beats.gist: Carl defiles Club Vanquisher and receives the Varg Vikernes achievement, banning him from most temples.

beats.headline: Leader of Earth, apparently
beats.text: Rishi, armless in a prismatic cell, says he hid because going into that temple meant dying, and because he had an offer. Under Syndicate law, in the absence of a working government, a court has named me the de facto leader of Earth, on his petition. His document: citizenship for Earth natives in naga territories and five generation ships, in exchange for settling the other planets in our system. He signed it as Sultan Rishi the Usurper. I tell him I'd like to renegotiate. Take the ships and drive yourselves into the nearest star. The ring's thirty seconds pass. His highest stat is Dexterity.
beats.gist: Rishi tells Carl that a court named him the de facto leader of Earth.

beats.headline: The plan for the day
beats.text: Operation: Ruin. Four offensives kicking off at once, then what Donut calls the Coup De War Crime. Florin has the orcs, Boomer the Reavers, Donut the Dream, and the Madness is mine. Rosetta is Theater Commander. I ride with Louis on his first bomb run, because my being near the bombs makes them bigger, then he drops me and Samantha in Reaver territory, I meet Elle, and we take the Gate to the Madness. I know friends will die today. If this is my last entry, know I went down fighting.
beats.gist: Carl plans Operation Ruin with four offensives and the Coup De War Crime.

beats.headline: Plans nobody told me about
beats.text: The war mages have the Gate, and Justice Light panics in chat that he needs it back. He needs it. He doesn't say why, or how he planned on getting it. That's the part that stays with me. Rosetta took King Rust's head without warning us. Juice Box and the NPCs make dangerous moves nobody mentions. People keep making plans without communicating them, and they use me as part of them. Meanwhile the portal Elle opened by accident is running down, and a feral god is coming out of it wherever we're standing.
beats.gist: War mages have the Gate while Justice Light panics in chat.

beats.headline: Boomer is right
beats.text: There's a dragon over the Reaver castle, with gravity magic, and I tell Louis to swing wide of it. Boomer comes on my private band. He needs those bombs; he has nothing else to kill their electronics; I gave operational command to Rosetta and the Reaver assault to him, and I can't call off a run because it's dangerous. He's right. I apologise, belay the order, and tell Louis to save his four anti-air missiles for the dragon. Then I make Samantha an officer so she can paint the thing. Elle asks if I'm done running everyone else's operation.
beats.gist: Carl tells Louis to swing wide of a gravity magic dragon over the Reaver castle.

beats.headline: Mind Balance sixteen, barefoot
beats.text: I sit against a tree and think about the Lone Ranger and my dad's westerns, and the Christmas present I haven't opened. Then someone slaps me awake, and Imani is shouting. They're hammering me with psionics: ten more Endless Threads, Self Harm, Intrusive Thoughts. If I surrender, maybe they let everyone live. A voice, male, friendly, maybe a dwarf, tells me I'm not crazy and to look at my feet. They're buried in an All Tree root. Mind Balance hits sixteen. The tree dies behind me. Now I can see the mind mages, and I paint them.
beats.gist: Carl sits barefoot against a tree and thinks of westerns until Imani and mind mages attack.

beats.headline: The castle in front of me
beats.text: Everyone I brought is in Eris's pile except the pets, Jamal, Bigs and Dong, and only Dong and I have the invulnerability. Louis is falling onto the Reaver castle. The instinct is to run to one of them. Dong says Jefferson believes we should take the Madness castle while their army is gone. He's right. I can't do anything for Louis, or for the pile. I can do something about the castle in front of me. Donut, Rosetta and Mordecai are smart. Then Donut commits an atrocity.
beats.gist: Carl chooses the Madness castle over Eris's pile and Louis, then Donut commits an atrocity.

beats.headline: Houston's table
beats.text: Houston is on his own table, joining himself to a dead changeling, and the traps on the balcony will burn the room if anyone steps on the floor or he dies. I jump table to table, put Burcu to sleep, and hit her bindings. Then the table tips and she hits the floor, and so do I. The traps fire. I phase through Houston, and something in the machine spins with me and wears Li Jun's face. Thank you for giving me more time with my sister and my best friend. Houston is dead. Burcu is dead. The Madness is defeated.
beats.gist: Carl jumps between tables, puts Burcu to sleep, and hits her bindings.

beats.headline: I trust her
beats.text: Victory asks what Donut's plan is. She hasn't told me, and no, I'm not going to question her. I trust her. Then two meteors come out of Larracos at the ball, and a woman is spat out of it: Nami, the pilot of Eris, ejected by a war mage from inside. Samantha reports another mage conscripting Yarilo with a potion. They are recruiting gods. I throw a healing potion onto the ball instead of a bomb, tell Donut to keep it intact and roll it toward the city, and run.
beats.gist: Victory asks for Donut's plan, but Carl trusts her and does not question her.

beats.headline: Shit Just Hit
beats.text: Toyotomi and Bomo go quiet, and I don't think. I drink my last Levitation potion at the railing and go straight up. The plan was to aim carefully at the Piccadilly. Instead I drop an entire inventory folder called Shit Just Hit: about twenty Waffle Makers, two No Disassembles, a pair of cheese cutters, some five hundred hob-lobbers and more dynamite than I can count. My Walk on Air runs out three quarters of the way to the lip, and I drop. The generator goes, and so does every window in the area, and the city's defence system wakes up. One tower locks onto me.
beats.gist: Carl drinks a Levitation potion and drops an inventory folder of waffle makers and dynamite.

beats.headline: Scars we rarely choose
beats.text: The potion takes. Under Orders; she drops the frightened act, and I order her protections off. Two hundred player killer skulls. Twenty hunters. Her own game guide. I tell her I don't have one, and that with scars we rarely get to choose. I put on the Ring of Divine Suffering. Florin thinks there are kids trapped in that head. Maybe. The conscription ends with the floor and she keeps coming for the people I love. So I apologise for what I'm about to do. Then her voice changes, and I stop.
beats.gist: Carl puts on the Ring of Divine Suffering and apologizes before he stops when her voice changes.

beats.headline: What sort of monster am I
beats.text: Florin's old dictionary, the one with the bullet hole, defines atrocity as an act of fiendish cruelty. The system calls Donut's War Crime spell an Atrocity, and maybe the real cruelty was giving it to her at all, out of the Legendary box we got for killing D'Nadia. I've never before prayed for my own plan to fail while needing it to work. If she doesn't cast it, we likely don't survive the coming hours. If she does, what then? She says she's ready. If I let her, what sort of monster am I?
beats.gist: Carl uses Florin's bullet-holed dictionary to define atrocity while Donut prepares to cast a War Crime spell.

beats.headline: The long description of War Crime
beats.text: Rosetta changes the plan at the top of the Nest. Bijanbi, a Dinner Bell variant from a cleric who fell defending the FUPA, and Wall of Fire, both through Donut's War Crime; the fleshers already wrapped round the enemy are the finisher. Oh. Oh hell. I have the spell's long description in my scratch pad. Health to one percent. Only on the Scolopendra levels, three casts, ever, and it can't kill anyone directly. The last part, which only I seem to see, is two hundred mercenaries paralysed and on fire for two weeks. I agree with Rosetta anyway.
beats.gist: Rosetta changes the plan at the Nest top; Donut uses War Crime on Bijanbi and Wall of Fire.

beats.headline: Waiting on top of the Nest
beats.text: On top of the Nest, Donut tells me Li Na said Li Jun's death was her fault. She says Li Na isn't wrong. Lucia killed Bomo. If something goes wrong and we lose everybody, it's on her. I tell her they put us here; this is their war. Then she says she and Katia have a plan, that Bautista can't know, and that Katia told her not to tell me because I'll Carl it up. The rest she sends by message: she got a benefactor box when I wasn't looking. Then Li Na says go.
beats.gist: On top of the Nest, Donut tells Carl Li Na blames herself for Li Jun's death.

beats.headline: A nuke in a block of ice
beats.text: A dog the size of a lion jumps out of the top honeycomb with a bomb notification on its back half, and Elle freezes it. I pick up the block of ice. It burns, but it goes into my inventory before the dog can explode. The bomb says Mini Tactical Nuke. Run. Juice Box drops Louis's No Disassembles and teleports him out, and I set them off from my crafting menu and dive on Donut. The castle goes up and throws us all. The System gives me fifty-one percent of the experience for Fang.
beats.gist: A lion-sized dog with a Mini Tactical Nuke jumps out; Elle freezes it and Carl inventories it.

beats.headline: The ring goes down the cat
beats.text: Over fifty thousand former crawlers came to fight for us. About twenty-eight thousand are left. Of the 32,500 crawlers who reached this floor, 20,221 are still here, a record. The mercenaries we beat are milling around Larracos, and my first instinct is to mark them, kill them, and go to three hundred across the board like Li Na. One look at her tells me that slope is too steep. I still don't want to let the ring go. I hold it up in front of Donut's nose. Are you sure? I'm sure. She swallows it.
beats.gist: Donut swallows a ring after over fifty thousand former crawlers fight for Carl and Donut.

beats.headline: Laughter in the river
beats.text: The stairwells fill. Tran goes in. Zhang goes in alone. Li Na goes in without a word. Tuba and Selvi, Burcu's party, leave to take deals, and never told me why Burcu thought I killed her father. That's the problem with such chaos. You lose so much around the edges. And right then I hear distant laughing, deep in the back of my mind, from the river I hoped would go with the ring. It sounds like Eris.
beats.gist: Tran, Zhang, and Li Na enter the stairwells while Tuba and Selvi leave to take deals.

beats.headline: The sound of nobody dying
beats.text: Quest complete. The Outreach Guild: a zero zone, a table, two chairs, no doors, and Quasar in a tie with Mongo on it. I'm covered in ash and blood and I can't stop shaking. It's done. We made it. Don't you hear it, Quasar? The sound of nobody dying. Nobody screaming. I could live in this room. The deals are all rubbish, so I tell him I'm not taking one. Then he says we need to talk about Donut's lawyer, Princess Chandra, Esquire. She's my new wife.
beats.gist: Carl enters the Outreach Guild covered in ash and blood to meet Quasar and Mongo.

beats.headline: Five thousand five hundred and one
beats.text: Five thousand five hundred and one. Seventy-five per cent of us took deals, and the relief I feel about that is enormous and secondhand. Every one of them earned it. Then the message I knew was coming: Justice Light, "I am not sorry," from a deceased mercenary. Quasar has already told me the Nothing is broken, the club on the eighteenth floor is inside an awake Scolopendra, and the guests there can neither eject nor die. I have a garage, two gremlins in overalls and four minutes on a countdown. I will not be taking that way out.
beats.gist: Carl has a garage, two gremlins in overalls, and four minutes on a countdown.

beats.headline: The wheel lands on a food truck
beats.text: The wheel ticks past a school bus, the Popemobile, a missile launcher and something that is either a floor polisher or a Zamboni, and settles on a box truck with windows. A food truck. Big Shot Chicken, the 1920s-gangster chain whose safe room Donut and I sat out the rage elemental in. Chrome fenders, a fiberglass nose built to sit at a state fair, and a giant plastic tommy gun on the roof whose drum magazine blocks half the windshield. No passenger seat. I turn the key and there is an engine. Good. I drive.
beats.gist: The wheel lands on a Big Shot Chicken food truck with a giant plastic tommy gun.

beats.headline: Only driving
beats.text: Seventy miles an hour down a black road in the dark, slumped low to see under the plastic gun, and Mongo pukes on the dashboard. And for a minute it is almost peaceful. If I make a mistake here, I die, Donut dies, and that is all. Nobody else. After the armies of the last floor I could cry at how small that is. It does not hold. Donut keeps wiping her paw on things and I keep not looking. Katia is out and free. Justice Light showed there is also the possibility of vengeance. First we have to survive this floor.
beats.gist: Carl drives seventy miles an hour down a dark road while Mongo pukes on the dashboard.

beats.headline: We tow them in
beats.text: The Trauco Triplets are eliminated the moment their mount dies. One team gone. The next one down is a red Pontiac minivan on its side and burning, with two bugbears trying to save it. If they go too, Prepotente's arithmetic says we race our friends. So Donut drops the manatee, I make fire hoses out of a bucket and a kitchen bowl with water scrolls, and when the van is plainly finished I tell them the truth and start building a flatbed. They are awake, they are scared, and they want to be free. The next race is the next race.
beats.gist: Carl eliminates the Trauco Triplets and builds a flatbed for two bugbears from a burning Pontiac.

beats.headline: A catalogue of weapons
beats.text: Hedy hands me a tablet with over a thousand upgrades, and I scroll past the hover and the climbing tires into the weapons. A barrel of spikes like the goblin murder dozer. A flamethrower. A pulse that shuts down other drivers. A brick wall you drop on the road behind you. We can maybe avoid killing other teams. We cannot stop them killing each other, and Zhang says Li Na has already killed most of her heat. Crawler against crawler is coming. I start thinking about a driving rig Katia could build, and then I remember. I pick the spider legs.
beats.gist: Hedy hands Carl a tablet of upgrades, and he picks spider legs for a driving rig.

beats.headline: Come to Daddy
beats.text: Most of my achievements are leftovers from the end of Faction Wars. Bomb's Away, for emptying my inventory in midair without aiming any of it. Wastrel, for feeding Frank Q's ring to a cat, reward withheld in terms I won't repeat. And Come to Daddy, for rejecting the exit deal, written like the AI is about to cry. I'm not like the ungrateful ones running off the playground. Good boy. The Gold Payload Box holds a skill potion that doubles my hotlist. No celestial this time. Then there is the fan box, and I already know what's in it.
beats.gist: Carl has achievements for emptying his inventory in midair and feeding Frank Q's ring to a cat.

beats.headline: We don't tell Dong
beats.text: The half-mantaur in the gimp suit waves at us before his garage door comes down, and Donut names him before I do. Dong's friend. Corcunda. They put him here to mess with us, and the way to handle that kind of drama is never to step in it in the first place. So we don't tell Dong. I say that out loud, which is my mistake. The air ripples. New quest: reunite them, part one of two, and part two needs his other half and a fleshmancer. Reward: two stand-ins of our choosing, sent to the arena on the eleventh floor.
beats.gist: Carl and Donut meet Corcunda, a half-mantaur in a gimp suit, and a quest to reunite him.

beats.headline: Who goes to the arena
beats.text: Kill certain mobs on this floor and the audience votes. One way, the mob survives and is sent to the arena. The other way, a stand-in goes instead, and the stand-ins are people from outside the dungeon, like the guests at the resort on the eighteenth floor. The arena is on the eleventh floor, and nobody knows anything beyond that. I can't stop thinking about it. The AI dragged Princess Formidable off her own spaceship. Could I pick someone in orbit? A liaison like Harbinger? Prime Minister Victory? Who could I send down there who would do the most damage?
beats.gist: Carl considers sending people like Harbinger or Prime Minister Victory to the eleventh floor arena.

beats.headline: The truck will not be modified
beats.text: Fifteen minutes to the line. I stand in the passenger door and try to tear the tommy gun off the roof with my bare hands, and the dungeon informs me I may not change the stock configuration of my vehicle. Fine. The driver is a crocodile who has driven a cart, the GPS threatens to drown him in a swamp, and the freezer in the back refills itself every ten seconds. Then Zhang's message lands. Tran's team is in his heat. And so it begins.
beats.gist: Carl tries to tear a tommy gun off his truck roof, but the dungeon forbids modifications.

beats.headline: Black and White at the start line
beats.text: The plan was one kill: Donut roots the womantaur driver with a Danforth bolt, Chiyome's bear does the rest, and nobody else dies, because if a second team goes, all of it was for nothing. Then the hail takes the awning off, Team Sparkles puts a cannon through the car in front of us, Donut never fires, and our one kill is somebody else's. The bugbears' van is playing "Black and White". My mom loved that song. For a moment I just sit there and listen.
beats.gist: Carl plans one kill using a Danforth bolt and a bear, but hail and a cannon ruin it.

beats.headline: There will always be clues
beats.text: Two province bosses, level 170, squatting on the road like kangaroos that grew spikes, with pouches full of dead joeys and one live engineer wearing a joey. Chiyome sets the other one's pouch alight and it pulls out a burning razor fox, eats him, and heals to full. Its only weak spot is inside the pouch. So I ask Donut to examine the dead joeys. Starvation. And their inventory is just their skin. A skin. There will always be clues.
beats.gist: Carl finds two level 170 province bosses with pouches of dead joeys and one live engineer.

beats.headline: Into the pouch
beats.text: Genesis was supposed to hook me a dead joey. She hooks the engineer through the face instead, so I peel the joey skin off his corpse: protection from acid, a jump skill, twelve hours on the clock, and I cannot walk in it, only hop. So I hop, onto the boss's pouch, and he shoves me in himself. Down through the goo to the bottom, two satchels dropped, then out again on Gloom Wraith Phase and the detonator in the air. It works. A gremlin drops his toolbox on me. I probably deserved that.
beats.gist: Genesis hooks an engineer through the face, so Carl peels the joey skin off the corpse.

beats.headline: Barely responsible for myself
beats.text: Last place, and alive because another team died first. No fuss, no epic fight: we'd just be gone. I lie on the garage floor in a dead kangaroo and look at the gremlin's blood on the ceiling. I thought I was relieved not to be responsible for so many people any more. Now I'm barely responsible for myself. It feels like the day my father put his motorcycle helmet through the fish tank, and every molly died, no matter what I did.
beats.gist: Carl lies on a garage floor in a dead kangaroo, remembering his father breaking a fish tank.

beats.headline: Everything is connected, somehow
beats.text: Akuma. He killed Stalwart, stole the Gate, and left me to deal with Agatha. Now he wants two teams dead and hasn't said why, so I won't do it, not deliberately. The Pineapple Cabaret I've heard once: the AI, wearing Growler Gary, offered "Backstage at the Pineapple Cabaret" to Formidable as a place of banishment, and every place on that list was bad. Samantha's daughter. The Scavenger. Emberus and Geyrun. Prepotente's crystal. It's all connected, and I have no idea what any of it means.
beats.gist: Akuma killed Stalwart and stole the Gate, leaving Carl to deal with Agatha.

beats.headline: He asks it on live
beats.text: The goats of the Plenty sentence us to death and then take questions. One explains what Justice did: broke the Nothing and let everything inside it loose into three levels. Then Orren and Victory are in my chat, wanting me to ask about the integrity of the tunnels in their exact words. I rephrase. Does the public know the gods have escaped? That the AI is in their tunnels? That they're in worse danger than us? That they need to run? Out loud. The AI lets it go out.
beats.gist: Carl asks the goats of the Plenty if the public knows the gods escaped into their tunnels.

beats.headline: Too dangerous for the herd
beats.text: Victory tells me that was reckless. Please. They knew exactly what would happen when they asked me. The goats stampede out through the wall, and the one who stays, Gamori, the matriarch, judges me: rash, impulsive, loud, a troublemaker, too dangerous to walk amongst the herd. So I ask why they're even here. She bursts into tears. They sponsored us at their partner's behest. The kids love us. I'm best friends with their champion. She knew all of it and told nobody.
beats.gist: Victory calls Carl reckless after goats stampede through a wall and Gamori judges Carl too dangerous.

beats.headline: Glue and foam
beats.text: Ninety seconds of invulnerability, twenty minutes, thirty kilometres straight down. I swing the two ghoul cages out on Hedy's booms and fire the eight-pack: four Denial of Service missiles at One Fine Pig, four at Team Sparkles. They don't explode. They glue. Three bury the unicorn's shield in green mucus and the bush goes spinning in circles. Then the sugar hermits come in twenty-foot waves, the ghouls throw Biscuit Packs, foam that sets like rock, and Donut puts up a wall of fire a mile long.
beats.gist: Carl fires Denial of Service missiles that glue One Fine Pig and Team Sparkles in green mucus.

beats.headline: Feet first into the skull
beats.text: Gluteus is out cold on the wheel with a three-storey beetle skull between us and the finish. I grab the wheel, which means I've driven. Donut takes the pedals. I climb out through the windshield, lie on my back on the hood, activate Daughter's Kiss and aim my kangaroo feet at the skull. Then Dwight's cannon hits us, and the truck, the GTO and the bush all go over the line spinning together. The suit shreds against the road. Both arms, both legs, the pelvis. First place.
beats.gist: Carl lies on the hood and aims kangaroo feet at a three-storey beetle skull.

beats.headline: Triple the price, and he pays it
beats.text: Rosetta and Tipid bring in team Helix: a Grulke named Olga, a Porsuk named Finley with poison on his claws, and a fire fairy named Quemada, three mercenaries for the price of one. They have raced two heats already. Quemada takes one look at the Emberus shrine in the back of the room and decides the fee is now triple. Rosetta says the price was settled with the guild. I ask whether they drove in the last races. Two of them drive. We'll pay the price.
beats.gist: Rosetta and Tipid bring in team Helix, three mercenaries who charge triple for the Emberus shrine.

beats.headline: Four ways out of the Emberus problem
beats.text: The Kill Hellik quest has been sitting in the back of my head and I have not planned for it, which is a mistake. The options: kill Hellik, and Emberus has told me to my face he will kill me for it. Don't kill Hellik, or leave the church, and I get smitten. Or kill Emberus, whom I cannot get near without burning to dust, and then every other god wants me dead. Now Eris wants me to ditch him for her. I grab her coin and it burns a swirl into my palm.
beats.gist: Carl considers killing Hellik, leaving the church, or killing Emberus, then grabs Eris's coin, burning his palm.

beats.headline: An idea he will not say in chat
beats.text: Eris is gone and my heart will not slow down. I write everything into my notes: the four sides of the coin, Britney and the pickaxe, Florin, the Pineapple Cabaret. I have to close the eye on my chest on purpose. We are on rails, playing their game. We have to break it. I have an idea so ridiculous, so completely suicidal, that I dismiss it straight away. Then I tell the group chat everything, and ask them to hear me out on a plan I cannot type the end of.
beats.gist: Carl tells the group chat a suicidal plan he cannot type the end of.

beats.headline: Trust, but verify
beats.text: I fist-bump Akuma into my chat and leave him on two percent health. He answers nothing except to say I'm annoying. I don't trust him. But Herot, and Eris swearing he has a way out, keep me on the hook. So: gather volunteers who can fight in the Cabaret, have Prepotente and Mordecai work the shop-interface exploit, send some of the strippers back to the Desperado Club for the other way in. Everything still has to fit between races. I miss bouncing around a map.
beats.gist: Carl fist-bumps Akuma into his chat and leaves him on two percent health.

beats.headline: Fists against an armoured door
beats.text: Finley walked out of our garage to go and find his friends a temple and One Fine Pig ran all three of them into the pavement, then backed up and did it again. I storm their garage. Their gun takes out a wall and a bus. I dent the door with my gauntlet until their shield throws me into the street. Imani and Donut pull me away. I sit on the curb in front of what is left. It was a simple act of defiance, and it was snuffed out.
beats.gist: Carl storms a garage after One Fine Pig runs Finley and two friends into the pavement.

beats.headline: Two traps, keyed to Tigrans
beats.text: While Donut talks, I lay a hidden trap on each side of their truck, as close to the shield as I dare. Disintegration traps, like the one I pulled off Akuma's door: silent, one target each, and I set them to fire only for a Tigran, so even if one of them is carrying the pig, she is safe. Five seconds. Imani asks how I'm feeling. I tell her I freaked out, that Donut talked me down, and that I have an idea.
beats.gist: Carl lays two silent disintegration traps keyed to Tigrans by a truck while Donut talks.

beats.headline: One Fine Pig is eliminated
beats.text: Two notifications, one after the other. A Tigran dissolved, then the other. One Fine Pig is out, both racers expired, five teams left. I hold my breath, and nothing comes about Penelope. We have drawn Satan's Water Park, an hour behind team Sparkles, with Florin already on it. We need to win the heat, because the winner gets a key, and we need the key, because we need that pig. Florin asks if there's a team I need slowed down. Let me tell you about a unicorn named Dwight.
beats.gist: Two racers dissolve and One Fine Pig is eliminated. Carl draws Satan's Water Park behind team Sparkles.

beats.headline: Mehmet's page
beats.text: An entry in the Book of Boom from Mehmet Or, level sixty-two, a Sipahi. He owned a bowling alley in Istanbul that his father left him. He killed his pregnant wife in the hydra. He has taken a deal, and he asks me to forgive the cowardice. His daughters, Azra and Yaz, did not step into the light with him, and he thinks they are with the children. If I cannot save him, find them and tell them he loved them. Associated spell: Gutter Bumper. I never met him.
beats.gist: Carl reads a Book of Boom entry from Mehmet Or, a level sixty-two Sipahi.

beats.headline: Ice, chains and rodents
beats.text: The River of Sloth is packed with Gingers on inner tubes, and Maurice is somewhere among them. I cast Mehmet's Gutter Bumper along the river, and Donut's Ice Slick follows the lines and freezes the lot solid. We drive over the ice dragging every spare weapon I own on chains behind the truck, then Donut casts Summon Ye, Vermin and the zipper shrews drill through whoever is left, Maurice included. Quest complete. People like Mehmet, who buffed everyone else and saved lives, are the real heroes here.
beats.gist: Carl casts Mehmet's Gutter Bumper and Donut casts Ice Slick to freeze Gingers on the River of Sloth.

beats.headline: Asking around about Chachi
beats.text: I send the same question to Rosetta, Mordecai, Tipid and Prepotente at once: who is this Chalchiuhtlicue, and why did my Scavenger's Daughter patch try to go off while I was talking to Lucia? Rosetta says she's a minor goddess of childbirth, water and fire, never sponsored, weak in the Ascendency game. Mordecai says what he always says, which is that nobody knows, this is all new. Donut says we're calling her Chachi. My question stands. If she can get from wherever those kids are to here, can we go the other way?
beats.gist: Carl asks Rosetta, Mordecai, Tipid and Prepotente who Chalchiuhtlicue is and why his Scavenger's Daughter patch activated.

beats.headline: Trust me on this one
beats.text: Donut wants the whole plan and I can't give it to her yet. The prize is two people of our choosing brought to the eleventh floor, and she's scared I mean to hurt somebody she likes. So I tell her what I can: I'm scared too, and the pig, this quest and the war mage plan will all help us survive. I'll explain once it's too late for them to take the prize away. Then Zhang says what he means to do, and I see it. Li Na can't worship a god. She's a weapon. She just needs pointing. I message Bodi.
beats.gist: Carl tells Donut the pig, the quest, and the war mage plan help them survive.

beats.headline: It's a go
beats.text: Splash Zone says the casino plan is a bust, so it's the cleaner bots. Li Na's poison won't clear, and it'll get worse, because health tops up on every new floor. If Herot's real and the war mages weren't lying about the Cabaret, getting her through stops that, keeps Zhang alive, stops her killing crawlers, and tests the route before we try it with a crowd. It only works if she agrees. She's too smart to trick, and I wouldn't want to. Everyone at the table is looking at me. "It's a go." Tran bows.
beats.gist: Splash Zone says the casino plan is a bust, so Carl chooses the cleaner bots.

beats.headline: Potions, a scroll, and A-ha
beats.text: I've never sung in my life, except hammered in a bar with a bunch of coasties, years ago. So Mordecai compounds potions to get round the cooldowns, and I'm Honeyed, Yo-Yo Ma'd and Dio'd. There's a scroll called Gelded Choirboy for the notes my voice can't reach. Mordecai insists the name isn't literal. I read it at the last second and sound like I've sucked on a helium balloon. The song is "Take on Me." I take the lead, so Donut's few lines have the better odds. Then the unicorn stabs the DJ.
beats.gist: Mordecai compounds potions and a scroll so Carl sings Take on Me before a unicorn stabs the DJ.

beats.headline: Singing through a bar fight
beats.text: The DJ's dead, so this is our only shot, and the music keeps going. I sing. Bottles break on me. I kick a gremlin and a Draconian off the stage before they reach Donut, catch her microphone stand between my big and index toe, and bounce off the stage when the curtains go up. I hit the high note and the gauge by my head throws sparks. Permanent access to the Stage Performance Guild, and an achievement, Sing for your supper. The sign over Donut says FAILED. I guess I gotta do this myself.
beats.gist: Carl sings while bottles break on him, kicks a gremlin and a Draconian, and catches a microphone stand.

beats.headline: A running list of gods
beats.text: Jurgen asks a better question than I'd managed: can people who worship gods not go to the Cabaret, or do the war mages just not want them there? Akuma lied to us about needing two teams dead, so he could be lying about this too. I've been keeping a running list of every god I hear of, sorted by affiliation and skill. Donar goes on it: thunder and lightning, like Thor but manlier, not sponsored this season, and he's given Jurgen lightning spells. My heart skips a beat. Then I'm through the door, and the guildmaster is stuck in his own zipper.
beats.gist: Carl keeps a list of gods sorted by affiliation and skill, including Donar.

beats.headline: He could have been kinder
beats.text: Dong's cursed. Mordecai says the sock has gone, and without it and every nickel the NPCs grabbed, a temple won't help. I gave him that sock. I got it from Quan Ch. The Dominators heard us outside their garage and drove for the starting line with Corky in the back, where we can't touch them. I sit on the curb. Dong's an NPC, and he's my friend, and I could've been a lot less of a jerk about it. So we stop waiting. We join the two halves during the race, and Grigori gets half an hour to learn to drive.
beats.gist: Carl gives Dong a sock from Quan Ch because a temple cannot help without it.

beats.headline: Holding on by his fingers
beats.text: I apologise to Bigs, and then to Dong, because they're right. This floor felt easy at first, on rails, no choices. It isn't. It's a drain for everyone spat out of the bottom of Faction Wars, spinning faster near the hole. I tell Dong he's coming: three mercenary seats, Grigori, Porky and him. But while I'm saying it I think of D'nadia, and of Finley, and the voices under the surface, and the tremor in my hands since Donut's attack in the tower. I'm not on the edge. I've already stepped off. You will not break me.
beats.gist: Carl apologizes to Bigs and Dong, tells Dong he has a mercenary seat, and resists breaking.

beats.headline: The rocket button
beats.text: I blow the tommy gun off our roof to clear the windshield, and Osvaldo complains the shrapnel hit them. Inside the factory the containment snaps on; five seconds' contact with anyone else and it merges. The Dominators take a conveyor belt loaded with metal balls toward the melting vats, so we follow. The edge isn't a ramp. It's a drop. I smack the untested rocket button, know within a second it's far too strong, tap it off and steer the Bubble Buddy through the air. We land, run off the side, and the bubble catches us.
