beats.gist: Carl blows a tommy gun off the roof and steers the Bubble Buddy through the air.

beats.headline: Upside down, at speed
beats.text: The next room is a river of molten metal three floors down, so we go sideways up the wall and then upside down onto the ceiling track. Behind me Grigori is vomiting, two half-mantaurs are unzipping, and Dong is wrapping their half brains in the kappa's plastic wrap. Slag elementals jump from the river and throw metal at us, and one blows a hole in the hood. I fold us between the legs of a ferret mount with the trans-dimensional upgrade and pop out ahead. When I look back there's one name over the mantaur. Then a god.
beats.gist: Carl goes sideways up a wall and upside down onto a ceiling track.

beats.headline: Fifteen seconds to spare
beats.text: Grull wants Corcunda, and Corcunda decides to go to him. Dong pulls out the lance I haven't seen since the day I gave him the sock, and they go out the back of the truck together, and the screws go with them, and the god says it was a good death and vanishes. We skitter through somebody's Hole and cross the line with fifteen seconds left. Fourth place. I can't look back at who didn't make it. We're alive. We won the quest. That was supposed to be the part that mattered most.
beats.gist: Corcunda goes to Grull, Dong uses a lance, and they exit a truck with screws.

beats.headline: What a hero
beats.text: Dong Quixote is dead. I let it sink in. What a way to go. Out of sixty teams in our race, eighteen came through, and there are about three hundred heats of four left. We're getting slaughtered. The quest pays out: two creatures of my choosing brought to the arena on the eleventh floor, the choice made once we're inside it. The AI's note carries a warning about exits that seem too good to be true. Then Mordecai says a single flower has bloomed on the cactus. Li Na made it.
beats.gist: Dong Quixote is dead and eighteen of sixty teams remain. Carl wins two creatures for the arena.

beats.headline: The plan, in the stables
beats.text: We meet in the pet stables, because Rosetta says a guild add-on room has a bug and the gods can't hear what's said in it. The numbers: two heats left, about two hundred people going to the Cabaret, and by Mordecai's math we need fifteen hundred more to take deals to keep the crawler-on-crawler races down. Only volunteers who've stayed human and don't worship a god can go. And me: Hellik has to be dead before the eleventh floor ends or Emberus smites me, so I'm leaving the party. Donut isn't speaking to me.
beats.gist: Carl meets Rosetta in the pet stables to plan because a bug hides their speech from gods.

beats.headline: Who killed Geyrun
beats.text: My quest is to find out who murdered Geyrun, Emberus's son. Samantha was there when someone was hired to do it, and her memory is spotty. One of the four sons of Sheol may be involved, and Amayon claims to know who did it. I'm building a family tree of gods in my scratch pad, and I miss Katia badly; she'd have had this worked out. I think it's the key to all of it. I think the AI wants it solved and doesn't know the answer either. I have a very loose theory. Not nearly enough.
beats.gist: Carl seeks the murderer of Geyrun, Emberus's son, while building a family tree of gods.

beats.headline: Is this truly the only way
beats.text: On the walk into Hungry Eyes Village, Donut asks me whether this is truly the only way. I think so. We're all dying, and every floor takes away a little more of our ability to fight back. The Emberus quest to kill Hellik is due. Mordecai says it could backfire the way it did for Drakea, when the Nagas cheated. It could. But the showrunners aren't in control anymore, and the AI, crazy as it is, still follows the rules. Eris wants devotion, not worship. That's a trap. She has the right idea, though.
beats.gist: Donut asks Carl if this is the only way while walking into Hungry Eyes Village.

beats.headline: Tempered in the fires of hell
beats.text: I raise my tea to all of them: the ones escaping, the ones taking a deal after the next heat, the ones staying for whatever comes after. We aren't perfect. This floor keeps making us turn on each other, and heat seven is three teams and one survivor. But these people are my family. Then Elle springs the trap on Linus, and I keep my hand on his neck. You keep trying to divide us, I tell him. We've been tempered in the fires of hell. You've already lost. All that's left is the wreckage settling.
beats.gist: Carl raises tea to those escaping or taking deals and tells Linus they are tempered in hell.

beats.headline: If he could slip in
beats.text: Everyone thought the Linus thing was a joke. It rattled me, because I was one of the last to notice anything fishy, and I pride myself on noticing. If he could slip in, who else is out there? The AI stopped Harbinger cold. Not every attempt will be so clumsy. And we still have our own strife: Osvaldo, and Agatha, who has simply disappeared. Our new mercenary is a Zebani cartographer, which reminds me of a dead crawler who accused me of killing her father. Just another mystery.
beats.gist: Carl worries about the Linus situation and the AI stopping Harbinger while Osvaldo and Agatha cause strife.

beats.headline: Crossed-out eyes
beats.text: Archie Mu's apartment: his wife, Mackenzie, screaming on a chair, their boy alive in the photographs. Her eyes are X'd out. His aren't. The boy's aren't. I think I've got it. Crossed-out eyes mean dead. Then we drive through and the loop breaks, and she starts pulling at her stitches. One floor down it's Imani's family, a man seizing on the carpet while everyone watches, and when her mother tears her eyes open, beetles pour out. The AI said it was done with this. I tell the ceiling exactly what I think of that.
beats.gist: Carl sees Mackenzie screaming on a chair with eyes X'd out and beetles pouring from eyes.

beats.headline: Forgive me, friends
beats.text: Jurgen needs help on the first floor, and Osvaldo says he's about to cross the line. That could put us last. So I open the Primed tab and find the detonator. Earlier, Samantha distracted the two bugbears while I used Oozy Form for the first time and swapped one of their peach beers for a can I'd drilled out and filled. It hides from anything under level twelve Find Traps. Forgive me, friends. I click it. They were NPCs. They were our friends. At least it's not another crawler.
beats.gist: Carl clicks a detonator to kill friends because Jurgen needs help and Osvaldo might cross the line.

beats.headline: Under a thousand left
beats.text: Imani's count: under a thousand of us. We started this floor at fifty-five hundred. A little over two hundred went to the Cabaret. Then a voice I've never heard, Damien, some behind-the-scenes lifer, tells us to take a deal, promises the garages and hired NPCs transfer down, and gives us ninety minutes on arrival to build a parade float. Donut gasps with delight. Imani, meanwhile, is running the entire upgrade-stealing operation. That assassin was right to target her. Look for the helpers.
beats.gist: Imani counts under a thousand crawlers left from an original fifty-five hundred.

beats.headline: The draw undoes everything
beats.text: For the first time we can see the other heats across the lobby. One is team Yokai against two NPC teams, all three NPCs, so they're allowing that now, and every calculation we made is worthless. Then the next two heats, side by side. A Cadillac, Imani and Elle's APV, and Chris's red semi. A gecko, an NPC sedan, and Florin's moped with Lucia on the back. Chris against Imani. Louis and Britney against Florin and Lucia. Everything we did to keep our circle alive, undone in one moment.
beats.gist: Carl sees other heats across the lobby and the draw undoes every calculation.

beats.headline: Red, and four legs
beats.text: Everyone in the truck gets a second wheel: mostly green, a sliver of red. Donut, green. Jamal, green. Samantha, who has no business being in the truck, green. Mine ticks past the green and stops on red. A level twenty Transformation spell. I black out for five seconds and wake up smaller, able to smell everything, including the frozen chicken patties, which smell delicious. Quadruped actions menu. Donut is suddenly huge and hissing at me. Samantha asks if she can pet me. I bark.
beats.gist: Carl receives a level twenty Transformation spell and becomes a small quadruped who smells frozen chicken patties.

beats.headline: Contingency three
beats.text: The messaging spells my name with a K now. A notice nearly slips past in the chaos: Pontiff has left the playing field and is no longer my mercenary. That's the idea. I know why this heat is four hours and why we can leave the blocks. Mordecai says the garden is intact. Contingency three, I tell everyone with more than one crawler team in their heat. It's a bad idea. I beg Osvaldo one last time, and he tells me to go fuck myself. Forgive me. The light goes green.
beats.gist: Carl tells crawler teams in his heat contingency three after the Pontiff stops being his mercenary.

beats.headline: Poleaxes, all the way up
beats.text: I designed them on the last floor and never got to use them: poleaxes. Focused charges that blast up and down in a cone but not sideways, vaporising a ten-meter circle below and a wider hole above instead of bringing the building down. I dropped several in a rough vertical line through the apartment building. When I hit the detonator they punch a jagged, almost straight shaft from the lobby to the roof. Being three times bigger this heat makes the holes three times bigger. A pleasant surprise.
beats.gist: Carl drops poleaxes in a vertical line through an apartment building and detonates a jagged shaft.

beats.headline: They laugh until they cry
beats.text: Mordecai's slugpox cure is still sitting on the crafting table, which I tell Imani with my tail down. About thirty of our people are waiting outside the Hairpin: Chris back in human form in his Meadow Lark overalls, Elle a goblin, Imani holding Jacobus the starfish. They see me, a dachshund, and every one of them, Prepotente and Lucia included, falls over laughing. Imani scratches my chin and cures me. Fine. Let's go rob a casino.
beats.gist: Carl tells Imani about Mordecai's slugpox cure while his tail is down.

beats.headline: The eye on the dog's forehead
beats.text: As a dachshund I can't punch, which I learn the hard way against a table. Worse: the Eye of the Bedlam Bride has moved from my chest to the middle of my dog forehead, and it's trying to wrench itself open. Let me take over, it says. No. You stay trapped. Then Mitch lunges at me, all mouth, and I open it on reflex. He freezes, glittering, screaming that it's too cold, and Donut finishes him. It's there when I need it. That's what worries me.
beats.gist: As a dachshund, Carl punches a table and the Eye of the Bedlam Bride moves to his forehead.

beats.headline: A promise at the hole in the floor
beats.text: I'm a dachshund, so I hold up a paw to look at the portal. It's the same as last time. Louis is going through it, and Samantha is crying, so I say it to him and to all of them: as long as I breathe, I will do everything I can to get you free, wherever you land. On the walk out Elle asks what the evil-eye business was. The Eye of the Bedlam Bride tattoo; I control it. She says I'm keeping secrets. She's right. One more floor, I tell her, and we'll talk.
beats.gist: Carl holds up a paw at the portal and promises to get everyone free.

beats.headline: Twenty-three
beats.text: Welcome to the eleventh floor. Twenty-three crawlers remaining. That number sobers me faster than Quasar did, and Quasar was shaking. The leaderboard is suspended, but my final ranking is two; Donut is three and wants to know who beat us both. I'm pretty sure I'm the last crawler left without a player-killer skull. I'm not a dog anymore, though I still want to lick myself, and the Eye of the Bedlam Bride is back where it belongs.
beats.gist: Carl is the second ranked crawler among twenty-three survivors and lacks a player-killer skull.

beats.headline: A patch, sewn crooked
beats.text: A patch, a gun, a sewing kit and a holster, laid out on the table, which is Mordecai. The patch is a foot crushing four-leaf clovers. Lucky Shot: a fatal blow gets deflected into a party member instead, once per floor. I sew it on above the Midnight Epicure. Donut says it isn't straight, and that I've started a new row without finishing the last one. It is straight. It comes off the second I've used it.
beats.gist: Carl sews a Lucky Shot patch of a foot crushing clovers above the Midnight Epicure.

beats.headline: He leaves the Royal Court
beats.text: An hour of flowers, and it's time. I click Yes. I have left the Royal Court of Princess Donut. I'm not in a party. My personal space is segregated, down to one room, a bathroom and my food boxes, and I accept the invitation from Safehome Yolanda. Most of my crafting tables, bomber's studio included, stay on Donut's side, which makes rejoining easier. Plus, if I die, she doesn't lose it all.
beats.gist: Carl leaves the Royal Court of Princess Donut and accepts an invitation from Safehome Yolanda.

beats.headline: He examines a Horrible
beats.text: I focus on a girl in the crowd. Maybe eight, long arms, bone-white skin, a green goblin mask. She scratches her leg with a black shoe. Her description isn't a stat block. It's the AI asking what her name was, whether she had a pet, who she would have become. Donut asks whether I understood any of it. I did, mostly, and a deep well of sadness comes with it. I think the AI is about to explain the rest.
beats.gist: Carl examines a girl with bone-white skin and a green goblin mask who scratches her leg.

beats.headline: Vengeance, not revenge
beats.text: Our turn at the stand. Donut asked me the difference, so I tell everyone. Revenge is direct. Vengeance is punishment, righteous and not always direct. The triangle falls away and there's the Unwashed, the Nothing's own face, an upside-down tree made of dahlias. Passing Grigori, I heal Chaco with a scroll and hold the AI's eyes while I do it. Then I point at the effigy and tell the galaxy it is coming for all of them. It may not be me. But we are coming.
beats.gist: Carl tells the galaxy vengeance is righteous punishment and warns them he is coming.

beats.headline: This is our revolution
beats.text: The missile launcher we looted from Dwight is bolted to the chicken truck under the Unwashed. The sluggalos have the wheel and the deep fryer on, which was not the plan. I have the microphone and my face on a jumbotron. We are done playing and dying on your terms. This is our revolution. The door opens on thousands of monsters and the masked stand-ins they're tearing apart. Then my first choice, and the galaxy hears it: Scolopendra.
beats.gist: Carl bolts a looted missile launcher to the chicken truck and chooses Scolopendra on a jumbotron.

beats.headline: A gun to the pig's head
beats.text: Penny's a crawler now. Level ten Yorkshire pig, no class, typing in capitals because the biscuit made her sapient without giving her a voice. She wants a chicken sandwich. I strap her to my chest in the harness Mordecai modified, pour splooge down her, drink some myself, and put my father's gun to her head. I've blown up settlements. I killed Jasha and Radoslav. This still feels like a line I didn't know was there. Then I yell for Taranis.
beats.gist: Carl straps Penny, a level ten Yorkshire pig, to his chest and puts his father's gun to her.

beats.headline: Inside Scolopendra
beats.text: Gloom Wraith Phase puts Penny and me through the centipede's wall. No air. Splooge doesn't help her breathe, and I can't risk her potion cooldown, so I pierce her nipple with Petey Motteux's Little Secret, a ring from Tiatha's pile that grants Oxygenated. Mordecai then tells me splooge counts as food, no cooldown. Now you tell me. Oozy Form gets us into Club Scolopendra. The Sin of Consumption wheel lands green for both of us. The alien in the web lands red.
beats.gist: Gloom Wraith Phase puts Carl and Penny through a centipede wall; Carl pierces Penny's nipple.

beats.headline: Lucky Shot, spent
beats.text: Emberus throws something at my chest that should kill me outright. The Four-Leaf Clover patch deflects it into my party member, Penny, out at Taranis's feet. Donut jumps us outside, into a demolition derby. Emberus climbs out of the bug at full size, screaming my name, and Taranis, who saw who hurt his pig, twists his wrist. I hold on to Donut. When the blast clears, most of the arena is dead or dying. I get on the motorcycle anyway.
beats.gist: Emberus throws a lethal object at Carl, which a Four-Leaf Clover patch deflects into Penny.

beats.headline: What the actual fuck, Carl
beats.text: I put the bike down, launch us into the air, and throw the ball down Scolopendra's open mouth. The biggest thing in the dungeon splatters into a puddle the size of a small elephant. The achievement is the AI saying what the actual fuck, Carl, one word at a time, and admitting it's got nothing for a reward. Then Eris, huge, tells me I'm chaos incarnate and she doesn't need my worship. Every exit is an entrance. Don't forget the coin.
beats.gist: Carl launches into the air and throws a ball down Scolopendra's open mouth.

beats.headline: Mark of the Damned, and a dart
beats.text: Nineteen crawlers. Twenty if you count Penny, which I don't. The sun tattoos on the backs of my hands are raised scars now: Mark of the Damned, no explanation. There's a dart in my leg I never felt. Tracking Tag. The Kyryap has claimed you. I send party requests until every one of us is in a single party. We do this together. I have to stay on the twelfth and stop anyone winning the Ascendency until everybody left is out.
beats.gist: Carl has a Tracking Tag dart in his leg and raised sun scars on his hands.

relations.note: Stuck with each other from the first night.
Marked him for death over a defiled shrine
The church's loan, and the disguised ring
Named him friend of the church
